#1753. Rabiot and Ruben’s rampant Rossoneri: All the key stats from AC Milan 5-1 Frosinone

AC Milan produced their best attacking display of the season on Sunday night as they put five goals past Frosinone at San Siro.

An own-goal from Gabriele Calvani early on set the tone, with Goncalo Ramos, Ardon Jashari, Alphadjo Cisse and Christian Pulisic all netting in the rout. The ruthless counter-attacking display moves Milan back inside the top four, after wins from Como, Roma and Lazio earlier in the round.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

The match stats make for interesting reading. Milan edged possession with 54%, generating 2.50 Expected Goals – so scoring double what they created – but also having five big chances which matches the number of goals scored.

Frosinone remarkably had more shots in total (15 to 12), but they were more wasteful with only three on target to the Rossoneri’s eight. The visitors also racked up nine corners, the most Milan have conceded all season.

📊 The stats from the win against Frosinone. pic.twitter.com/ERVTj98m9Y

— MilanData📊 (@acmilandata) November 22, 2026

Only Nereo Rocco’s (29) and Lajos Czeizler’s (31) Milan sides scored more goals than Ruben Amorim’s (28) in their first 12 matches in charge in Serie A.

Adrien Rabiot is the first Milan midfielder to be involved in at least one goal (including goals and assists) in seven consecutive Serie A appearances since Kaká in 2004, and he became the first midfielder in the last 20 years of Serie A with more than 10 goals in his first 10 games in a single season.

With his sixth goal in his 10th Serie A appearance for Milan at 20 years and 31 days, Alphadjo Cisse became the second-youngest Rossoneri player to reach this milestone in his first 10 appearances in the three-points-for-a-win era, after Alexandre Pato , who achieved it at 18 years and 189 days.

No team has scored more goals than Milan in the first 15 minutes of play in the five major European leagues currently underway (7, like Barcelona and Chelsea).

Milan are now unbeaten in all seven meetings against Frosinone in Serie A (W5 D2): among the teams against which they have never lost in the competition, the Rossoneri have played more games only against Pisa (14 – six also against Crotone and Lecco).

Milan have won five of their last six league games (L1), scoring at least two goals in each, after failing to win three of their previous four (D3). The last time they scored more than one goal in a run of Serie A matches was between September 2020 and January 2021, when they managed 15 games.

#1752. Man Utd told they made ‘criminal’ mistake not signing Premier League winner

Ex-England striker Carlton Cole has slammed Manchester United’s recruitment under INEOS and claims it was ‘criminal’ the club didn’t explore a move for Danny Welbeck in the summer.

There had been a sense of optimism amongst United’s fanbase heading into the season after Michael Carrick picked up the pieces from Ruben Amorim’s turbulent reign to lead the club to a third-place finish last term.

But the Red Devils once again find themselves in a state of disarray after a wretched start to the 2026/27 campaign, which ultimately cost Carrick his job earlier this month.

With genuine fears growing that United could become embroiled in a relegation scrap, Mauricio Pochettino has been tasked with steadying the ship and steering a dispirited squad away from the bottom of the Premier League table.

The Argentine’s tenure got off to a nightmare start at the weekend, though, as his side were put to the sword at the hands of arch-rivals Liverpool in a thumping 4-0 defeat at Anfield.

Read exclusive analysis of the biggest stories in football with Metro's weekly football newsletter In The Mixer. Sign up now for free.

Sunday’s result ensured United remain firmly in the drop zone after 11 matches, only one point better off than rock-bottom Crystal Palace with the worst defensive record of any team in Europe’s top five leagues.

If Pochettino was expecting to be supported with significant financial backing in his efforts to turn United’s fortunes around this winter, he will likely be disappointed.

After all, Reports this week suggest the 54-year-old will have a budget of ‘well under £50million’ to work with when the January transfer window opens for business.

Asked what Pochettino must address with his meagre funds while tackling United’s woes on The Dressing Room Podcast, Cole replied: ‘The spine. They haven’t got a striker, a worthy striker.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

‘Midfield, I think they’re alright there for now because they’ve got Carlos Baleba and I think he’s a fantastic player by the way, they’ve got Kobbie Mainoo, Bruno Fernandes… I think they’re alright in that position.

‘I know the boy from Chelsea, Andrey Santos, he’s there, but I know he’s not tuned in yet because it’s high pressure right now and he’s a little bit off it. They’ve got Youri Tielemans as well. Then you’ve got the centre-backs…’

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

According to Cole, United missed a trick when they gave Chelsea a free run at signing Welbeck from Brighton in the summer.

‘I think it’s criminal they didn’t sign Welbeck,’ he added.

‘I think he’s wasted at Chelsea at the moment, they should have signed Welbeck. He’d have done alright!’

Eyebrows were raised when Pochettino named his team to face Liverpool on Sunday, with Matthijs de Ligt thrown in for his first Premier League start of the campaign.

There were signs of rustiness in De Ligt’s game from minute one and it was the Dutchman’s calamitous defending that led to Dominik Szoboszlai’s breakthrough – and Leny Yoro’s sending off – after only ten minutes.

‘I thought that was him [Pochettino] protesting already,’ Cole said of De Ligt’s surprise selection.

‘I think it was on the first or second day that he was in, he was already saying he wanted more control in the transfer market. I thought you negotiated that in your deal!

‘He’s chosen the right time to do it [make a protest], in a game like that.

‘This was a free hit for him and yes, he needs defenders. But I’ve said it before, INEOS have gone with signing forward first and then the next window they get a midfielder… who does that? So that’s what has happened.’

Cole went a step further on Pochettino’s decision to field De Ligt, adding: ‘I think it’s bang out of order, he’s been stitched up.

‘He’s obviously not fit, he can’t read it. When you’ve been out so long, you get your bearings wrong, you don’t know where you are on the pitch. It happens, right? So I give him grace for that.

‘The problem is that Yoro is not experienced. So if you’re going to bring in De Ligt, you’ve got to bring another experienced defender in with him.

‘If De Ligt is going to be there and Harry Maguire is there then it’s alright and if Maguire makes that mistake that Yoro made, I get it.

‘But Yoro is still young, he’s still learning the game. They’re both, to some extent, inexperienced at this moment in time so it’s the blind leading the blind.’

United will look to stop the rot when they switch their focus to Champions League matters away to Sporting on Wednesday evening.

Three days later, Pochettino’s men return to Premier League action at home to Brentford.

#1751. Serie A sensation Gustavo Varela responds to Arsenal transfer links

Monza star Gustavo Varela has distanced himself from speculation that he could be set for a January transfer move and insists he is ‘paying no attention’ to incessant rumours linking him with Arsenal, Barcelona and Napoli.

Varela, 21, was deemed surplus to requirements at Benfica and completed a switch to newly promoted Italian outfit Monza for a fee of just €2million (£1.7m) – plus performance-related bonuses – in the summer.

It has proven a tough start to the season for Monza on their return to Serie A, with the club picking up just three wins and languishing down in 14th place in the table.

Varela has proven a shining light up front, though, scoring 11 goals in his opening 11 top-flight appearances, and the striker’s barnstorming form in Lombardy has begun to attract the attentions of European football’s elite.

According to recent reports emanating out of Varela’s native Portugal, Barca, Napoli and Arsenal are all actively pursuing a deal for the forward on the back of his goalscoring exploits in the first three months of the campaign.

Read exclusive analysis of the biggest stories in football with Metro's weekly football newsletter In The Mixer. Sign up now for free.

Premier League champions Arsenal are said to be among a host of Premier League clubs that have ‘expressed an interest’ in Varela and were ‘one of the first to enquire’ about the player’s potential availability.

It’s understood the Gunners are in the market for an attacker of Varela’s profile, with Viktor Gyokeres struggling to live up to expectations following his £64m arrival from Sporting last year.

On Monday night, Varela ensured he remained in the headlines with a terrific brace in Monza’s 3-0 victory over Fiorentina – in doing so, becoming only the third player in the last 50 years to reach the double figures in their first 11 Serie A games.

‘I can’t believe what I’m doing. I go home, close my eyes and I can’t believe it. Football is made of moments,’ Varela told DAZN Italy following Monza’s win.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

On his brilliant flicked effort to complete his double, Varela added: ‘It was pure instinct, it’s not something I practice.

‘A very beautiful cross came in, I was close to the goal and I decided to try my luck. If you don’t try, you can’t do it, and it happened.’

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

Varela was then asked for his reaction the rumoured interest he was receiving from some of Europe’s most high-profile teams, to which he responded: ‘I continue to thank Monza for allowing me to be here. It has all been incredible.

‘I feel lucky to be part of this reality and I only hope to continue on this path.

‘I pay no attention to the news. I only focus on what I have to do on the field. It’s normal, it’s part of football.

‘I’m going through a great moment but a less good moment may arise tomorrow.

Trust us, you're going to want to watch this OUTRAGEOUS finish from Gustavo Varela 😮‍💨🔥#MonzaFiorentina #UNROSSOALLAVIOLENZA pic.twitter.com/Z2RvJFul6X

‘That’s why I try to simply enjoy the present without paying attention to the news.

‘Sometimes they speak well of me and sometimes they speak badly, but this is the world of football and I only think about what I have to do on the field.’

Monza are believed to have slapped an asking price on Varela in the region of €40-50m (£33-42m).

Though they did not insert a buy-back clause in their deal with Monza for Varela, Benfica will be entitled to 20 per cent of any future transfer fee for the sought-after youngster.

The Primeira Liga club also have the right of first refusal should a bidding war break out for the Portugal Under-21 international, who was named the Serie A Rising Star of the Month for October.

Varela’s current contract with Monza runs through to June 2030.

#1750. Bradford City 3 Barnsley FC 0: Rinse and repeat for rock-bottom Reds as visiting fans vent their ire at end

It is one etched into Barnsley folklore. Bradford City were famously the opposition as the Reds provided one of those wonderful, soul-enhancing moments that lights up football from time to time as they reached the top-flight for the first occasion in their history.

At the minute, Barnsley supporters have only memories to cling onto. It’s pretty grim in the present - with just over a month to go, 2026 has already marked itself out as one of the most inauspicious in the Reds’ modern-day history.

Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

How they needed something on a cold, dank West Yorkshire night. Ten without a league win in an appalling autumn, two points from a possible 30, propping up the table and with growing fears that they could drop into the fourth tier for the first time since 1978-79 if the narrative doesn’t change.r

City, for their part, were in no mood to be charitable and sympathetic after tough derby moments against Doncaster Rovers and Huddersfield Town in their previous two league matches, both at Valley Parade.

Despite missing chances to make the night more straightforward after an early opener, they eventually found a way midway through the second half.

To rub salt into Reds’ wounds, it was former Oakwlel striker Stephen Humphrys who did the damage with his second of the night as he scored for the third successive game as City ended the glut of home games in the right fashion from their perspective.

A third in stoppage time from the spot, from Jake Beesley, was the prelude to chants of ‘You’re not fit to wear the shirt’ from disgruntled Reds followers.

The pre-match portents weren’t great for the Reds. Reyes Cleary, who scored one of the EFL’s goals of the season from some 70 yards here last autumn, was absent through illness.

Cam McGeehan did at least return from suspension - as did ex-City loanee Jack Shepherd - while there was a rare start for Tyrese Noslin.

The hosts made four changes, including a first in their three-man backline since September 1.

Macaulay Gillesphey got the nod, on his 31st birthday, with ex-Reds duo Adam Phillips and Humphrys also starting alongside Will Swan - the front three who finished the weekend derby against Doncaster Rovers.

Beesley was back on the bench for the hosts after recovering from a knock.

It was a bit of a Groundhog Day half from Barnsley, truth be told.

Again, they showed evidence that between both boxes, there are certainly far worse teams at this level. In their defensive duties, there are surely no-one worse and as Daniel Stendel said beforehand, getting it right in both boxes wins and loses football matches.

City led 1-0 at the interval and given events on Saturday, when they failed to get a two-goal cushion against another struggling White Rose visitor, there should have been understandable disappointment.

Humphrys ‘old-manned’ Barnsley’s meek and ineffectual backline and was too much for them in the first half. He could easily have laid claim to the matchball.

His opener was helped by some pitiful defending.

Direct from a goalkick, Jon McCracken showed quick thinking like on Saturday. Humphrys brushed aside the meek Sam Gale far too easily and the covering from Arley Kay was similarly powder-puff and he easily converted as the Reds conceded early for the second successive derby.

Gale and Kay would later switch positions as Barnsley morphed into a back three.

Bradford were only too happy to stick it on Barnsley’s flaky defence and go direct and there were gaping holes to exploit on occasions.

Humphrys soon played in Kayden Jackson, in oceans of space, but Cieran Slicker saved at his near post.

Humphrys also found a hole to exploit in the box and headed over from Ibou Touray’s cross, while Swan also fired a good chance wide after being sent clear by Callum Connolly’s pass. Later on in the half, Phillips headed a decent opportunity off target.

At the other end, Barnsley’s best chance came in the first few minutes when Patrick Kelly cashed in on Matt Pennington’s loose clearance, but McCracken parried his well-struck half-volley - straight at him instead of a yard either side.

McGeehan also blasted a presentable chance over. In both boxes, it was as you were for the ailing Reds.

On the restart, Barnsley were afforded a sniff with his crisp low shot from Ryan Brownlie’s low shot flashing just wide following Ziyad Larkeche’s cross before a skewed high clearance from Connolly had to be tipped over in the nick of time by McCracken.

Despite their side’s form, the backing from the stoic band of visiting supporters was impressive.

Those in visiting jerseys, for all their deficiencies in defence, had a good dig at the start of the second period.

City gradually awoke and Connolly fired a loose ball wide following consternation in the Reds box. At the other end, Kelly lashed a shot into the empty Bradford end before Connell fired straight at McCracken.

Substitute Makenzie Kirk was then off beam, with home punters starting to get a touch agitated at the lack of a second goal at the other end.

They were soon appeased when astute hold-up play from Powell teed up Humphrys, who rammed home a second.

McCracken then grasped a free-kick from Connell, one of the few visiting players who managed to convince.

Winter is nigh and it looks like being a long and hard one for Barnsley unless they get January right.

Beesley added a third in stoppage time from the spot.

Bradford City: McCracken; Pennington, Baldwin, Gillesphey (Pratt 82); Jackson, Connolly, Morgan, Touray; Phillips (Neufville 57), Swan (Powell 57); Humphrys (Beesley 74). Substitutes unused: Hadi, Matthews, O’Keeffe.

Barnsley: McCracken; Kay, Gale, Shepherd, Larkeche (Johnson 78); Connell, McGeehan; Noslin (Reid 84), Kelly, Brownlie (Kirk 63); Yoganathan. Substitutes unused: Ravenhill, O’Riordan, Okedina, Alker.

#1749. Union SG vs Lech Poznan - prediction, team news, lineups

By Saikat Mandal | 24 Nov 2026 19:25, Last updated: 25 Nov 2026 06:17

Union SG will be looking to maintain their impressive Europa League form when they host Lech Poznan at King Power at Den Dreef Stadium on Thursday.

The Old Lady remain unbeaten in the competition and sit fourth in the standings, while the visitors are languishing second from bottom in the table.

The Belgian side began their Europa League campaign with a convincing 3-0 victory over Viktoria Plzen away from home and have since collected 10 points from four matches, scoring 10 goals in the process.

The only occasion on which they dropped points came against Real Sociedad, when David Hubert's side fought back from behind to secure a 1-1 draw.

A scintillating second-half display helped them to a commanding 4-0 victory over Hapoel Be'er Sheva, while Union followed that up with a 2-1 triumph over Celta Vigo on matchday four.

They are unbeaten in their last 16 matches and head into this encounter on the back of seven consecutive victories across all competitions, a run that should give them plenty of confidence.

USG are also setting the pace in the Pro League, sitting top of the table with 32 points from 12 matches, having recorded 10 wins and two draws without tasting defeat.

Lech Poznan comfortably dispatched Swiss side Thun 9-2 on aggregate to secure their place in the Europa League league phase, but they have since struggled to find their feet in the competition.

The Railwaymen began their campaign with a 4-0 defeat to Crystal Palace before suffering another heavy loss by the same scoreline against Bayer Leverkusen.

The Polish side ground out a hard-fought 1-1 draw against Sunderland, but Benfica proved too strong in their next outing, handing them a 3-1 defeat on matchday four.

Having scored just two goals and conceded 12, they are among the three teams languishing near the bottom of the table with only one point, with only FC Ararat-Armenia faring worse.

Lech Poznan, however, have been outstanding domestically, sitting top of the league with 35 points from 14 matches, four clear of Gornik despite having played a game fewer.

Union SG are currently without Mateo Biondic, who is struggling with a knee injury, while Kevin Mac Allister has been ruled out for the remainder of the season with an ACL injury.

Hubert could make several changes to the side that faced Kortrijk in their last league outing, with Nikki Havenaar potentially coming into a three-man defence and Louis Patris moving into midfield.

Besfort Zeneli, who scored twice against Celta Vigo, is likely to return to the starting lineup in place of Darius Olaru, while Kevin Rodríguez is expected to lead the line.

Lech Poznan, meanwhile, are likely to adopt a more cautious approach away from home, with Niels Frederiksen potentially setting his side up in a 4-2-3-1 formation, with Yannick Agnero operating as the lone striker.

Mateusz Pruchniewski has been ruled out for the rest of the season with an ACL injury, while Ali Gholizadeh is still recovering from the same problem and is unlikely to return before January.

Alex Douglas is sidelined with a broken rib, while Joao Moutinho is not expected to return before February. However, Pablo Rodriguez and Mikael Ishak have both returned to training.

Koffi; Chibani, Sykes, Havenaar; Patris, Van de Perre, Zorgane, Smith; Mofokeng, Zeneli; Rodriguez

Lis; Gurgul, Yegbe, Skrzypczak, Pereira; Kozubal, Murawski; Sayyadmanesh, Berggren, Bengtsson; Agnero

Union SG are flying high at the moment and have plenty of momentum on their side, having remained unbeaten in their last 16 matches across all competitions.

Lech Poznan are still searching for their first Europa League victory this season, and although they may have to wait a little longer to break that duck, we expect the visitors to find the net and put up a strong fight.

#1747. Sheffield United 1 Southampton 1: Michael Cooper's late save ensures Sydie Peck's heroics do not go to waste

Just as Peretz's brilliant save from Tahith Chong was undone by Sydie Peck beating him in the 90th minute, so it looked like the midfielder's 90th-minute goal and Jordan Ayew's brilliance to create it might have been in vain when Finn Azaz played Samuel Edozie through in stoppage time.

But Cooper came out on top in the one-on-one to earn his side a 1-1 draw against opponents who completely outplayed the Blades in the first half-hour.

Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

If only they had played the first half as they had the second, perhaps they might have been celebrating victory rather than a point which felt like one, thanks to the timing of Peck's goal.

If the first half showed how short the Blades are of the very best in the division, the second showed what they have in their locker to try to do something about it.

Southampton will have walked off more relieved to take the point than the home team.

The Saints took the lead in the 11th minute when Hamza Choudhury gave the ball away and was unable to close Lewis Dobbin down before he curled a beautiful shot inside the far post.

Already by then it was on the cards, with Saints dominating possession as James Ward-Prowse pulled the strings in midfield.

The only saving grace is that the Blades only trailed 1-0 at the break.

Mads Roerslev had a shot blocked and Kuryu Matsuki thrashed an effort into the side netting from a tight angle.

The Blades did at least improve as half-time approached, Mark McGuinness heading a Peck corner, and Romelle Donovan - switched to the right - came inside and shot at the goalkeeper.

With Patrick Bamford introduced at the break, the Blades were much sharper in the second half.

Peck's shot from distance in the 50th minute showed ambition, if not accuracy.

A couple of minutes later, Bamford headed over at a corner nodded to him by Mark McGuinness. Next was Ayew, who headed at Daniel Peterz after Donovan got to the byline to tee the chance up.

Ayew was released down the left but delayed too long, and could only force a corner from a tight angle.

Donovan had a penalty appeal waved away, perhaps not helped by the fact he was clearly looking for it.

But the football was as one-way as the first half had been, only with more chances to show from it.

Chong was unable to keep his shot down when the ball dropped to him 16 yards out, and Harrison Burrows had an effort blocked.

Southampton briefly provided some variety in the 80th minute when Donovan blocked Cyle Larin and Ward-Prowse ballooned the follow-up over, but the play quickly moved back to the Kop End.

Chong's cross went all the way through to Burrows at the back post, but he could only loop his header up for Peretz to catch.

But the gilt-edged chance fell to Chong in the 83rd after a lovely move through Ayes and Bamford. The winger steered his shot into the right place, but Peretz stretched out brilliantly to his right to save it.

When that was squandered, it felt like the Blades might run out of time.

But in the 90th minute Ayew did brilliantly to dribble along the byline and pull the ball back for Peck to find the net through a busy penalty area.

It could have counted for nought had Cooper not intervened in the 95th minute.

#1743. Braga vs KuPS - prediction, team news, lineups

By Adeyeye Oluwapelumi | 24 Nov 2026 19:40

Braga will look to strengthen their position in the Conference League knockout-stage race when they welcome KuPS Kuopio to the Estadio Municipal de Braga on Thursday evening.

Franclim Carvalho's side are 17th in the 36-team standings with four points from three matches, while the Finnish visitors sit 33rd with just one point after failing to win any of their opening three European outings.

Despite going unbeaten in their six matches across three Conference League qualifying rounds (W4, D2) and keeping clean sheets in all of them, Braga have found life in the league phase considerably more challenging.

The Archbishops began their campaign with a disappointing 3-0 defeat away to Copenhagen before responding with a 2-0 home victory over Gent on matchday two, giving Carvalho his first win since replacing the sacked Carlos Vicens in October.

However, Braga were unable to build on that success in their latest continental outing, playing out a goalless draw away to Aarhus, although the new manager can take encouragement from the defensive improvements made in recent times.

The Portuguese outfit are unbeaten in their last four matches across all competitions, keeping clean sheets in each and winning three, with their latest success coming in a 2-0 victory away to Vitoria de Guimaraes in the Taca de Portugal at the weekend.

That result followed a 1-0 league win at Rio Ave, leaving Braga eighth in the Primeira Liga table with 17 points from their opening 11 fixtures and three points adrift of the top five.

The Archbishops are also three points away from fifth place in the Conference League standings, with several teams between 10th and 14th sitting just two points ahead, meaning maximum points on Thursday could strengthen their hopes of securing a top-eight finish.

Braga have plenty of reason to feel confident ahead of the contest, having won 14 of their last 16 home matches in European competition (D1, L1) and kept 12 clean sheets during that run.

KuPS, meanwhile, have struggled to make an impression in their second consecutive Conference League league-phase campaign, losing 4-2 to Trabzonspor in their opening fixture before suffering a 2-0 defeat away to Borac Banja Luka on matchday two.

The Finnish side collected their first point with a goalless draw against Gent on matchday three, but that result did little to disguise their attacking struggles, having scored just twice and conceded six goals across their opening three matches in the competition.

Miika Nuutinen's men have also gone seven matches without a victory, including a 1-1 draw against Swedish side Norrkoping in a friendly on November 19, while their most recent competitive outing was a 2-0 home defeat to Inter Turku in their final match of the 2026 top-flight campaign.

That result left the Yellow-Blacks third in the Veikkausliiga table, meaning they missed out on retaining the domestic title they won last season but secured a place in the first qualifying round of the Conference League.

KuPS have also struggled on their travels, recording just one victory in their last eight competitive away matches and failing to win any of their most recent four, three of which ended in defeat.

Braga will be without Sikou Niakate, who is recovering from a ruptured Achilles tendon that has kept him sidelined since April.

Jonas Wind is also doubtful after missing the recent victory over Vitoria because of physical overload, while Gabriel Silva returned as a second-half substitute at the weekend after missing the previous four matches through fitness problems and could feature again as he builds up his match fitness.

Fran Navarro ended a more than three-month wait for a goal by scoring against Vitoria and is expected to retain his place at the head of the attack, with club captain Ricardo Horta and Pau Victor also likely to feature in Carvalho's forward line.

KuPS could be without 22-year-old Ghanaian winger Bob Nii Armah, who picked up an injury during the goalless draw with Gent.

Thirty-three-year-old attacker Piotr Parzyszek has started all three of the Finnish side's league-phase matches and could retain his place despite failing to score in his last 10 competitive appearances for the club.

KuPS have managed just two goals in three Conference League matches and enter this encounter without a win in six outings, while Braga have won three of their last four matches and kept clean sheets in all of them, making a home victory the most likely outcome.

#1742. MOTHERWELL 1 RANGERS 2: Naderi rides to the rescue as wasteful Ibrox men get out of jail with late winner

Published: 18:01 EST, 21 November 2026 | Updated: 18:10 EST, 21 November 2026

FOR a team that just couldn’t find a way to get the ball into the net, no matter how they tried, it was always going to take a couple of jammy deflections or something out of the ordinary to get out of jail.

And that’s exactly how it panned out with just two minutes left on the clock. Rangers, tied at 1-1 and in danger of falling six points behind arch-rivals Celtic at the head of the Premiership, were throwing everything bar the kitchen sink at their hosts.

Balls were being blazed high and wide of the target. Chances were being passed up left, right and centre. It looked like Derek McInnes’ men were destined to rack up a third straight away draw in the league and take the club’s record to three years without a win at Fir Park when, in the 85th minute, substitute Findlay Curtis saw an effort parried by Alex Paulsen, Dujon Sterling blasted the rebound towards goal and Motherwell’s No 1 somehow flung an arm in the air and diverted it onto the crossbar.

It looked like the last throw of the dice. Until Ryan Naderi, who had suffered a miserable evening up to that point, made the difference.

A speculative shot from Badredine Bouanani from the edge of the area whacked off the outstretched boot of Martin Moormann and fell into the Czech internationalist’s path on the right.

His jabbed effort towards goal was nothing to write home about, but it carried just enough juice on it to whack off the hapless Moormann again, change direction and fly into the net.

Messy? Yes. Did Naderi care, though? Not a bit. He ran straight into the Rangers crowd behind the goal and lost himself in the relief and jubilation of a victory rescued from the fire.

That’s all that matters right now. Rangers won to keep up the pressure at the head of the table.

Naderi celebrates his late winner that snatched all three points for Rangers

McInnes applauds the travelling supporters after his side kept pace with Celtic at the top

However, there is a recurring problem with this squad. This game should have been out of sight, but missing chances and lacking that killer instinct manager McInnes demands remains a serious problem.

Just look at the stats. Rangers had 29 shots on goal in this affair and 11 on target. It should have been a procession, really. In the end, they only got through by the skin of their teeth.

There are times when these players look like they couldn’t hit a cow on the backside with a banjo and that is going to trip them up big-time in this title race unless they sort it out tout-suite.

They started like a runaway train in this game and got off to the perfect start with Manny Fernandez heading home from a corner within the first 10 minutes.

The problems started when Naderi, just nowhere as convincing in the role of main striker as he is when played with the likes of Kevin Kelsy, benched last night before a late cameo, up beside him, started missing sitters.

Jake Girdwood-Reich then levelled for Motherwell with pretty much their first forage upfield and it all got way more uncomfortable than it should have been. It is something McInnes is going to have to sort out.

The match started exactly the way McInnes would have wanted following the return from the international break with Rangers in the ascendancy from the first whistle and a goal to the good after eight minutes.

It was also as straightforward and as simple a goal as you could wish to see. One from a set-piece which Motherwell really ought to look back upon with some serious self-reflection. It was just too easy.

Djeidi Gassama had won a corner on the left thanks to a cross being deflected wide by Tom Sparrow. Kim Minsu fired in the flag-kick and Fernandez rose unchallenged to nod the ball home from close range. Like taking candy off a baby.

Fernandez gets his head to Minsu's corner to put Rangers in front early on at Fir Park

Fernandez milked the celebrations in front of the home fans after netting his first goal of the season, but Minsu’s reaction was tinged with the same senses of jubilation and relief.

The South Korean had been getting himself in a twist over failing to deliver an assist so far in his Rangers career. Now he’s off the mark on that front, it’s time for him to satisfy the demands from McInnes for a goal as well.

Shortly after the opener, Naderi, leading the line in front of Minsu, with Kelsy having been left on the bench, should have made it two.

An initial chance fell to the Czech internationalist after a Gassama shot had broken to him in the area. Moormann, however, put in a fine tackle to deflect the ball wide for a corner-kick.

Minsu took charge of that situation and fed it to Gassama, whose shot from a central position was parried by Paulsen.

It fell perfectly for Naderi and he should have buried a close-range header that ended up being cleared by Moormann again.

Fail to take your chances when on top and the prospect of getting yourself into bother is always there — and that’s what happened to Rangers on 21 minutes.

Motherwell had barely been up the park. Barely been in the game. However, they won a corner on the right thanks to some decent forward play from Regan Charles-Cook, on for the injured Ibrahim Said, and made the very most of the set-piece.

Emmanuel Longelo played a short corner to Sparrow who fired a low ball into the area at pace.

Girdwood-Reich timed his diagonal run nicely to move into space in front of a static Olwethu Makhanya and his first-time effort with the right foot beat visiting goalkeeper Ivor Pandur to his right to settle in the bottom corner.

Girdwood-Reich turns home Sparrow's cross to equalise for the home side

Nico Raskin had a shot touched over by Paulsen just before the half-hour and, moments later, it took a good saving tackle from Fernandez at the other end to deny Seb Palmer-Houlden a shot at goal after he had surged into the area.

With Motherwell getting their tails up before the interval, a ragged-looking Rangers really needed something to get a grip back on the game. It came just before the break with a one-on-one chance squandered by Naderi.

He had done well to get himself into a position where he could see the whites of Paulsen’s eyes, but the home keeper came out on top in the end by getting down low and touching the striker’s angled shot wide for a corner.

After Dan Neil had sent a low sidefooted effort just wide from the edge of the area and Palmer-Houlden had forced a save from Pandur with an unconvincing effort, Rangers passed up a super opportunity a little before the hour mark.

Naderi did well to set up Minsu in an unmarked position on the left side of the area. That elusive first goal in Rangers colours — or, rather, the foul red-and-black mish-mash that is their ‘third kit’ — beckoned.

Unfortunately, Minsu’s effort was awful. A straight-up sclaff that indicated a player just trying too hard or actually beginning to let a lack of confidence or a touch of anxiety interfere with his technique.

Whatever the reality, his poorly hit shot was saved at the near post by Paulsen.

Rangers did come close when a Tuur Rommens cross was deflected by Sparrow onto his own near post and Gassama then blazed a terrible effort over from a promising position.

When Paulsen made that double save, it looked like Motherwell had done enough to get a valuable point until Naderi got the visitors over the line by hook or by crook near the death.

It shouldn’t take this much effort and pain for Rangers to win a game of football, though. They need to show they can be cold-eyed killers if they want to win this title.

Leading thanks to Stephen Humphrys’ early goal, City failed to add to their tally by the interval against a rock-bottom Reds side who were very unconvincing at the back, especially in the first half.

Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

But a second goal midway through the second half from ex-Barnsley forward Humphrys settled the contest. Substitute Jake Beesley added a stoppage-time penalty.

Duff said: “I was disappointed at half-time because I thought we should have been put the game to bed.

"I didn't think we started the game particularly well, but Humps showed a little bit of quality that he’s got.

"We lost too many duels in the first half. We just felt that once we won a duel and made a couple of passes, we got in.

"If I was playing centre-half in the team, I’d have picked one of the forwards up and throttled him at half-time.

"You live on a knife-edge constantly, and the longer it goes on, you feel the nerves in the stadium.

"We weren't particularly good today, but I don't think we're in a position where we can start turning our nose up with 3-0 wins at home.

"We were better on Saturday and drew. The positive is it’s the first time we’ve scored three goals in 51 league games and it’s one defeat in 17 now.

"We need to be more clinical. You're not always going to create that many chances in the game.

"The forwards know that. Like I said, it's not a nice feeling living on a knife-edge, living on a bounce of a ball or an overhead kick, like we were on Saturday.

"We have to put the game to bed and I think once the second goal went in, it calmed a little bit.

"Barnsley are random in the way that they play. They put people in strange positions and it's really difficult to play against.

"But when you do turn it over, they're wide open. So, I just felt that's where those duels were important.

"I know people will say they're bottom of the league but it's not easy winning a game of football. We've seen that.

"I watched them play Sheffield Wednesday last Friday, and after the first 10 minutes, they dominated the game.

"We have to be respectful of what we're up against and be humble enough to go, ‘we can improve’.

#1737. Brighton & Hove Albion vs Universitatea Craiova - prediction, team news, lineups

By Oliver Thomas | 24 Nov 2026 19:45, Last updated: 24 Nov 2026 21:47

Seeking to bounce back from a rare Premier League defeat, Brighton & Hove Albion welcome Universitatea Craiova to the Amex Stadium for matchday four in the Conference League on Thursday night.

Both teams have identical records in the League Phase, collecting seven points courtesy of two wins and one draw from their first three games.

Following a strong run of six wins and one draw in seven Premier League games, Brighton came away from the MKM Stadium stunned after conceding two stoppage-time goals to lose 2-0 away against Hull City on Sunday.

Head coach Fabian Hurzeler rued his side’s “missed opportunity which can't happen again” after seeing leaders Arsenal and Man City also drop points over the weekend. Brighton still sit between both clubs in second place in the table, six points behind the Gunners and level on points with City in third.

Brighton have scored a whopping 40 goals in 18 games across all competitions this term, but the goals have dried up slightly in recent weeks; they have drawn a blank in front of goal in three of their last seven games and have scored at least twice on just two occasions during this run.

While the prospect of qualifying for next season’s Champions League via their domestic performances has become a distinct possibility, Brighton also have aspirations of winning their first-ever major trophy and following in the footsteps of Crystal Palace, West Ham and Chelsea in winning the Conference League this term.

The Seagulls, who secured a narrow 1-0 win over Getafe in Spain three weeks ago, currently sit fifth in the 36-team League Phase standings and could consolidate their place in the top eight with a victory on Thursday.

Should they beat Craiova without reply, they will become just the third English team this century to prevail in five consecutive European home games without conceding a goal.

Universitatea Craiova narrowly missed out on a place in the Conference League knockout rounds last season, finishing outside the top-24 positions on goal difference after accumulating seven points from six matches.

However, the White-Blues have already picked up the same number of points in half as many games so far this season and sit eighth in the table, leaving them well-placed to secure a historic first-ever appearance in the knockout stages of UEFA competition and potentially bypass the playoff round altogether.

After holding Getafe to a 1-1 draw on matchday one, Filipe Coelho’s side have since celebrated back-to-back wins over Andorran outfit Inter Escaldes (3-1) and Albanian team Egnatia (1-0) – they have not won three consecutive European games since a four-match streak in the 1984 UEFA Cup.

Craiova travel to the South Coast of England in superb form, having put together an impressive 15-game unbeaten run in all tournaments (W11 D4), most recently winning 6-2 against UTA Arad last weekend to retain their position at the top of the Romanian Superliga table.

Femi Azeez was “available” to face Hull at the weekend but was not selected in the matchday squad. The summer signing from Millwall recently recovered from a thigh injury and could be ready to make his long-awaited debut for the Seagulls on Thursday.

Brighton’s Jack Hinshelwood has scored each of his last five goals for Brighton on home soil and could be recalled to the first XI along with the likes of Ferdi Kadioglu, Mats Wieffer, Ibrahim Osman and Charalampos Kostoulas.

As for Universitatea Craiova, Monday Etim (muscle) and Pavlo Isenko (knee) are both ruled out with injuries, while Mihnea Radulescu is ineligible for the Conference League.

Coelho is expected to stick with a 3-4-3 formation, with Oleksandr Romanchuk, Nikola Stevanovic and Vladimir Screciu set to continue in a three-man backline as Nicusor Bancu and Carlos Mora operating as wing-backs.

Stefan Baiaram scored a brace at the weekend and could retain his starting spot on the left side of attack, while Simon Elisor and Assad Al-Hamlawi have both netted 11 goals this season and will battle it out for a start up front.

#1736. Amorim explains dislike for ‘AmorimBall’ term and what leaves him ‘really worried’ about Milan

Ruben Amorim had some interesting comments after the Frosinone win, including why he is not a fan of a term that is going viral.

Milan put on a five-star display at San Siro on Sunday night as they routed that Canarini. All five of their goals came via flowing counter-attacks, which has led to the tag ‘AmorimBall’ doing the rounds on social media, with many believing things are starting to truly click.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

The head coach is keeping his feet firmly on the ground though, as he spoke after the game about the need to find consistency both within matches but also from game-to-game. In this sense, Thursday’s trip to face Olympiacos is another big test.

Amorim was present in the press conference room at San Siro following the win to answer questions from journalists, with his comments relayed by MilanNews.

“I don’t like that expression. I think we play games to win, we want to dominate the opponent. I don’t think we succeeded today: every game has its own story, and today it was man-on-man.

“Today we didn’t have to prepare much: the idea was simply to give the ball to Pulisic, to Moreira, and then exploit the combinations of these players, the understandings they already have, and conquer space.

“Today you saw that we didn’t spend much time near the opponent’s penalty area and we scored five goals, because the space wasn’t there, it was forty meters away to attack on the run.

“That’s why Cisse came on to play as a striker and not, for example, Camarda: because there was space behind him and Cisse is very good at that. So, I think we’ve played very good games in the past, but today it was just a question of the quality of the players, of one-on-ones, of reading the game.

“Today it wasn’t a question of the coach, I think, but of the players. And they, since it was man-on-man, just had to do what they can do. when they’re so good: beating the man and opening up space. So today the credit goes entirely to the players.”

“I watched the France game and I think he’s one of the best players on the team. So I think his importance is paramount. You can see there’s rotation, there’s a lot of talent. France has a lot of talent, but Rabiot is always there. There’s a reason for that.

“And then, if you look at the way France play, with Mbappé, with the way all these players position themselves on the pitch, sometimes with four players with Olise as the No. 10, he has to stay there to play a different kind of game.

“With us, he’s the player who has to push the team forward, he’s the decisive element. In France, however, he has a different job to do. So it depends more on his role in the national team and his role at Milan.

“This changes his way of interpreting the game, and it’s further proof of how Rabiot can play by adapting to the team he’s in. For me, therefore, he’s one of the best midfielders in Europe. I hope his contract renewal comes soon.”

“Today’s match wasn’t just about tactics. We saw changes in position, one-on-one situations with plenty of space: it seemed like a crazy game. What I felt against Genoa and in the other matches was that we were too far away, we didn’t reach the final third of the pitch.

“We’re not like the big teams: if you look at the big teams, like Juventus, they might struggle to get results, but you see the volume they produce. For us, it’s a bit of the opposite, so I’m really worried that, if we don’t improve, we won’t be able to maintain this number of points.

“Today, however, was a step forward: we saw many players attacking the depth, something we hadn’t seen against Ferencvaros. In the other matches, we’d managed the ball well, but today we needed pace and runs.

“We need to be able to play both games within the same game, but today was clearly the type of game we needed to win.”

"I was proud of the players today for the way they really stood up to the challenge," he commented. "I thought when the bullets were flying, they were there.

"But I was absolutely delighted with it. I'm proud of the players, the way they got themselves back in the game.

"I don't think anybody's done that to them all season, I don't think anybody's done that since Tonda (Eckert) took over.

"Sometimes, when you look back on draws, it's bigger than just the draw, with the performance against a side of the quality that we played against."

#1728. No advantage played and an indirect free-kick: Pairetto criticised for Milan-Frosinone officiating

Referee Luca Pairetto has been criticised for his performance in AC Milan’s 5-1 win over Frosinone last night.

This morning’s edition of La Gazzetta dello Sport (seen below) comments on three incidents above all in which the referee ultimately seemed incapable of providing the right decision, one of which could have cost a goal.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

In the first half, Adrien Rabiot stole the ball from Cittadini, who blatantly dragged him back by the shirt. The ball rolled to Goncalo Ramos who was through on goal and had a man to his left, effectively making it a two-on-zero break with just the goalkeeper to beat.

Yet, the referee Pairetto blew his whistle for a foul and showed a yellow card to the defender. He immediately apologised for his error in failing to play the clear advantage for the Rossoneri, in an incident reminiscent of the Junior Messias goal not given against Spezia in 2021-22.

That wasn’t all, either. Nine minutes into the second half, an indirect free-kick was awarded inside the Frosinone penalty area following a clear back-pass from Calvani to Palmisani, that was actually flagged by the assistant referee and not initially given by Pairetto.

Former referee Mauro Bergonzi commented on the refereeing incidents in Milan-Frosinone to La Domenica Sportiva.

“In the first half, the referee failed to take the lead: he missed the lead, he squandered it, if we’re being honest. The situation is this: Cittadini fouls Rabiot, who steals the ball, a clear hold, the referee hastily calls the foul, and he also realises it immediately because he stops, as if to say, ‘Wow, it’s a shame I called’ because Gonçalo Ramos was hurtling toward goal.

“He apologizes, he says: ‘No, I apologise, I’m booking the Frosinone player.’ He said sorry. But this is something that really bothers you from a refereeing perspective because the lead was clear, but the referee’s gesture is commendable because he raises his hands and humbly says: ‘I made a mistake’.

“53rd minute: we rarely see them called on football pitches during matches. It’s a deliberate back pass from Calvani to the goalkeeper, the goalkeeper saves it, the referee wouldn’t have called anything, he turns to the right, looks at the assistant because the assistant signals it to him.

“Pairetto tells the assistant, ‘Well done’ and, to make matters worse, ‘Well done’ again. The assistant was good because he saw it perfectly correctly. He made his choice, he got it right because this is a pass, a deliberate back pass.

“Chiffi, the fourth official, is also there, pressing the button to communicate with the refereeing team via his headset, and if the assistant hadn’t seen it, the fourth official would have signaled it.”

Rangers manager Derek McInnes praised his side for having the mentality to grind out last-gasp winners and hailed their late victory over Motherwell as a ‘top-class performance’.

McInnes admits he would have liked a more comfortable evening from a match which saw his side fire 29 shots with 11 on target, but he was happy with the level of chance creation and delighted to see Ryan Naderi serve up yet another crucial goal with a deflected effort that made the difference two minutes from time.

Rangers had opened brightly with a Manny Fernandez goal on eight minutes, but looked like sliding to a third straight league draw away from home after Jake Girdwood-Reich had levelled for the home side in the first half.

‘I thought it was a very good, strong performance. I’ve just been told that every one of my outfield players had a shot,’ said McInnes, whose men are four points behind Celtic with a game in hand against Aberdeen at Ibrox on Tuesday.

‘I’ve never known a team who practice so much shooting, and crossing and finishing during the week. It was the only thing missing for us, I thought it was a top class performance.

‘Away from home in the Premiership, you’re never going to dominate a whole game. There were little spells Motherwell had on transitions, but our press was strong and we were aggressive. I’m just disappointed it took so long to get the winning goal.

Derek McInnes revels in the victory at Motherwell at full-time

Ryan naderi scored the dramatic late winner for Rangers as they closed the gap on Celtic

‘Equally, on the sidelines, I felt a goal was coming. It’s OK me feeling that, but I think the players feel it too and it’s important they do. It would have been such a body blow if we hadn’t found a winning goal, given the stats and the performance.

‘It’s a tough away game and it’s the first time we’ve won here in three years, so that illustrates that.

‘When we pick the bones out of it, there will be a lot of what we ask for in that game.

‘It’s good that we’ve got that in us, a last minute goal, because we know how important they are in a campaign. I’ve never found mental strength an issue for my side.

‘On this fantastic run, we’ve been very strong. We were by far the better team. We dominated the chances and a lot of what I was hoping for was there.

‘It was just that execution. We’ve had this story before, but, as long as we keep winning, I’m all right with that.

‘I’m getting asked about not putting teams to bed. That’s another away game with two goals. It’s four in a row now. In our last two home games, we’ve scored four and three, so scoring goals isn’t really causing a problem, even if people are looking for a negative.

‘I think that performance was an improvement from where we’ve been in recent weeks.’

McInnes also reserved special praise for matchwinner Naderi.

‘Ryan’s game is really strong at the minute. He looks like a very confident boy and so he should be,’ said the manager. ‘Wrongly now, when you think of Ryan or people ask me, it’s about him knocking his pan in.

‘His pressing is unbelievable and he’s a big horse up there. He runs and works and puts people under pressure, but he gets goals and has an influence. In that system tonight, his was the most important position for us, in terms of running channels and getting hold of the ball.

Manny Fernandez opened the scoring for the Ibrox men in the 2-1 victory

‘He led the line brilliantly. It was a proper No 9 performance.

Naderi admits he is delighted to be scoring messy goals that are making a real impact on his side’s challenge for the title.

‘I like those games. Of course we would like to win 3-0, but, when you win in the last minute, that's something special,’ said the Czech internationalist.

‘I can't score nice goals, only ugly ones.’

Motherwell head coach Alfred Johansson said: ‘It is obviously tough to concede that goal at the very end. We had a feeling we could finish the game with a draw.

‘I think Rangers were better than us. They had a good start to the game and it was tough for us conceding a goal from a set-piece when we are not aggressive enough.

‘At the end, we lost the energy. Rangers were turning up the heat in the last 15, 20 minutes. We were fighting and surviving and then they scored.

‘Alex Paulsen played fantastic in goal. He has been making a lot of saves for us this season and, at the end, it is tough for him to concede a goal like that.’

#1726. Theo Walcott sends message to ‘frustrated’ Arsenal star after Borussia Dortmund draw

The Walcott has urged Arsenal star Noni Madueke to ‘big himself up more’ after Mikel Arteta revealed last night’s man of the match was frustrated in the wake of a 1-1 draw against Borussia Dortmund.

For the second match in succession, the Premier League champions threw away a lead and squandered numerous chances to record a convincing win.

Viktor Gyokeres opened the scoring with a blistering strike in the 10th minute, but the Sweden international, like many of his teammates, was profligate thereafter.

Ultimately, the Gunners were forced to settle for a point following Maximilian Beier’s second half equaliser and Mikel Arteta’s side are now likely to require two wins from their remaining three group stage games to secure a top eight finish and avoid a two-legged play-off in the New Year.

Madueke, meanwhile, walked away with the man of the match accolade after another lively display. The England international has been to the fore in recent weeks and, in the absence of Bukayo Saka, appears to have won the faith of the manager who raised eyebrows with his decision to sanctionthe decision to sign him from Chelsea in a £52million deal 18 months ago.

Duff, who maintained his good record against former side Barnsley - five wins and a draw since leaving Oakwell in the summer of 2023—said: "Everyone knows what Humps can do. I said to him early in my tenure, I need to see what the worst version of Stephen Humphrys looks like.

#1723. How Sheffield United's 'dinosaur' changed tactics to turn game against Southampton

A game which began like a demonstration of how short the Blades were of the Championship elite ended with them proving they have what it takes to mix it with them.

For half an hour the Blades were outclassed by a Saints side who looked Premier League-ready. The Blades had only just over 20 per cent of the ball, which for them in a Championship home game is extremely rare.

Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

When Hamza Choudhury gave it away and failed to stop Lewis Dobbin curling the ball in, it was no less than the Saints deserved.

But from that unpromising start, the hosts turned it around. The second half was pretty much all them, so when Daniel Peretz saved brilliantly from Tahith Chong in the 83rd minute, you wondered if it was going to be one of those nights.

But the drama was just beginning. Jordan Ayew, who had shown what mood he was in with a nutmeg in the middle of the pitch, produced another in the 90th minute as he beat two men along the byline and teed up Sydie Peck to equalise. It still could have all been for nothing had Blades goalkeeper Michael Cooper not made a crucial save one-on-one with Samuel Edozie in the third added minute.

“The concentration of Michael was absolutely outstanding and the save was great,” commented Wilder.

“It would have been incredibly cruel if we'd have not got a result.

"There would (still) have been a certain amount of pride - not enjoyment because when you play as well as that, you have to get something.

"But I think I'd have put my head on the pillow and I would have gone, whatever the result, I don't think they've been dealt with like we've dealt with them in the second half."

As for the other bit, Tonda Eckert played the Blades the compliment of moving the player who normally operates in the hole in front of James Ward-Prowse and Flynn Downes to sit between them and the back four.

"They've got really technical players, and we didn't get to grips with their shape," admitted Wilder. "They had control of the game, they had seven touches in our box in the first half.

"So the old man, the dinosaur, had to get to grips with their press, our press, which we did after half an hour.

"We just wanted the two wide players to jump a little bit earlier and we needed to get around their six (holding midfielder) because the six was dominating and dictating the game. So we stuck somebody a little bit higher, got around their six and had a little bit of a change at the back, just slid over and got more pressure on the ball. In the second half we've had 31 touches in the box, 16 shots, 71 per cent possession.

"We made really good footballers resort to just clearing the lines for the last 20, 25 minutes. Sometimes, when you look back on draws, it's bigger than just the draw, with the performance against a side of the quality that we played against."

#1722. Shaun Wright-Phillips: Chelsea star must make himself ‘hard to ignore’ for Xabi Alonso

Former Chelsea and England star Shaun Wright-Phillips has urged Estevao to fight tooth and nail for a starting spot at Stamford Bridge and make himself ‘hard to ignore’ under Xabi Alonso.

Estevao burst onto the scene across an eye-catching opening campaign with Chelsea having joined the club from Palmeiras in the summer of 2025, racking up eight goals and four assists for the Blues.

A serious hamstring tear brought Estevao’s debut season to a premature end, though, a devastating blow that saw him miss out on a place in Brazil’s squad at this year’s World Cup.

Just days after Estevao sustained his injury, Chelsea decided to call time on Liam Rosenior’s turbulent managerial spell – and it has proven difficult for the 19-year-old to work himself back into the side since Alonso took charge.

The teenager had been limited to only two starts in the Carabao Cup approaching late October and rumours were beginning to circulate that he had grown frustrated with his peripheral role, with Barcelona reportedly keeping tabs on the situation.

Read exclusive analysis of the biggest stories in football with Metro's weekly football newsletter In The Mixer. Sign up now for free.

However, Joao Pedro’s absence over the last month-and-a-half has created an opportunity for Estevao in Alonso’s attack and the youngster has started two of Chelsea’s last three games.

A humbling 4-1 defeat at the hands of Leeds may not have been what Estevao had in mind for his return, though, following a substitute appearance at Sunderland, and he will no doubt be desperate to banish those memories with a strong performance versus Nottingham Forest on Friday night.

Asked if he felt that Estevao still had a big future at Chelsea under Alonso, Wright-Phillips told Metro, courtesy of kwiff: ‘It’s a hard one, because it seems like players at Chelsea outlive the managers, which is sad to say.

‘That’s where modern football is going at the minute. It seems like players are outlasting coaches.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

‘But in general, that’s more of a tactical thing, in that Xabi plays more with wing-backs.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

‘If you play Estevao, you want him in the front three. Chances come in random ways, so he will get his chance again, and he has to do what he did the other day.

‘When he came on, I thought he was flying: not the weekend just gone, the weekend before that [against Sunderland. He came on and played really, really well.

‘So that’s him saying, “Look, I’m good enough to stay in your squad.” If he continuously does that, it becomes hard to ignore.’

Another player whose development has hit something of a stumbling block in recent months is Malo Gusto, who, like Estevao, has found regular game-time hard to come by this season.

Reports just last week indicated Gusto could be open to the prospect of leaving Chelsea, with Manchester United understood to be among the right-back’s admirers.

But when asked if it could be time to move Gusto on should a suitable offer come in for the Frenchman, Wright-Phillips replied: ‘Who do you replace him with? I think Gusto is a really fantastic player.

‘He might not be happy, which is understandable, because before Xabi came, when the other managers were there, his playing time was a lot greater, because it was either him or Reece James.

‘Reece James has had bad luck, he’s injured quite a lot, so Gusto got to play a lot. Whereas now, I think he’s better than a bit-part player, to be honest.

‘I haven’t watched him enough this season to turn around and say he should definitely be starting, but from what I saw of him last year and the type of player he is, I’d have him in my team at the drop of a hat, because I don’t think there are many right-backs out there that are gettable of that standard.’

Chelsea splashed out in the region of £350million on new signings in the summer transfer window, including Morgan Rogers, who commanded a club-record fee of £117m when he joined from Aston Villa.

There were signs that the Blues were reaping the rewards of their big spending in a promising start to the 2026/27 campaign, with Alonso’s all-star front three firing on all cylinders.

An injury to Joao Pedro has coincided with a concerning dip in results, though, and Alonso’s men were targeted with a chorus of boos as they exited the pitch following their latest setback on Saturday.

‘I think at the very beginning he showed why he’s there, and at the minute it seems to have plateaued a bit. I don’t know what that’s from,’ Wright-Phillips said when asked what he had made of Alonso’s start to managerial life in the Premier League, with Chelsea languishing down in eighth.

‘Playing as many games as they have, with the internationals that have come in the way they’ve come in, it feels like the Champions League is every week; it feels like it’s the Carabao Cup or something every week at the minute.

‘It’s going to take a bit of time for the players to get used to that change, where every game is a big game now for everybody; literally every game comes around very quick.

‘I think those clubs will settle down and get it together because they’re lucky to have the players within that squad to do that.’

Pressed on whether there were any areas of the squad in need of strengthening in January, Wright-Phillips responded: ‘I’m not sure they need midfielders. I would say if they had two, or even one, solid defenders who can teach the other young ones there, that would be more than enough.

‘Chelsea have got an amazing squad. They’re missing that rock at the back; who will fight and die for everybody, because that rubs off on the team.

‘You might not like him, but that attitude and mentality will naturally rub off on you. Someone in the Thiago Silva mould.

‘They need to learn; they’re learning from each other. They’re good players, but to get to the top, most younger players and defenders learn off somebody with a lot more experience.’

Switching his focus to the title race, Wright-Phillips, who represented Manchester City, Chelsea and QPR during his playing days, picked out Brighton as this year’s surprise package.

And while they were beaten in stoppage time by Hull City at the weekend, the ex-England winger is confident the Seagulls remain one of Arsenal’s ‘main challengers’.

‘No disrespect to Arsenal, but the best club for me in the Premier League this season, to watch and for output, is Brighton,’ Wright-Phillips – a Premier League winner with Chelsea in 2006 – explained.

‘Brighton are probably playing the best, but they’re not at the top of the league.

‘It can change and go a different way. I don’t think Arsenal are playing that well, and I don’t think City have played that well, but they’re the two teams that know how to get results when they aren’t playing to the level they know their maximum is.

‘Unfortunately for City, that hasn’t happened in the last four games, which is something they have to deal with and turn around.

‘The Christmas period is the right time to possibly do it, because all the games come quick and fast and the league table can change a dozen times in that time.

‘The main challengers to Arsenal would be Brighton and Manchester City as it stands. They’re the ones with the points on the board.

‘Until people start putting the points on the board, which is turning around, you’re seeing Liverpool sneak back up the table.

‘There will be other challenges as well, but leading into this Christmas period, I would say Arsenal’s challenger right now is Brighton and Manchester City.

‘Brighton, I think, are the only team to beat both of those two teams and do it nicely as well. It wasn’t a smash and grab.’

#1720. Bruno Fernandes names club he could join after Man Utd: ‘I’ll never close the door’

Manchester United captain Bruno Fernandes is open to a return to Sporting CP before his career ends.

Fernandes spent three years in the Portuguese capital before joining United in January 2020. Th attacking midfielder has been the club’s best signing of the post Sir Alex Ferguson era but his future at Old Trafford is in more doubt than ever amid the club’s worst season in 40 years.

The Portugal international has already rejected to new contract offers. His current deal is set to expire in the summer but United do have the option to extend that by a further 12 months.

Fernandes is back at his old club this week with United taking on Sporting in the Champions League on Wednesday night. Speaking on Tuesday, the skipper revealed talks over a new deal are on hold now but was also quizzed on his club future.

Al-Hilal have made repeated attempts to sign the attacking midfielder but Fernandes says he would consider a return to Sporting if the chance were to present itself.

#1718. Ramos upset by substitution: The clarification and why Cisse came on over Camarda

Goncalo Ramos got his name on the scoresheet in AC Milan’s rout of Frosinone, but he was forced off in the second half.

As Sky (via Calciomercato.com) report, everything seemed great when Milan were dominating Frosinone at San Siro and scoring nearly every time they went forward. However, during the second half, a minor alarm sounded.

Ruben Amorim was forced to replace his Ramos in the 50th minute. The Portuguese striker – who had scored in the first half – was hastily removed from the pitch by the head coach shortly after Ardon Jashari’s goal to make it 3-1.

The reason? The change was made due to a minor muscle problem that the player reported to the bench, even though Ramos himself did not seem happy about the substitution at the time of the change.

The former PSG man informed the bench that he had a small calf problem and – to avoid worsening the issue – Amorim immediately opted for a substitution. Alphadjo Cisse was sent on in his place, and he scored the fourth goal just a few minutes later.

When he was taken off, Ramos showed a grimace of disapproval towards his bench, miming the ‘wait’ gesture. He then complained that he would have liked to try to stay on the pitch, but some post-match comments cleared things up.

When asked if his calf is ok, he told DAZN: “Yes, yes, everything’s fine, everything’s fine.” Rabiot later revealed the background to the substitution to Sky, admitting that he played a hand in convincing the coach.

“Gonçalo is the first player to do a lot. Today I saw he had a bit of pain in his thigh. I know he’s a very important player for us, and we have a lot of matches. I even asked the coach to let him rest a bit,” the Frenchman said.

Speaking to DAZN after the final whistle, Amorim was asked why he felt it was right for Cisse to come on rather than Francesco Camarda, the only other natural centre-forward in the squad

“We didn’t spend many minutes near the penalty area; he was behind. Today we were 40 metres from the goal, and Cisse was perfect for that. That’s why I didn’t bring on Camarda for Ramos: I needed someone who could run in behind.”

#1717. Championship strugglers sack managerial duo as reality of second tier hits hard

Lincoln City have sacked joint head coaches Chris Cohen and Tom Shaw after the club’s run of five straight Sky Bet Championship defeats.

#1716. Frustrated Cole Palmer shares frosty exchange with Joao Pedro after upsetting Chelsea staff member before walking off down the tunnel after 4-1 drubbing by Leeds

Published: 16:00 EST, 21 November 2026 | Updated: 19:04 EST, 21 November 2026

Cole Palmer was involved in a frustrated exchange with team-mate Joao Pedro after Chelsea crashed to a 4-1 home defeat against Leeds.

The Blues were beaten by Leeds at Stamford Bridge for the first time since 1999, despite having taken the lead through Emmanuel Emegha's first goal for the club.

Noah Okafor scored twice for Leeds either side of a Dominic Calvert-Lewin penalty, with Brenden Aaronson adding a fourth in stoppage time.

Palmer, who opted against going around the pitch applauding the remaining fans at full-time, was captured approaching Joao Pedro following the match.

The Chelsea star could be seen covering his mouth while speaking to his team-mate, who had been left to watch from the sidelines as he continues his recovery from injury.

Joao Pedro put his hand on Palmer's shoulder as he responded to his team-mate, with the Brazilian then shrugging his shoulders as a frustrated Palmer went to walk down the tunnel.

Cole Palmer and Joao Pedro were involved in a frosty exchange following Chelsea's 4-1 home defeat by Leeds. Source: Instagram/farihaxchels

Joao Pedro shrugged his shoulders as a frustrated Palmer headed down the tunnel after their exchange. Source: Instagram/farihaxchels

Chelsea boss Xabi Alonso was asked post-match about the exchange, amid a suggestion Joao Pedro and Willie Isa, Chelsea's player support and development officer, had attempted to persuade Palmer to applaud the fans.

‘No, we were disappointed, the fans were disappointed because the expectations from them are high,' Alonso responded.

'We feel sorry for them and we need to go through together and to find solutions to that and now, as I said, for sure it’s not the easiest moment.

‘It’s a fragile moment but we need to work together and stick together because there is still such a long way to go.'

Alonso's side have now lost three of their last four Premier League matches, having been beaten at home by rivals Tottenham and falling to defeat at Sunderland prior to the international break.

The Blues have now dropped to eighth in the table, with Alonso's side having won five, drawn one and lost five of their 11 matches to date.

Palmer had begun the season brightly under Alonso by scoring in their opening two fixtures but has only scored one league goal since, netting with a penalty in a 2-0 win over Man United.

Chelsea will look to bounce back when they face struggling Nottingham Forest and Crystal Palace in their next two matches, before blockbuster clashes with Liverpool and Man City.

#1715. Man United captain Bruno Fernandes drops Sporting Lisbon return hint as Portuguese discusses contract situation

By Matt Law | 24 Nov 2026 20:03, Last updated: 24 Nov 2026 20:04

Manchester United captain Bruno Fernandes has said that his future is currently "not important".

Fernandes, 32, only has a contract with the Red Devils until the end of the campaign, but the club do have the option to extend it for a further 12 months.

The Portugal international has reportedly rejected Man United's latest offer, allegedly wanting a longer deal with higher wages given his contribution during a tough period.

There is currently speculation surrounding his future at Old Trafford, but Fernandes has insisted that his main focus for the moment is on helping Man United to turn their campaign around.

"For us to start winning games and then we can talk about contract," Fernandes told reporters ahead of Wednesday's Champions League clash with Sporting Lisbon, when asked what would need to happen for him to sign a new deal.

"It’s not important now. It’s my future, I haven’t got much left in my contract, but we will have time to speak about that. The conversations stopped when we thought now was not the moment."

Fernandes also refused to "close the door" on returning to Sporting before the end of his career.

"I will never close the door to [returning to] Sporting. It will always be a club with a special place in my heart," the Man United captain added.

The Portuguese represented Sporting between 2017 and 2020 ahead of a move to Man United, scoring 63 goals and registering 50 assists in 137 appearances for the club.

Since arriving at Man United, Fernandes has a record of 113 goals and 111 assists in 342 appearances for the English team in all competitions.

Fernandes is again expected to be in the starting side when the Red Devils tackle Sporting in the league stage of the Champions League on Wednesday night.

The playmaker has six goals and three assists in 15 appearances in all competitions this season.

Meanwhile, Fernandes has a record of nine goals and 12 assists in 29 career appearances in the Champions League during his time at Sporting and Man United.

#1714. Raheem Sterling dodges prison for dangerously driving Lamborghini

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

Former England footballer Raheem Sterling, 31, has been handed a suspended prison sentence today.

He was sentenced to 12 months in prison, suspended for 18 months, at Basingstoke Magistrates’ Court after dangerously driving his Lamborghini and possessing nitrous oxide canisters.

Sterling was also ordered to complete 100 hours of unpaid work and was banned from driving for 24 months.

He had been seen by other motorists inhaling from a balloon while driving his black sports car, swerving in and out of lanes – with one driver ‘shocked’ by what he saw, a court previously heard.

Sterling arrived at Basingstoke Magistrates’ Court this morning, wearing a black top and dark trousers.

Read exclusive analysis of the biggest stories in football with Metro's weekly football newsletter In The Mixer. Sign up now for free.

He has been on unconditional bail and subject to an interim driving ban since he admitted offences in September.

The former Manchester City player had pleaded guilty at the Hampshire court to driving a Lamborghini Urus dangerously on the M25, the M3, the A327 and Minley Road before he crashed on the morning of May 28.

Sterling also admitted possession of six nitrous oxide canisters for wrongful inhalation, a class C drug, and failing to provide a specimen.

Police body-worn footage of the footballer’s arrest at 9.15am shows him in the crashed car with two canisters on his lap as the officer tells him: ‘You can put that down mate.’

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

The court previously heard witness Christopher Jennings on the M25 called 999 at 7.49am after he was driving in parallel to Sterling’s car and ‘he was shocked by what he saw’.

Sterling scored 20 goals in 82 appearances for England, helping Gareth Southgate’s side reach the 2018 World Cup semi-finals and the final of Euro 2020.

He came through the academy at QPR before joining Liverpool, where he made his senior debut.

Sterling, who was born in Kingston, Jamaica, moved to Manchester City in 2015 and won four Premier League titles, five League Cups and the FA Cup in 2019.

He left for Chelsea in 2022 but, after falling out of favour, spent the 2024-25 season on loan at Arsenal.

After leaving Stamford Bridge, Sterling joined Dutch club Feyenoord on a short-term deal until the end of the season.

Sterling was made an MBE in the 2021 Queen’s Birthday Honours for services to racial equality in sport after fronting anti-racism and discrimination campaigns and speaking out against racism on and off the pitch for several years.

It came amid controversy over England fans booing players taking the knee at matches as a gesture against intolerance.
