#1709. Ex-Man United star Gordon Strachan tells Mauricio Pochettino what will get the Red Devils out of current crisis

By Matt Law | 24 Nov 2026 20:30, Last updated: 24 Nov 2026 20:31

Manchester United need to show character as they attempt to bounce back in Wednesday's Champions League clash with Sporting Lisbon, ex-Red Devils midfielder Gordon Strachan has exclusively told Sports Mole.

The 20-time English champions will enter the European fixture with Sporting off the back of a 4-0 defeat to Liverpool in the Premier League.

Mauricio Pochettino will now take charge of his first European match for Man United, and there is pressure on the Argentine following the four-goal mauling at Anfield.

When asked whether the Sporting match provided Man United with the perfect chance to bounce back from the defeat to Liverpool, Strachan insisted that the players need to show character and heart in a bid to turn the club's campaign around.

"Well, to be fair, Liverpool should never really be a big ask for Man United as such, because the record there is terrific over the years. I mean, it's always been decent. That fixture is one of the ones that Liverpool really want to win because they know how dangerous Man United are," said Strachan.

"But it wasn't a real game after the first two goals, there was the sending-off, you know. And even the free kick, you think, right, if you see the free kick off, we can reorganise and organise with 10 players. We never even had time to do that. So, as a manager, you can't count that, you've just got to count that as a no-game.

"But what you can do in that situation is ask, who kept pressing? Who do I want in my team? Because in adversity, you see the real character coming out, and in adversity in big games, you see the real character. And it's not on your social media, it's not saying to the fans, we love you and we're sorry and all the rest of it. Don't apologise to me, just do something about it.

"Don't come in and hold your hand up and say, I'm sorry, gaffer. Don't apologise to me because I'm not interested in you telling me you're sorry for making a mistake. Just don't make a mistake. And if you do make a mistake, rectify it as quickly as possible.

"What I'm talking about is managers will try and sort it out. Invariably, unless you can do something about it, physically or mentally, then it will appear again. They will appear, and they'll appear in crisis moments.

"As I said, your character is shown up in crisis times and the same mistakes will be made by the same people whoever they play. And some people are just not good enough to play at this level.

"You know, we all talk about shapes and systems and this and that. The funny thing is, I don't think there's too many people talking about systems now. I think most people are now talking about, even if you talk with a bright manager, they talk about putting people under pressure, winning knockdowns, getting to the ball first, getting the ball to your front men.

"So, the system thing has kind of changed now. The only one that kind of really changes, it's gone from a back four to a back three, but the rest, like Brighton, Liverpool, Bournemouth, they're all playing the same sort of way.

"It's a kind of 4-2-3-1, where the four players up front are attacking players, whatever way you want to use it, two wide men, just off the front. Wales were the same with Craig Bellamy.

"So, I think that people are moving to that in general now, but there's not too much talking about systems now. It's more about closing down, getting to knockdowns, winning headers and free kicks and corner kicks."

Man United have six points to show from their two matches in the league stage of this season's Champions League.

Gordon Strachan was speaking to Sports Mole on behalf of William Hill Football Odds.

#1707. Guardiola urges Portugal to ‘ensure a dignified end to Ronaldo’s career’

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Pep Guardiola has called on the Portuguese Football Federation (FPF) to "ensure a dignified end to Cristiano Ronaldo's career".

Ronaldo called time on his international career earlier this month, retiring as Portugal's all-time leading scorer and appearance-maker, netting 146 goals in 234 games.

After making his debut in 2003, Ronaldo led Portugal to their first-ever major trophy at Euro 2016 and also won the Nations League in 2019 and 2025.

His time with Portugal ended abruptly, with the 41-year-old leaving their camp midway through the September-October international break after a fallout with head coach Jorge Jesus.

He was subsequently given a 30-day suspension by the FPF, though he announced his retirement ahead of the November break.

The FPF said they would plan a farewell for Ronaldo, and Guardiola has urged them to do so.

"The Portuguese Football Federation must ensure a dignified end to Cristiano Ronaldo's career," Guardiola said on Romario TV.

"Cristiano Ronaldo shouldn't leave the Portuguese national team in this manner. They can't let him go like this.

Messi also retired from international football this season, after Argentina finished runners-up at the 2026 World Cup.

"I think the two of them helped each other a great deal; if Messi hadn't had Cristiano, or if Cristiano hadn't had Messi, their careers would likely have been shorter," Guardiola added.

#1706. Marseille vs Levski Sofia - prediction, team news, lineups

By Freddie Cotton | 24 Nov 2026 20:48, Last updated: 24 Nov 2026 20:58

Marseille welcome Levski Sofia to the Stade Velodrome on Thursday evening on matchday five of the 2026-27 UEFA Europa League campaign.

In their previous competition outing, Les Olympiens claimed a crucial 1-0 win away to Bayer Leverkusen, while the Blues beat Polish side Jagiellonia by the same scoreline at the National Stadium Vasil Levski.

After narrowly missing out on booking their place in the UEFA Champions League for the second consecutive year last season, finishing fifth in Ligue 1 and just one point below Lyon in fourth, Marseille will be extremely disappointed with how they have performed on the continent so far this campaign.

Although they edged out Leverkusen in their latest Europa League fixture, losses to Sturm Graz, Olympiacos and Besiktas in each of their opening three matches mean Bruno Genesio’s men have earned just three points so far in Europe, leaving them 31st in the league phase table and outside of the knockout stage places.

Despite conceding two late goals to lose against Le Mans on Sunday evening, Les Olympiens have seen a huge improvement in their league endeavours, having won each of their prior five matches to currently sit fifth in the Ligue 1 table and just three points outside the automatic Champions League qualification places.

Marseille are yet to claim victory over Levski, though they do boast a mainly positive record against Bulgarian opposition, having beaten CSKA Sofia in each of their other two meetings with efbet League sides.

Having won their first efbet League title since 2009 last season and finished 10 points ahead of runners-up Ludogorets, who had triumphed in each of the previous 14 consecutive campaigns, Levski competed in the qualifying stages of the Champions League for the first time in 17 years during the summer.

The Blues impressed in their efforts for tournament qualification, beating Borac Banja Luka, Univ Craiova and Kairat Almaty to progress to the decisive playoff tie, but having endured a 4-0 aggregate defeat against Greek giants AEK Athens, the Bulgarian side are instead competing in the Europa League this season.

However, Julio Velazquez’s men have given a good account of themselves so far on the continent as after taking just one point from their first two matches, Levski have won back-to-back matches in the Europa League to sit 10th in the standings with seven points and only outside the round-of-16 positions on goal difference.

While the Blues do not have the best recent record against French opposition, having won just one of their previous four meetings with Ligue 1 sides, that triumph did come over Marseille, with Levski securing a 1-0 win over Les Olympiens in the group stages of this competition in December 2005, when it was branded as the UEFA Cup.

>> Click here to view the best UK football betting sites for Thursday's fixture<<

Marseille continue to be without Canadian defender Derek Cornelius, who has been sidelined since the end of September with a hip issue, while former Chelsea full-back Emerson Palmieri is also unavailable due to a knee problem.

On a more positive note, after missing the match against Leverkusen as a precaution, Moroccan forward Amine Harit has started Les Olympiens’ previous two league fixtures and looks set to return to feature from the off in the week too.

Netting eight Ligue 1 goals so far this season, including one in each of his previous four outings, Algerian forward Amine Gouiri is undoubtedly the hosts’ biggest threat going forward and will be hoping to add to his winner against Leverkusen last time out in the competition.

Having been left out of Levski’s Europa League squad list, Oliver Kamdem, Mustapha Sangare and Petko Hristov are all unavailable for Thursday’s fixture, while 34-year-old striker Radoslav Kirilov remains out with a knee issue.

However, the Blues will be delighted to have welcomed midfielder Asen Mitkov back from injury against Lok. Sofia on Sunday afternoon and the 21-year-old will be hopeful for more minutes in the week too.

Contributing to six goals in 12 league appearances, Portuguese midfielder Serginho has been the visitors’ dangerman so far this season and will be hoping to replicate his efbet League form on the continent this week.

De Lange; Bezahaf, Egan-Riley, Aguerd, Garcia; Hojbjerg; Weah, Kondogbia, Abdelli, Paixao; Gouiri

Vutsov; Neves, Dimitrov, Makoun, Maicon; Sergingo, Grujic, Moubarik; Soula, Reinaldo, Everton Bala

Having finally bounced back from their three-game losing streak in the Europa League by claiming an important win over Leverkusen in their latest European outing, Marseille will certainly be aiming to fight their way into the knockout progression places with victory on Thursday evening.

While Levski have made a promising start to their campaign, we think Les Olympiens will bag all three points at the Stade Velodrome this week and are backing them to mount a late charge for a top-eight finish in the league phase.

#1705. Frosinone boss Alvini content with aggressive approach vs. Milan despite ‘naive’ mistakes

Frosinone head coach Massimiliano Alvini has admitted that his side simply gave AC Milan too many opportunities.

It has been a very positive return to the top flight for Frosinone so far, given that a point last night at San Siro would have seen them move back into the European places. However, they were ultimately given a bit of a humbling by Milan, who won 5-1 thanks to a ruthless counter-attacking display.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Some have questioned if the Canarini were a bit too aggressive in their approach to the game, given they played with such a high line and allowed space for Adrien Rabiot, Diego Moreira, Goncalo Ramos, Ardon Jashari, Alphadjo Cisse and Christian Pulisic to exploit.

Alvini was present in the press conference room at San Siro after the full-time whistle and he analysed what was perhaps the most difficult night of the season for his team. MilanNews transcribed his assessments.

Should the game have been played differently?

“Frosinone played their game but made a few mistakes they don’t usually make, but that’s certainly not my concern, losing by such a large margin. What’s worrying are the mistakes we made that we could have avoided.”

“We made a mistake on the first goal, which was a mistake of our own, while the other goals we conceded were goals we absolutely could have avoided. We conceded them and were naive.

“It’s a mistake of our own, and so today, from this perspective, if you come to Milan against Milan and make these mistakes, it’s only natural that we end up losing like this, by such a large scoreline.

“That’s the analysis, even though I think the scoreline is even too large: the first half, in my opinion, was extraordinary on our part.”

Did the absences have an impact, forcing you to experiment a bit?

“There’s nothing experimental about it. We played with the same principles, running forward to get to Rabiot. We preferred to bring on a defender who would push forward rather than a midfielder.

“In my opinion, this definitely didn’t influence the result, but rather the attitude, the idea, or the match strategy. And we certainly made – as I said before and I’ll repeat – mistakes we don’t usually make.

“If you give Milan certain chances, with such strong players and the quality of this team, you risk losing, and that’s what happened. You risk losing with a heavy defeat, and that’s what happened.

“He had a problem with that back heel in the box, and he definitely needs tests. It’s too early now; we’ll have to wait for the tests, which will be done starting Tuesday, but it’s definitely a problem.”

“We had a chance with Monterisi after a minute, we hit the post, and we created a lot. I have nothing to say to the team for their attitude and the way they played.

“We, I repeat, made some naivety, some mistakes. It’s also up to me to understand that there are important players on the other side who can cause problems.”

“It’s a result that definitely needs to be managed, navigated, and channeled, but it doesn’t change my attitude at all. We have 20 points today. The path we need to take is to try to stay in Serie A, and we’ll try to do so with this attitude, with this identity: this is the path we’ll take.

“Four years ago, I drew a game against Milan by playing defensively, and we took home a point. Today we made some mistakes, but this is the path we’ll take. I’m happier with the management, with the team’s identity, to try to achieve that objective, and this is what we’ll continue to do.”

Viktor Gyokeres opened the scoring in the first half with a wonderful dipping strike from distance, but it then became a night of missed chances for the Gunners.

Maximilian Beier equalised after the break and despite the hosts pushing constantly for a winner, it would not come.

#1703. Revealed: Just two Man United stars are selected in combined XI with Liverpool by stats boffins as Andoni Iraola's defence dominates... but is the Liverpool boss missing a hidden gem?

Published: 01:43 EST, 22 November 2026 | Updated: 01:45 EST, 22 November 2026

All eyes will be on Manchester United's new head coach Mauricio Pochettino when they take on Liverpool at Anfield this afternoon.

Liverpool manager Andoni Iraola has freshened up the squad since joining in the summer, including the £123million purchase of Bradley Barcola from Paris Saint-Germain, while blending in young emerging talent. They have made a solid start across all four competitions, knocking Chelsea out of the League Cup on penalties, and they currently sit in fourth place in the Premier League.

United have had a dire start to the season, with only one win in 10 games leading to the axeing of head coach Michael Carrick. Will his replacement be able to save the season and galvanise a group of talented but dispirited players?

So, who from United’s struggling side have done enough to break into Sofascore's combined XI based on their performances throughout the 2026-27 season so far?

Manchester United's new head coach Mauricio Pochettino will face his first test against Liverpool on Sunday

United currently sit at 18th in the Premier League after a disappointing start to the season

Between the sticks is Liverpool’s No 1, who since signing for a record fee in 2018, has established himself as one of the best shot-stoppers in the world.

Rated for his positioning, distribution and consistency, Alisson has an impressive record, especially in one-on-one situations.

The 34-year-old Brazilian goalkeeper has kept four clean sheets in 10 league appearances this season, averaging 2.5 saves per game. He has conceded 10 goals, including a brutal 3-0 loss to Manchester City at Anfield last month.

Alisson was poor in Liverpool's 3-2 defeat by Fenerbahce but responded with a fine display in the Reds' 3-1 win over Crystal Palace when back in league action days later.

At right back is Liverpool’s Ronald Araujo, on loan from Barcelona this season, and there are already cries from Liverpool fans to sign him permanently.

The 27-year-old is a natural centre back, but he has done wonders to ease Liverpool’s problems in the right-back position. Jeremie Frimpong started the season in that position but the Liverpool backline were far too exposed. Araujo has helped Liverpool tighten up defensively.

The Uruguayan defender has featured in all of Liverpool’s league matches so far this season, with his defensive actions helping him contribute inside his own penalty box. He has averaged six clearances per game and has won 30 aerial duels so far this season, behind only Virgil van Dijk in the Liverpool squad.

Ronald Araujo (right) has impressed this season for Liverpool, on loan from Barcelona

Jeremy Jacquet is a young player to watch this season after joining Liverpool this summer.

The 21-year-old has a 95 per cent accurate pass rate, including long balls. He had a standout performance against Fulham early on in the season, winning five aerial duels, five recoveries and making a clearance off the line to keep his team in the game.

Despite playing in France's second division just two seasons ago, Jacquet has fitted seamlessly into Iraola's style of play at Liverpool and there are suggestions he is an upgrade on the man he replaced, fellow France international Ibrahima Konate.

Centre back - Virgil van Dijk (Liverpool)

It is no surprise that Liverpool and Netherlands team captain Virgil van Dijk makes it into the XI.

Known for his strength, leadership, speed and aerial ability, he is the only defender to win the UEFA Men's Player of the Year Award, and finished runner-up for both the Ballon d'Or and Best FIFA Men's Player in 2019.

This season, he has shown his aerial ability with 3.8 duels won in the air (79 per cent) per game and 4.8 total duels won per game.

The team struggled against Manchester City, however. In the game at Anfield that ended their unbeaten run, Van Dijk only made four defensive contributions and picked up a yellow card for a frustrated foul on Rayan Cherki in added time.

Van Dijk's contract expires next summer, and the 35-year-old has a big decision to make.

Is Iraola missing a hidden gem? Tsimikas is very much understudy to Milos Kerkez after acting as a reliable deputy to Andy Robertson.

But across all competitions this season he is statistically rated higher than the man who's ahead of him in the pecking order. Kerkez is rated at 6.67 – so it is tight.

Nicknamed 'Greek Scouser' by Reds fans, Tsimikas has only started five games but has produced three assists with 1.78 key passes and 1.56 accurate crosses.

Manchester United, on the other hand, have struggled to fill this position. They were unable to recruit in the summer, and now rely on Luke Shaw – who has been sidelined with a muscular issue since limping off during their 1-1 draw with Tottenham Hotspur in October – and are adapting with makeshift alternatives.

Liverpool captain Virgil van Dijk celebrates with the fans after beating Crystal Palace

Centre midfield – Dominik Szoboszlai (Liverpool)

Versatile vice-captain Dominik Szoboszlai signed a new five-year contract with Liverpool this summer, and has proven his worth after scoring a stoppage-time penalty to level the score in their first game of the season against Newcastle.

With his ability to go forward and send crosses into the box and drop back to defend, Szoboszlai has been crucial for ball recovery, key passes and creating big chances.

It is a testament to his creative ability, including registering four big chances and one assist in the Premier League this season, that he makes the XI despite being sidelined with a hamstring injury for three games.

However, the Hungary midfielder has received backlash from fans for playing 90 minutes for his country in a 2-0 win against Georgia in the UEFA Nations League despite early withdrawal against Palace, and injury concerns remain ahead of this afternoon's clash.

Centre midfield – Kobbie Mainoo (Manchester United)

Only one of two Manchester United players in this line-up, Kobbie Mainoo deserves recognition for his creative efforts this season, which have earned him the second highest Sofascore rating in this XI.

The 21-year-old England midfielder is known for his high pressing and long balls to create chances up the pitch. He has also registered four shots from outside the box.

He has been through some turbulent times at Old Trafford but Michael Carrick turned to him regularly this season.

A product of Manchester United's youth system and there is plenty of potential, especially with new manager Mauricio Pochettino’s penchant for developing young players. A chance to refresh and discover his best form.

Kobbie Mainoo is one of only two United players to make the combined XI this weekend

Centre midfield – Alexis Mac Allister (Liverpool)

After his public revelation that he nearly left Liverpool, Alexis Mac Allister has been in form and pulling the strings in midfield and played an important role in Liverpool's season so far.

He headed in Liverpool’s second goal in their 3-1 away win over Crystal Palace and his passing and playmaking abilities have been key for their attacking chances this season.

He has scored five goals in 16 appearances across all competitions this season.

Right forward – Bruno Fernandes (Manchester United)

The Portugal forward was named the PFA Players' Player of the Year last season, but he has divided United fans this season.

Inconsistent performances and publicly questioning Carrick's tactics after defeat in Como.

In the 1-1 draw against Spurs at Old Trafford, the skipper did not record his first successful pass until the 23rd minute, and he missed a big chance against Chelsea.

He has bagged four goals and two assists in the Premier League so far, but this is largely owing to his hat-trick against Ipswich, which earned him a perfect 10 Sofascore rating.

United fans will hope he can get back to his old ways under Pochettino.

United fans will be desperate to see Bruno Fernandes find consistent performances again

Centre-forward – Alexander Isak (Liverpool)

Liverpool’s star striker, transferred for a British record-breaking fee of £125million last summer, has scored eight goals in 14 games this season, showing just how clinical he can be.

Reds fans are finally seeing the form that earned him the big-money move from Newcastle.

Isak edges out United's Bryan Mbeumo to lead the line in this team. He has a 55.6 per cent big chance conversion, scoring a goal every 113 minutes.

The Dutchman is establishing himself as Liverpool's go-to wideman among Iraola's plethora of options. His rapid pace and direct approach proves a massive threat.

This season his end product has improved, notching three goals and supplying six assists in 12 appearances across all competitions.

He is proving to be a reliable outlet while summer signings Bradley Barcola and Victor Munoz continue to settle into life in England.

His stunning long-range strike to equalise against Newcastle United shows just how clinical he can be in front of goal.

He averages 1.9 key passes and one big chance per game, which lands him a spot in this XI.

#1702. Man United head coach Mauricio Pochettino issues Luke Shaw fitness update as "fragile" accusation is rejected

By Matt Law | 24 Nov 2026 21:10, Last updated: 24 Nov 2026 21:12

Manchester United head coach Mauricio Pochettino has refused to confirm whether Luke Shaw will be involved in Wednesday's Champions League clash with Sporting Lisbon.

Shaw has made the trip to Portugal alongside his teammates, having recovered from the muscular problem that has sidelined him since the early stages of October.

The 31-year-old has been a huge miss at the back for Man United, and Pochettino has welcomed the Englishman's return to fitness.

However, it remains to be seen whether he is involved against Sporting.

“All the players need to feel they can have an impact for the team and they can perform," Pochettino told reporters during his pre-game press conference.

“It’s up to us to give the opportunities to every single player in the moment that we believe that they deserve to be involved in the game.

“Of course, I know Luke from the past, in our time in Southampton, but all [of us who are] involved, we are not the same people now. It’s more than 10 years ago.

“Obviously, it’s good to see him and he came from a small issue but now he needs to recover his best form.

“It’s good to have him, because he’s experienced everything with the squad, but we’ll see if he can be involved tomorrow or not, from the beginning or during the game.”

Matheus Cunha is suspended for the match following his red card against Roma in the team's last European fixture, while Benjamin Sesko, Marcus Rashford, Carlos Baleba and Manuel Ugarte are all injured for the 20-time English champions.

Pochettino also insisted during his press conference that Man United are 'not a fragile team' despite their huge difficulties this season.

The Red Devils will enter the game with Sporting off the back of a 4-0 defeat to Liverpool, and they currently sit down in 19th spot in the Premier League table.

"We are not fragile, we are a strong team who last season finished third. Sometimes things happen in football for different reasons. We need to identify why and we are working on it. I think we are going to turn the situation around," said the head coach.

Man United have two wins and two draws from their four matches in this season's Champions League, beating Sabah and Roma either side of defeats to Atletico Madrid and Como.

#1701. Sarr injury still ‘touch and go’, reveals Palace boss Frank

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Thomas Frank revealed Ismaila Sarr's injury is still "touch and go" and ruled the winger out for Crystal Palace's Europa League encounter with Real Sociedad.

Sarr has missed each of Palace's last six games with a groin injury, last appearing in their 2-2 draw with Besiktas on October 22.

The 28-year-old scored 21 goals across 45 games in all competitions last season, marking the best scoring campaign of his career.

Since his move to Selhurst in August 2024, Sarr (41 – 33 goals, eight assists) has directly contributed to the joint-most goals among Palace players, along with Jean-Philippe Mateta.

However, Sarr will have to wait longer to appear under Frank, who took over from Pierre Sage during the international break.

"Sarr, that will not be a long, long one, but it will be weeks before he can help the team," said Frank.

"That [Sarr returning after the international break] was the hope. But it's a groin issue, so it's a bit touch and go. It's nothing big, it will just take time."

MD-1. Ready for work.  https://t.co/ck6ICuGVKD

— Crystal Palace F.C. (@CPFC) November 25, 2026

Palace's only previous European meeting with a Spanish side came in the 2025-26 Conference League final, when they won 1-0 against Rayo Vallecano.

Since losing 1-0 to AEK Larnaca in October 2025 in the Conference League, Palace are unbeaten in all eight major European games at Selhurst Park (W5 D3).

La Real have just one win in 11 European games against English teams (D3 L7), winning 1-0 away at Manchester United in September 2022.

"To be able to play the Europa League is fantastic," added Frank.

"It's a big praise to the former staff, the reason why we are here is because they won the Conference League.

"We're going to be very competitive tomorrow and will do everything we can to win the game."

#1700. Can Ethan Nwaneri play against Arsenal for loan club Borussia Dortmund in the Champions League tonight?

Your weekly briefing on Arsenal, featuring team news and expert analysis from Matt Verri

Arsenal dropped points from a winning position for the second time in as many games following a 1-1 Champions League draw with Borussia Dortmund at the Emirates Stadium.

Mikel Arteta’s men led at the interval after Viktor Gyokeres scored his first goal on home soil in 206 days with a wonderful 25-yard opener inside 10 minutes.

But just as they did in the Premier League at Newcastle on Saturday, Arsenal were unable to see out the victory, with Maximilian Beier netting for the visitors after half-time.

Jobe Bellingham had a goal ruled out for offside, while Gyokeres could perhaps count himself fortunate not to give away a penalty when a Dortmund corner struck him on the arm.

Gyokeres then wasted a golden opportunity to restore Arsenal’s advantage when he headed wide unmarked from six yards, while the ball cannoned off Serhou Guirassy to twice strike the Dortmund post in the closing stages. Declan Rice hit the woodwork again for Arsenal with five minutes left.

The draw leaves Arsenal fifth in the table, but they could be on the bubble of the top-eight places – which are assured of automatic qualification for the next phase – if results work against them on Wednesday.

Gyokeres was introduced only as a stoppage-time substitute in Arsenal’s 2-2 draw at St James’ Park despite the Gunners chasing the game for most of the second half.

Here, he began from the start and opened the scoring with his first meaningful contribution of the game.

Noni Madueke had time and space to bring down a crossfield ball before finding Gyokeres, who immediately tried his luck from range, and perhaps catching Gregor Kobel in the visiting goal by surprise.

But that was to take away nothing from the velocity and dip behind Gyokeres’ effort – the sort of strike which encouraged Arsenal to spend £68million last summer but has not always been repaid. It was Gyokeres’ first at the Emirates since May.

Rice fired over from range and then only a last-ditch tackle from Dortmund captain Nico Schlotterbeck denied the England midfielder moments later. Arsenal led at the break, but they did in the North East before a second-half collapse saw them emerge with just a point, rather than three.

#1698. Real Madrid 5-1 PSV Eindhoven: Kylian Mbappe creates Champions League history in statement Los Blancos win

By Matt Law | 24 Nov 2026 21:53, Last updated: 24 Nov 2026 21:54

Kylian Mbappe became the first French player to score in seven consecutive Champions League appearances in Real Madrid's clash with PSV Eindhoven on Wednesday night.

An Ivan Perisic penalty sent PSV ahead at Bernabeu, but Real Madrid managed to turn the game around to record a 5-1 victory over the Dutch giants.

Federico Valverde levelled the scores in the 50th minute, before Jude Bellingham made it 2-1 to Jose Mourinho's side on the hour mark.

Mbappe then scored in the 64th minute to create history, becoming the first French player to net in seven successive fixtures in the Champions League.

The France international is also now one of just two players to have scored 75 Champions League goals before their 28th birthday, the other being Lionel Messi.

Mbappe was on the scoresheet once again in the 84th minute to make it 4-1 to Mourinho's team, before Vinicius Junior struck a fifth for the hosts late on.

Real Madrid's French attacker scored six goals and registered two assists in five Champions League appearances this season, while he now has 19 goals in 18 appearances for Real Madrid this term.

Real Madrid are currently the only team to boast a 100% record in this season's Champions League from five games, sitting top of the table on 15 points.

Meanwhile, Los Blancos are now on a run of 10 straight wins in all competitions.

Real Madrid will aim to continue their excellent form when they resume their La Liga campaign against Alaves on November 28.

Los Blancos have three league matches to come, also taking on Real Sociedad and Athletic Bilbao, before their next Champions League fixture away to Arsenal on December 9.

Arsenal vs Borussia Dortmund latest updates

Here was Arsenal’s very own Groundhog Day. Again.

Mikel Arteta would have feared what was coming as the misses piled up and his team found increasingly remarkable ways to not score.

How did Matt Verri rate the Arsenal players?

#1695. Aston Villa news: Unai Emery issues frank Alejandro Garnacho response after Galatasaray defeat

By Darren Plant | 24 Nov 2026 22:55

Unai Emery has suggested that Alejandro Garnacho is far away from a first start for Aston Villa.

On Tuesday night, the Premier League outfit succumbed to a 1-0 defeat at the hands of Galatasaray in the Champions League.

Not only are Villa now outsiders to finish in the top eight of the league phase, they have now gone six matches without a win in all competitions.

When quizzed on the prolonged wait for Garnacho to make his first Villa start, Emery has often been encouraging towards the Chelsea loanee.

However, when asked about his absence from the squad in Turkey, Emery hinted that the winger is not in his plans.

Emery named 11 substitutes - with two goalkeepers - for the Galatasaray game, one fewer than he was permitted.

Questioned over Garnacho not being involved, he told reporters: "Today the players were here who I think are the best players to be here with us."

At his pre-match press conference, Emery stated that everyone was available, apart from Matty Cash, Matteo Ruggeri, Amadou Onana and the ineligible Brian Madjo.

Emery has been facing suggestions that Garnacho has been discarded from his plans in the same fashion as Liverpool loanee Harvey Elliott in 2025-26 since September.

He seemingly spoke sincerely when saying that Garnacho had made a positive impact during training and a friendly during the September international break.

However, he remains with just 64 minutes across four substitute appearances since September 5. Although the appearances required for a permanent transfer from Chelsea has never been confirmed, the assumption is that it is 10 matches.

Garnacho is on seven outings, and there is now little to no realistic prospect of Emery choosing to activate a clause that would require Villa to pay approximately £43m for his signature.

As much as Villa's hierarchy and fans back Emery, questions need to be asked how two loanees who are known to have buy clauses in their respective agreements have been frozen out so quickly.

Villa have agreed separate deals worth a combined total of £78m. Elliott and Garnacho have made just three starts - all for Elliott - between them.

#1694. Iordanescu named Watford’s new head coach

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Edward Iordanescu has been appointed as Watford's new head coach, three days after Alessio Dionisi was sacked.

Dionisi was only in charge for five months, with his sacking coming on the back of a run of seven defeats in 10 league games, culminating in a 4-0 loss to Sheffield United.

That result left Watford 20th in the Championship table, three points above the relegation zone, with Iordanescu becoming their sixth new boss in less than 18 months.

He is also the 25th manager since the Pozzo family took over the club in 2012.

"I am very proud and happy to be at this football club," Iordanescu told the club website.

"I can see the team is in a difficult moment, but I have already watched many of the games over the last few days, and I'm very confident about the future.

"I will put all my passion into my job, and I will demand the full commitment of everybody. It all starts with hard work – the rest will follow.

"I look forward to meeting the fans at the game [on Wednesday] and starting work."

Edward Iordănescu is our new Head Coach. Welcome, Edward. https://t.co/E0wum5RdDR https://t.co/6aC3X7Kd54

— Watford Football Club (@WatfordFC) November 25, 2026

Iordanescu's first game in charge of Watford will come against Derby County on Saturday, but he will be in the stands for Wednesday's clash with Blackburn Rovers.

This will be the 48-year-old's first job since leaving Legia Warsaw in October 2025, having led the side to the Polish Super Cup in July 2025.

Iordanescu also took charge of Romania for two and a half years, guiding them to the last 16 at Euro 2024 when they were beaten by the Netherlands.

#1693. Leny Yoro: Manchester United make Pro Ref decision amid Mauricio Pochettino red card rage

Manchester United are furious at referees’ chief Howard Webb’s support for the decision to send off Leny Yoro at Liverpool, despite the defender having his one-match suspension removed.

The French centre-back was dismissed after only eight minutes of United’s 4-0 defeat at Anfield on Sunday for fouling Reds striker Alexander Isak as he advanced towards goal, with referee Sam Barrott deciding Yoro had denied an obvious goalscoring opportunity.

United successfully appealed for wrongful dismissal and the suspension has now been removed, the Football Association has confirmed, meaning Yoro is free to play in the Premier League match against Brentford at Old Trafford on Saturday.

Liverpool scored their opening goal directly from the free-kick awarded for Yoro’s challenge.

One question raised was whether Isak had the ball sufficiently under control for this to count as denial of an obvious goalscoring opportunity. The Swede’s touch took the ball into the arms of United goalkeeper Senne Lammens.

Pro Ref’s chief refereeing officer Webb backed the decision to dismiss the 21-year-old, saying it was “certainly not clearly wrong”.

However, United boss Mauricio Pochettino vehemently disagreed and hit out at the lack of VAR intervention.

It is understood that the club are unhappy with Webb’s comments and plan to make their feelings known to Pro Ref.

Speaking at a press conference ahead of his team’s Champions League match against Sporting in Lisbon on Wednesday, the Argentinian said: “Very disappointed. My question always was the same, we can accept the referee can make a mistake because of the emotion of the game, sometimes the view or the position can affect that. But if we have VAR, what were they doing?

“Now, are we going to repeat the game? Are we going to have the possibility to play with similar tools – 11 v 11?

“We have an unbelievable car, but we need to have the level to drive, we need to drive in the best way. We love the technology, yes, and we accept the technology is there, but what are they doing? But it’s not only this mistake, it affects everything.

“No-one is talking about the [Dominik Szoboszlai’s] goal wasn’t legal, they should have disallowed the goal because [Bradley] Barcola was touching our wall. Maybe in the last two years the rules have changed while I was in America. Why didn’t they check it? It must be disallowed.”

Man Utd blow as Pochettino drops hint in Champions League squad

Man Utd star ‘opens door’ to January transfer after Pochettino arrival

Liverpool hit with double injury blow for Club Brugge travelling squad confirmed

Rediscover your adventurous side on an exotic getaway

Webb discussed the sending-off with former Liverpool and United striker Michael Owen in the latest edition of Match Officials: Mic’d Up, which aired on Tuesday evening but was recorded before the FA confirmed Yoro’s suspension had been removed.

“The reason we’re talking about it is the fourth consideration [in DOGSO decisions], that’s control or likelihood of keeping or gaining control of the ball,” Webb said.

“Isak’s got control of the ball, he’s got possession, he’s got the touch, he knocks it past Yoro. He’s moving at pace at that moment and a crowd comes in and knocks him down.

“There’s a question mark I guess around whether or not he would get onto that ball before Lammens. Now, in the moment, the referee looked at it and felt he would.

“The VAR checks to see whether that decision made on the field was clearly and obviously incorrect, and formed the opinion that it wasn’t.

“I think by and large, most people would see that as a correct decision, with Isak moving quickly on towards that ball. The alternative view is that Lammens might get there first, but I think it’s a little bit debatable. (It’s) certainly not clearly wrong.”

VAR John Brooks was of the same opinion as he said in the audio between him and referee Barrott: “Let’s roll it through firstly to see whether the attacker is going to get on the end of the ball.

“Just roll through real speed. So, at full speed, Isak maintains his momentum and likely gets on the end of it.

“OK, certainly not clearly wrong that he doesn’t. So I think the DOGSO confirmed.”

Between Donnarumma and Kessie it was actually Kessie that lied and went behind the fans back, not Gigio. Neither one of them should be booed.

Kessie did none of those things. Initially Kessie did want to come back and would have, but the M & M boys did what they did with everybody which was make an initial low ball offer, drag the negotiations out for months until either the player gets fed up or some other club like Barcelona swoops in and makes a better offer. They could have and should have locked him up earlier. It’s a mistake they repeated with multiple players.

“They have to rest assured. I always keep my word, they should know me. Now I am here in Tokyo to get something important with my country, but as soon as the Olympics is over I return to Milan and we fix everything. There will be no problems,” he said (via MilanNews).

“Did I hear from the club? Of course, we had a chat and we constantly text with Paolo Maldini and Frederic Massara, they know my thoughts perfectly.”

All that remains, therefore, is to wait for the signing, which will come soon, after he is done representing his country in Japan: “I want to go on as much as possible in the Olympic tournament. At the end, Milan will have me for as long as they want.”

I have no issues with any player making the best decision for their career. I don’t hold it against Kessie for leaving Milan. I also think that Maldini and Massara were unqualified to hold the positions they held. But, this interview is the reason why some fans think that Kessie lied. Gigio always said that the agent will take care of the contract situation. We knew that he wants a lot of money and will stay only if they give him what he wanted, juts like his previous renewal. Gigio didn’t lie to anyone.

Yes, I know Kessie made those statements, but if you look at the initial offer M &M made it was actually insulting for a player as important as Kessie. They raised the offer a couple times after months went by but I believe if they made the final offer initiallly, that he would have signed. There aren’t many players that would choose Milan over Barcelona currently or when he did. I don’t blame him at all.

For a dude that like to talk about revisionist history you sure do alot of revising. Your hate for Maldini, the last director to deliver us a a Scudetto – which burns you up on the inside, makes you fail to tell the entire story properly. You forgot to add, M&M couldn’t go past a certain wage budget..beyond 6m per season to be exact. It left us vulnerable in negotiations with players. Just like with Thuram…and it came back to haunt us, live in the derby. We couldn’t even pay Hakan 0.5m more to get it over the line because of the cap, even though he snaked us. But I digress. I believe the only times we went over budget was with rare exceptions…Donnaruma and I believe Ibra – where M&M once more had to beg for that exception. Also recall that everytime his agent met with M&M they met their demands to the point where they maxed out the wage budget but they kept moving the goal posts, pun intended, each subsequent meeting. M&M had to ask for an exception for him and I believe the last offer was 6m with 0.5m bonus breaking the cap, net or around 10m gross. That’s easy to beat for teams like Barca who eventually offer somewhere around 13-14m for a player to warm the bench. There’s no way to compete with that, regardless. We had a top 5 defensive mid in the whole of Europe, what exactly do you think would happen with a wage budget under 6m courtesy Elliott?? M&M didn’t control the caps, those were the parameters they had to work under – which makes the Scudetto they won even more glorious. Go offer that, in their last contract year, to Mike and Pulisic who are on 7m with bonuses and 6.5m rising to 10m with bonuses respectively and see if they’ll sign for 6m or lower.

Spectacular way to ruin your career. No respect for players heading to Arabia under 35.

#1691. Cool Palmer has turned into Complaining Cole... his sulking as his club lurches into crisis doesn't say a lot for Chelsea's cultural reset, writes KIERAN GILL

Published: 01:47 EST, 22 November 2026 | Updated: 04:11 EST, 22 November 2026

We do not know why Cole Palmer headed for the tunnel in a huff after full-time while others in the same Chelsea side paraded the pitch to thank those supporters who had stayed to the end.

Perhaps he was frustrated with himself after a performance in which he did not score, assist, or even test James Trafford in Leeds United’s goal. Maybe he did not fancy thanking those who had been booing as Chelsea trailed 4-1. It is possible he simply does not like losing.

Most superstars can feel the same, and they can show their stroppy side when the game is not going their way.

An extreme example is Bruno Fernandes. Manchester United fans have long accepted his reputation as the Premier League’s temperamental nonpareil because of the numbers he can produce with the whingeing, albeit not so much this season during their downturn.

Such names can get away with petulance when their performances are proper, though Palmer has no such justification currently. The 24-year-old Englishman, unfortunately for Chelsea, put up another anonymous 90 minutes.

We could see he was frustrated even while on the pitch towards the end, with the way he was performatively kicking passes backwards as if to tell everyone else he had no other option. We have seen that before when Chelsea are losing, and it can be somewhat unhelpful when the pressure is being piled on the manager. It indicates the tactical set-up is not to his liking.

Cole Palmer and Joao Pedro were involved in a frosty exchange following Chelsea's 4-1 home defeat by Leeds. Source: Instagram/farihaxchels

As the biggest name within this Chelsea team and a player whose profile transcends his team-mates’, like it or not, he is the totem when it is all going wrong.

We wax lyrical when he is at his brilliant best. It can be as if there has been an explosion at a praise factory when he is dropping that shoulder to down a helpless defender. We know how terrifically talented he is. He is still compared to that 2023-24 season when his statistics were, in a wonderful way, stupid.

But when he is not performing, so too does he need to take the medicine of disapproval, which came in the form of a chorus of boos aimed at all those in Chelsea shirts at Stamford Bridge.

Leeds had not won at this ground since 1999. They corrected history, then Complaining Cole showed up at full-time.

His reaction did not speak to the cultural reset which Chelsea hoped they had orchestrated in the summer when they finally signed some experience for the changing room, bringing in Danny Welbeck, the 35-year-old whom Palmer has nominated as their new ‘Unc’ after Tosin Adarabioyo’s departure, and Jordan Henderson, 36.

It was a poor show from someone who, in his fourth season at a club that gave him his chance when spending £42.5million to sign him from Manchester City in 2023, should be seen as a leader by now.

Palmer is, probably, still undroppable. Alonso would create an almighty problem for himself if he suddenly relegated his No10 to the substitutes’ bench when playing Nottingham Forest next week. But he is in danger of such conversations cropping up at a time when he should want to be impressing enough to get back into Thomas Tuchel’s England squad at the next opportunity.

We are told both Palmer and Levi Colwill are desperate to represent their country again, but neither are performing to that standard of late. Colwill is a defender devoid of confidence, questioning himself and making mistakes. There was one moment during this demoralising defeat by Leeds when he booted a long ball straight out of play and reprimanded himself for it.

Colwill is perfectly capable of playing a good game. You do not have multiple clubs including Bayern Munich making enquiries with Chelsea without being considered elite. He is in a bad spell, and can come back from it, just like Palmer.

Inevitably, the response of some on social media was to say that Alonso’s time should be up.

For clarity, he is not under threat of suddenly being sacked by those at the top of Chelsea. He is 11 Premier League games into his career, and, clearly, deserves time.

The tactics are on him, absolutely. But he is also dealing with a few issues outside of his control, such as holes in his squad and injuries inflicted, like his highly-influential vice captain Moises Caicedo having to be substituted after 22 minutes in this match.

Xabi Alonso has made errors but was rightly considered a huge coup when Chelsea landed him

When appointed head coach of Bayer Leverkusen in October 2022, they went through patches in the Bundesliga. First, they beat Schalke 4-0, which was good. Then they failed to win any of their next three fixtures, which was bad.

Then they won five in a row – happy days. Then they won only one of their following five – bad days. Then they won five in a row again – perfect. Then they won only one of their next seven – pitiful.

But the following season, Leverkusen won the Bundesliga without losing a single game. Alonso was considered an almighty coup when secured in the summer. A little patience is deserved from my perspective, even if Chelsea are currently in a dismal spell.

It is hard not to think Malo Gusto’s time at Chelsea is almost at an end.

He was priced out of a move in the summer when the club asked for £75million, with Liverpool, Manchester City and others across Europe indicating their interest in that window.

Malo Gusto cut a lonely figure after being beaten for Leeds's fourth goal

But the 23-year-old Frenchman has shown little worth as the season has progressed.

Gusto started in five of Alonso’s first six games in all competitions at the beginning of the campaign.

Since then, he has been handed one start in eight, and that was in the Carabao Cup at Liverpool. Coming on as a substitute in this loss to Leeds, he tried and failed to play Brenden Aaronson offside and was then beaten by his man as the visitors made it 4-1.

We should expect to hear more on Gusto’s situation as January approaches.

#1690. Why Mikel Arteta must eradicate familiar Arsenal habit after Champions League frustration

Your weekly briefing on Arsenal, featuring team news and expert analysis from Matt Verri

Here was Arsenal’s very own Groundhog Day.

Mikel Arteta would have feared what was coming as the misses piled up and his team found increasingly remarkable ways to not score.

Gyokeres nets stunner as Arsenal held by Dortmund in thriller

Arsenal vs Borussia Dortmund LIVE: Latest score and updates Champions League

Man Utd make Pro Ref decision amid Pochettino red card rage

Rediscover your adventurous side on an exotic getaway

It was rinse and repeat from an Arsenal perspective. Completely dominate the opening 45 minutes with some sublime football. Take the lead but then fail to kick on. Drop the intensity in the second half and regret those missed opportunities.

That happened against Slavia Prague, when the Gunners just about held on in the second half to win. It happened on Saturday, when they had to come from behind just to draw a match they should have been three or four goals up in.

And it happened here, in perhaps the most ridiculous way yet. With some better decision-making in the final third, the Premier League champions might have put six past Dortmund.

Instead, from their 30 shots, Arsenal managed just four shots on target and one goal. The visitors rode their luck but they stayed within touch and when their moment came, Maximilian Beier took it with the kind of ruthlessness Arteta can only dream of.

It is unrealistic to expect the north Londoners to dominate a match for the full 90 minutes, even more so against Dortmund than the likes of Slavia Prague and Newcastle.

The problem is Arsenal’s lack of efficiency when they are on top means they cannot afford even the slightest drop in standards or intensity.

Score the two or three goals that the dominance deserves in the first half and a dip after the break will not be so decisive. As it is, with Arsenal leaving the margins so thin, one moment is all it takes for the hard work to be undone.

At St James’ Park, that moment was Odegaard mis-kicking a clearance. Here, it was Joane Gadou charging away from Christos Tzolis and nobody in the home midfield coming across to cover.

The match should have been done by then. Again, Arsenal were sensational in the first 45 minutes.

Noni Madueke, a constant threat, could not sort his feet out quickly enough when a rebound fell to him. The winger was then completely open, screaming for the ball shortly after when Declan Rice instead went by himself and had his shot deflected wide.

Counters were wasted. Viktor Gyokeres, who opened the scoring with a superb strike from distance, suddenly could not hit the target. When Arsenal went in only 1-0 up, what followed next was as predictable as it was galling for the Gunners.

The level dropped just slightly and the Bundesliga leaders came back into the game, equalising ten minutes after the restart.

Even then, though, Arsenal should have been able to recover. Unlike against Slavia Prague or Newcastle, Arsenal did not fall away for an extended period. This match was there for them to win and the chances came thick and fast.

Gyokeres headed wide from a few yards out. The Arsenal fans spent almost the entire final half an hour screaming at the players to shoot as extra touches were taken around the area.

When Serhou Guirassy then bounced the ball off his body onto his own post not once but twice, Arteta collapsed to the ground in disbelief.

The winner would not come. A top-two finish, which was so important in last season’s run to the final, has now become much harder.

But that is what this side keep doing. They seem determined to make things hard for himself. Another match that should have been won inside an hour turned into a 90-minute slugfest.

With Arsenal hoping this is another long season domestically and in Europe, it is a habit they must shake fast.

#1689. Brest vs Paris FC - prediction, team news, lineups

By Joel Lefevre | 24 Nov 2026 23:33

In a matchup featuring two of Ligue 1's biggest surprise stories at the moment, Brest will welcome Paris FC to Stade Francis-Le Ble on Friday.

A 1-0 win at Strasbourg on matchday 11 lifted the Brittany side to sixth in the Ligue 1 table, five points behind Paris, who are second after a convincing 4-0 triumph over Angers.

It appears as though Julien Lachuer has finally figured out the right buttons to push to help Brest find some consistency domestically.

This team entered November having dropped points in four of their last five league fixtures, but they will boast a 100% record this month should they triumph on Friday.

Brest can also win at least four domestic affairs in a row for the first time in a single league season since 2023-24 when they claimed six consecutive victories in this competition.

With a win on matchday 12, they would temporarily move into third place in Ligue 1 and that final Champions League spot above Lille on goal difference.

A team that gave up at least one goal in each of their first eight matches in this competition have not conceded in their last three such games.

After 11 matchdays, Les Pirates are third in Ligue 1 regarding expected goals but also rank third in big chances missed (23).

Liam Rosenior must be happy to be back in France, managing in a league where he has found tremendous success as a head coach.

The man who guided Strasbourg to a place in the Conference League has transformed Paris FC into title contenders, with his side just three points below Paris Saint-Germain heading into this match.

A victory by three or more goals on Friday would temporarily put them in first place and extend their winning run in this competition to four matches.

Right now, Paris FC are averaging 2.09 points per match in this competition, which is 0.80 more than a season ago, the biggest such increase among Ligue 1 clubs over that span.

They boast the lowest expected goals conceded in the league (10.2) and are one of three teams in the top flight that have not allowed a set-piece goal so far, with PSG and Lens being the others.

Paris FC can earn a third successive Ligue 1 triumph versus Brest on Friday, beating them 2-1 in their last visit to Stade Francis-Le Ble a season ago.

A calf strain may keep Brendan Chardonnet out of the Brest fold on Friday, while Kenny Lala is questionable with a knock and Kamory Doumbia is also doubtful with an ankle injury.

Noah Edjouma netted his third of the competition last week, while Egil Selvik stopped five shots to collect his third successive clean sheet in Ligue 1.

Meanwhile, for Paris FC, Nhoa Sangui may miss another match because of a hamstring issue which he has struggled to recover from.

Patrick Zabi, Luca Koleosho, Maxime Lopez and Diego Coppola all found the back of the net on matchday 11, with each strike coming in the second half.

Selvik; Zogbe, Tousart, Lloris, Locko; Chotard, Magnetti; Edjouma, Nonge, Mboup; Ajorque

Trapp; Matondo, Chergui, Coppola, Otavio; Lopez, Lees-Melou; Kebbal, Zabi, Pagis; Koleosho

While Brest are trending in the right direction, Paris FC have shown more consistency all season, and we believe their overall balance will see them collect maximum points once again.

#1688. ‘Mismatch’: Jobe Bellingham reveals Arsenal weakness that Borussia Dortmund exploited

Your weekly briefing on Arsenal, featuring team news and expert analysis from Matt Verri

Jobe Bellingham has revealed an Arsenal weakness that he and Borussia Dortmund looked to exploit in their Champions League encounter.

The Bundesliga leaders left the Emirates Stadium with a share of the spoils after Maximilian Beier’s equaliser cancelled out Viktor Gyokeres’ stunning opener in the first half.

The Gunners had plenty of chances to kill the game off and secure all three points, but Declan Rice hit the post, Noni Madueke went close a number of times and Gyokeres missed a gilt-edged opportunity from close range as they were forced to settle for a stalemate.

Post-match, Bellingham, fresh off his maiden senior England call-up, said that there had been a “mismatch” that he was instructed to take advantage of in midfield.

“One of the coaches pointed out to me that I was against Myles [Lewis-Skelly],” he explained on Amazon Prime Video.

“For the long ball - I don’t want to say a mismatch - but I’m obviously bigger.

“You would expect that if I was against Gabriel or Ezri [Konsa] it would be a bit more difficult to win the long balls. I thought that there was a bit of an advantage there in terms of height. I managed to win a few flick-ons and get us up the pitch.

“We varied it well, we played short, and we retained possession and defended a lot better in transitions.”

Jobe, the younger brother of Real Madrid star Jude, was unfortunate not to hit the winner as he followed in Julian Ryerson’s saved shot, which Kepa Arrizabalaga spilled.

The midfielder was alive to tuck away the rebound, only to be flagged for offside to deny him a first goal of the season.

“Gutted,” the 21-year-old continued, “A bit unlucky at the minute. It would have been nice if it was today, back in England.”

#1687. Arsenal told penalty verdict as Viktor Gyokeres ‘gets away’ with Borussia Dortmund controversy

Your weekly briefing on Arsenal, featuring team news and expert analysis from Matt Verri

Arsenal were fortunate not to concede a penalty against Borussia Dortmund during their Champions League draw.

The Premier League champions and Bundesliga leaders held each other to a 1-1 stalemate at the Emirates Stadium, as Viktor Gyokeres’ rifled opener was cancelled out in the second half by Maximilian Beier.

It was the Gunners’ second draw on the spin after a 2-2 encounter at St James’ Park, where Noni Madueke rescued a point against Newcastle after Malick Thiaw and Harvey Barnes had put the Magpies ahead following Eberechi Eze’s opening goal.

But it was the goalscorer Gyokeres who almost turned from hero to villain, as he allegedly handled a Dortmund corner in the second period.

It led Amazon Prime Video pundits Alan Shearer and Mark Clattenberg to question referee Maurizio Mariani’s decision not to award a spot kick to the visitors.

“I think Arsenal were fortunate to have gotten away with that one,” Shearer said on co-commentary.

"I know it might have been Fabio Silva in front of him trying to flick it on, but he didn't, and his arm is actually out."

Clattenberg, said alongside the record Premier League goalscorer in the north London gantry, concurred.

"We all know UEFA have a stricter handball rule than we see in the Premier League, but what doesn't save Gyokeres in this situation is, the ball comes in from a distance and he makes a little movement of his arm towards the ball so that makes it look more like a penalty kick for me,” the former official said.

Former Arsenal forward Theo Walcott spoke of his relief at the penalty not being given.

"As soon as it hit his hand, straight away my heart is in my mouth, I think it's a penalty," he said.

"I think he's got away with that. I'm pleased it wasn't given because it's not a penalty, but in Europe it probably should be."

Gyokeres asserted his innocence in his post-match interview.

"I think the arm was towards my body," the Swede said.

"I don't think it was outside, so I don't think it was anything."

#1686. Xhaka and Brobbey improving but unavailable for clash with Jagiellonia

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Regis Le Bris confirmed both Granit Xhaka and Brian Brobbey will miss Sunderland's Europa League clash with Jagiellonia Bialystok, but said the pair would be back soon.

Sunderland welcome Jagiellonia to the Stadium of Light on Thursday as they aim to build on positive results against Chelsea and Aston Villa either side of the international break.

The Black Cats have picked up more points in their last four Premier League games (five – W1 D2 L1) than they had in their first seven this season (four – W1 D1 L5).

But they have been missing captain Xhaka, who sustained a calf injury against Chelsea, while Brobbey has been suffering with a problem in his thigh over the last few weeks.

Speaking to reporters on Wednesday, Le Bris ruled out Xhaka and Brobbey of their upcoming European match, while saying it was unlikely they would feature against Tottenham this weekend in the Premier League.

Le Bris' side travel to Anfield to face Liverpool next week before turning their attention to the Tyne-Wear derby against rivals Newcastle United on December 6.

"They are doing well, both are in a better place and are being assessed weekly," Le Bris told reporters.

"They want to play, but we need to take care of them because the season will be long. So they won't be available for this week, but we will see after [this week]."

Checking in for Europa League prep https://t.co/vNDdJFXglL

— Sunderland AFC (@SunderlandAFC) November 25, 2026

With Dan Ballard also missing with a hamstring injury, Sunderland are missing the spine of their team.

However, Le Bris insisted that dealing with injury setbacks and problems comes with the territory of competing on so many fronts.

"It's part of the process. We know in a season you won't have your main XI if it is always available, so you need depth, and with this club, we've shown we can build something new with young lads or players from abroad, and they are doing well," Le Bris added.

"Jules [Ahoka] is a great example, coming from nowhere and able to play against Chelsea and Villa."

Sunderland have already faced Polish opposition in the Europa League this season, drawing 1-1 with Lech Poznan. They are the first English club to face two Polish clubs in one major European season, and will want to bounce back from their defeat to Dinamo Zagreb last time out.

But their problems in the competition in 2026-27 have been in front of goal. No side has had more shots in the Europa League this season than Sunderland (84), though the Black Cats have the fifth-worst shot conversion rate (4.8%) and have underperformed their expected goals (xG) by more than any other side (four goals from 9.49 xG).

Jagiellonia have, however, lost their last two Europa League matches, both without scoring. They have never lost three major European games in a row, nor have they failed to score in three in a row.

#1685. Rabiot grateful for Amorim’s trust and offers insight into renewal plea: “Makes us feel important”

Speaking to French TV, Adrien Rabiot has looked at the interest from Ruben Amorim in a renewal at AC Milan and praised the Portuguese.

It’s no secret that Rabiot is one of Milan’s most important players. Gerry Cardinale admitted that he’s something of a ‘franchise player’ already and the love from Amorim has not been kept quiet. Indeed, the former Manchester United head coach is a huge admirer of his.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

After a summer of questions about his future, a renewal has seemed to be on the cards for the majority of the season and with continued good performances, the talk of one coming soon won’t go away. In fact, it could be completed before Christmas, with a deal reportedly close.

Speaking to Telefoot during the international break, Rabiot revealed a little more about his renewal and Amorim’s dream to offer him a new deal quickly into his tenure, as MilanNews have relayed.

“My excellent start to the season with good stats? It’s also positive to have players capable of being decisive without being attackers. It also encourages those around us. At Milan we have quite young players and it’s important for them to have role models in their everyday lives.

Your weekly briefing on Arsenal, featuring team news and expert analysis from Matt Verri

Mikel Arteta provided a coy update on David Raya’s availability for Arsenal’s showdown with Manchester City this weekend.

The goalkeeper missed the Gunners’ draw with Borussia Dortmund on Tuesday night with a shoulder injury that he picked up against Newcastle.

The Spaniard left the pitch at St James’ Park in significant pain and Arsenal feared a lengthy absence, but scans proved to be positive.

The No1 has avoided a serious injury and he will not require surgery, though there is uncertainty over exactly when he will return.

There are suggestions that the goalkeeper will only be out for a matter of days and could be in contention to face City on Sunday.

“No, we have nothing to add today unfortunately,” Arteta said after his side’s 1-1 draw with Dortmund.

“We need to know first how bad it is and whether he has a chance or not [to face Man City].”

In Raya’s absence, Kepa Arrizabalaga started against Dortmund, as Arsenal had to settle for just a point despite a dominant performance.

The Spaniard was fairly comfortable throughout, though he did have some shaky moments from corners and when rolling the ball out to Myles Lewis-Skelly to play him into trouble.

However, it was an improvement on Kepa’s display in the Carabao Cup final last season and solid enough to be confident he will keep his place over Illan Meslier while Raya remains out.

Kepa has had limited football since joining the club, so trusted has Raya become for Arsenal, but Arteta insisted he will have full faith in the goalkeeper if he is required to start in goal against City.

“Him and Illan, they’re both in the same situation,” Arteta said.

“I think Kepa had a really good performance today. We fully trust our keepers and if he needs to play against City, he will play.”

#1680. Morocco FA confirm appeal plans after Senegal awarded AFCON 2025 title

The Moroccan FA say they plan to explore all legal avenues to appeal after expressing their “protest” against the CAS ruling to reinstate Senegal as 2025 Africa Cup of Nations winners.

While Senegal won 1-0 against Morocco in the final of AFCON 2025, the match was beset by controversy. Senegal players and staff left the pitch in the 98th minute in protest against the award of a penalty for the hosts, which left the game paused for 14 minutes. The match eventually resumed, Brahim Diaz missed the spot kick and the game went to extra time, which saw Senegal score and go on to lift the trophy.

But African football governing body CAF retrospectively awarded the title to Morocco two months after the final, stating that Senegal’s conduct during the match had disqualified them as winners. Morocco were named automatic 3-0 winners.

The Senegalese FA took an appeal to the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) which, after a months-long saga, reinstated Senegal as champions on Tuesday.

But Morocco have not given up, citing reports of an alleged telephone conversation between CAS panelist Ulrich Haas and the president of Senegal’s football federation hours before Tuesday’s ruling as one reason they have grounds for an appeal.

The CAS ruling said: “The Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) upheld the appeal by the Senegalese Football Federation (FSF) against the Confederation of African Football (CAF) and the Royal Moroccan Football Federation (FRMF, in French) concerning the final of the Africa Cup of Nations Morocco 2025 (AFCON 2025). The decision rendered by the CAF Appeal Board is set aside and the decision by the CAF Disciplinary Board is reinstated.

“Consequently, the result obtained at the end of the AFCON 2025 final is confirmed (1-0 for Senegal).

“By blowing his whistle to restart play, the referee considered that the conditions for resuming the match had been met – both teams were on the pitch again, and both expressed their willingness to resume.

“In the Panel’s view, there is no doubt that the effects of the Referee’s decision were limited to the pitch. As such, the Panel considers that the Referee’s decision was covered by the "field of play" doctrine.

“Since Articles 82 and 84 of the AFCON Regulations are intended solely to determine the outcome of a match when a team’s conduct leads the referee to call off the game permanently, they are therefore not applicable in this case.”

But Morocco have vowed to appeal CAS’s ruling.

A statement from the Moroccan FA stated: “We take note of the decision of the Court of Arbitration for Sport regarding the appeal filed by the Senegalese Football Federation against the decision of the CAF Appeals Committee, relating to the final match of the 2025 Africa Cup of Nations. In this context, the Royal Moroccan Football Federation expresses its surprise and protest at the failure to take into account its demand to arrange the necessary legal consequences for practices that would compromise the integrity and credibility of the arbitration procedure, especially what has been confirmed regarding communication between the German referee Ulrich Haas (who sat on the CAS panel) and the president of the Senegalese Football Federation, 48 hours before the decision was issued.

“The Royal Moroccan Football Federation also notes that the decision did not take into account the approach recently adopted by both the International Football Association Board (IFAB) and FIFA, regarding players leaving the field of play without the referee’s permission, and the resulting disciplinary responsibilities and penalties.

“Accordingly, the Royal Moroccan Football Federation confirms its intention to pursue all available legal avenues to appeal the decision of the Court of Arbitration for Sport.”

#1679. Brentford transfer news: Bees among three Premier League clubs keen on '£33m-rated' Serie A star

By Ben Sully | 25 Nov 2026 00:26, Last updated: 25 Nov 2026 02:43

Brentford are reportedly among three Premier League clubs interested in signing Lazio midfielder Kenneth Taylor.

The Bees splashed out around £41m to recruit midfielder Mamadou Sangare from Lens in the summer in a club-record transfer.

Sangare has featured in all 11 of Brentford's Premier League games, but he has not always been a guaranteed starter due to the competition from Vitaly Janelt and Yehor Yarmoliuk.

Mathias Jensen is also available to Brentford boss Keith Andrews, who currently has plenty of options at his disposal in central midfield.

However, Jensen is out of contract at the end of the season, and the uncertainty surrounding his future may be one of the factors behind Brentford's apparent interest in Taylor.

According to TuttoMercatoWeb, the Bees are one of three Premier League clubs that are keeping tabs on the Dutchman's performances at Lazio.

Bournemouth and Newcastle United are also showing a keen interest as they scour the market for potential midfield recruits.

The Cherries are believed to view Taylor as a potential replacement for Alex Scott, who continues to draw interest from some of the Premier League's biggest clubs.

Meanwhile, Newcastle appear to be still open to bolstering a midfield that lost the services of Bruno Guimaraes and Sandro Tonali at the end of last season, despite recruiting Nico Gonzalez and Aladji Bamba in the summer window.

Taylor has played regularly since joining Lazio from Ajax in January, contributing five goals and five assists in 34 competitive appearances.

In fact, he has registered two goals and three assists in 12 league matches this term, helping Gennaro Gattuso's side establish a two-point lead at the top of Serie A.

With Taylor under contract until June 2030, there is a belief his potential suitors will have to offer around €40m (£33m) to have any hope of prising him away from Lazio.

However, a January departure seems unlikely at this stage, with Gattuso keen to keep one of his key players for the club's title battle.

Brentford, Bournemouth and Newcastle will also have to be wary of rival interest from Juventus, who view him as the 'ideal' midfield target.

#1678. Manchester United want Nathan Collins

According to talkSPORT, Manchester United have identified Brentford’s Nathan Collins as a January transfer target as the club looks to strengthen its defence following a difficult start to the season.

United’s plans for a defensive rebuild were initially expected to begin next summer, but ongoing problems at the back are forcing the club to act sooner. As a result, Collins has emerged as one of the key names being considered ahead of the winter transfer window.

New United boss Mauricio Pochettino wants to add both a centre-back and a striker during the winter transfer window. The club’s recruitment staff are reportedly focusing on experienced Premier League players with leadership qualities, and Collins is viewed as fitting that profile.

However, any move for the 25-year-old Ireland international is expected to be complicated by the fact that the defender remains under contract with Brentford until 2029, which obviously puts the Bees in a strong negotiating position.

#1676. ‘I want to see’: Thierry Henry makes Arsenal vs Man City prediction

Your weekly briefing on Arsenal, featuring team news and expert analysis from Matt Verri

Thierry Henry believes Arsenal can end Manchester City’s title hopes this weekend.

Mikel Arteta’s table-topping champions take on Enzo Maresca’s struggling contenders on Sunday, November 29, with six points currently separating the two sides.

As such, victory for Arsenal would extend the margin between the Gunners and City to nine points after 12 games.

Henry is predicting his former side to “dominate” City, despite a stuttering return to action, with draws with Newcastle and Borussia Dortmund, since returning from the international break.

He told CBS Sports: “You have two teams who have to rectify two things at the weekend. Arsenal, like we’ve been saying recently, and Mikel Arteta has been saying, when you’re on top of a team, don’t let them come back to attack like we’ve seen in the last two games.

"If you go back to City, and I’ve said it since the beginning of the season, the balance of the team isn’t right. Simple as that.

"They have quality, they have goalscorers who will bail them out, Rayan Cherki bailed them out [against Napoli] but the cohesion of the team, the way they don’t stop counters, they don't control the game on and off the ball like they used to.

"That didn't stop them losing games under Pep [Guardiola] but they were more in control of games.

"You have two teams who have been dominating the league in the last two, three years. But I want to see an Arsenal team that's going to dominate City, and they are there to be dominated.

"But on the other side, it might be the day that City wake up. But if they play the same way they’ve been playing recently, being open and all over the place in midfield, it could be a long day."

Jamie Carragher agreed with his CBS Sports colleague, adding: "I think Arsenal will win. I can’t see City getting anything from that game.

"They’ve been really poor of late, the results have shown that, not strong defensively at all.

"And that's not because Arsenal are amazing. Listen, they are a top team, don’t get me wrong, but in terms of the Champions League, I don’t think the Premier League teams can match… only Arsenal can really match what we’re seeing from the top teams.”

Carragher went on to argue that Arsenal’s proven strength in the Champions League automatically made the Gunners favourites for a second Premier League crown in two years.
