#1675. Doncaster Rovers vs Huddersfield Town - prediction, team news, lineups

By Sam Varley | 25 Nov 2026 01:26

Doncaster Rovers will welcome Huddersfield Town to Club Doncaster Sports Village on Thursday for a Yorkshire Derby with importance at both ends of the League One table.

The visitors fell off the summit of the division following a defeat at the weekend, while their hosts drew on Saturday and only lead the relegation zone on goal difference.

Doncaster Rovers head back into action on Thursday aiming to move clear of the relegation zone at the beginning of the League One weekend, having endured a difficult start to the campaign.

In their second season back in the third tier after promotion from League Two and a 14th-placed finish last time around, the Yorkshire outfit currently find themselves 20th having managed just 13 points from their first 14 outings, losing seven and winning just three of those.

Indeed, their last six outings have produced just four points, as Grant McCann's side broke up four defeats with a 2-0 home victory over Sheffield Wednesday, before falling to Luton Town and MK Dons away from home and experiencing mixed fortunes in a pair of cup ties against Rochdale and Kidderminster Harriers, losing to the latter in the FA Cup first round.

A trip to Yorkshire rivals Bradford City followed on Saturday, and the Rovers were at least able to bounce back from consecutive league defeats, twice falling behind and levelling through Jordan Thomas in the 78th minute and Sean Grehan deep into injury time to leave with a creditable point from a 2-2 draw.

Still only leading the bottom four on goal difference, Doncaster Rovers will now aim to bounce back to winning ways to put themselves three points above the drop zone before the rest of the weekend's action.

They face a tough test, though, as the visitors arrive in search of a rebound of their own to return to the top of the table.

Beginning their third straight season in League One and their first full one under the management of Martin Drury with the hopes of battling for promotion back to the second tier, Huddersfield Town have enjoyed a strong start as they headed into the November international break in top spot on 29 points from 14 games.

The Terriers won eight and only lost one of those while scoring 28 goals and conceding just 12, having headed into that break in a seven-game league unbeaten run in which they won four in a row before drawing against fellow promotion-chasers Luton Town in early November.

Then following a brief international break and a pair of cup outings against Exeter City and Liverpool Under-21s, Drury's side returned at home to Leicester City on Saturday but fell to just a second loss of the season in the third tier as Louis Page scored the only goal of the game for the visitors early in the second half.

That saw Huddersfield Town fall three points behind new leaders Stockport County, albeit with a game in hand, but only ahead of third-placed Oxford United having played a game more, and they will hope to quickly put things right and retake their place at the summit with a Yorkshire derby win on Thursday.

Doncaster Rovers form (all competitions):

Huddersfield Town form (all competitions):

Doncaster Rovers remain without James Husband, Tommi O'Reilly and Francis Okoronkwo due to ongoing injuries, while Harry Clifton and Will Keane missed the game against Bradford and will likely remain sidelined too.

Brandon Hanlan led the line in that game and may continue to do so with Alfie May ineligible against his parent club, although James Collins is back in contention having made his Rovers league debut off the bench at the weekend following a long layoff.

Elsewhere, George Broadbent should again join Robbie Gotts and mainstay Owen Bailey in midfield.

Huddersfield Town are still without Murray Wallace, Jack Whatmough, David Kasumu, Herbie Kane and Marcus McGuane through injuries.

Drury should avoid making many changes despite the weekend's defeat, with Radinio Balker, Ibane Bowat and Sean Roughan having formed a strong back three in recent weeks and Cameron Humphreys and Archie Collins likely to continue their midfield partnership.

Joe Taylor and Derensili Sanches Fernandes have shone in attack, with the former scoring 10 goals in 14 league games and the latter notching up seven goals and six assists in 15.

Doncaster Rovers possible starting lineup:

Simkin; Nixon, Grehan, Pearson, Senior; Broadbent, Gotts; Hutchinson, Bailey, Thomas; Hanlan

Huddersfield Town possible starting lineup:

Young; Bowat, Balker, Roughan; Bronkhorst, Collins, Humphreys, Mumba; Sanches Fernandes, Taylor, Radulovic

Huddersfield Town will hope their rare defeat at the weekend does not derail their promotion push, and despite the hosts taking a point from Bradford at the weekend, we back the Terriers to bounce back on Thursday and outclass Doncaster.

#1672. Bruno Fernandes reveals contract negotiations with Manchester United have stalled after he rejected a new deal in the summer

By KATE MCGREAVY, EXECUTIVE SPORTS EDITOR

Published: 04:01 EST, 22 November 2026 | Updated: 05:10 EST, 22 November 2026

Bruno Fernandes has revealed there are no ongoing contract negotiations with Manchester United after he rejected their proposed new deal.

The Manchester United captain's contract is set to expire in June 2027, which means that if the club and player fail to agree fresh terms, Fernandes will be free to discuss a summer move with clubs abroad as early as the January transfer window.

Fernandes has divided United fans during their dire season so far but new manager Mauricio Pochettino confirmed he will remain as captain in his first press conference on Friday.

It was widely known that discussions between Fernandes and Man United began over the summer, on the heels of a strong campaign which saw him named Men's PFA Player of the Year.

But Fernandes has now shed light on his future by admitting contract talks have stalled after the club put a deal on the table.

'No, there's no negotiations ongoing,' Fernandes told Sky Sports ahead of United's trip to Anfield this afternoon. 'But I've seen people saying that he's asked for more money, he's asked for more years. If I wanted more money I wouldn't be here.

Bruno Fernandes has revealed there are no ongoing contract negotiations with Man United

'I had somewhere to go to get much more money than being at Manchester United. I could have been in a place that is much warmer than Manchester. Two summers ago, three summers ago, last summer, I always had a chance to leave and I always chose to be here.

'The thing is I've always showed how much I care about the club and how much I want to win at this club.

'And I've always said the moment the club thinks is the time for me to move on, I will move on. I'm not going to be the player that I've seen many in this time at Man United they're going to stay here just by staying, just by finishing my contract and then we will see.

'In the moment the club says "Bruno, it's time to part ways", I'm going to be the first one walking out the door.

'Yeah the club offered me a new contract so I think that from their side shows that they want me to stay.

'As I said there are no negotiations going on. We spoke about the contract at the end of last season. We came in the beginning of the season speaking about the contract but about the context of the team and the club I just put that to a side because I don't think it's the right moment, neither for me, neither for the club to be talking about negotiations because the most important thing now is that the club gets back to winning games.'

The club may yet seek to trigger the 12-month extension in Fernandes' contract. Daily Mail Sport understands Galatasaray as well as AC Milan and Saudi are among those monitoring developments.

The Portuguese was linked with a big-money move to Saudi Arabia last year with Al-Hilal reportedly willing to offer a contract worth up to £200m to the midfielder, on top of a £100m transfer fee to United, but he chose to commit his future to the Red Devils.

United currently sit in the relegation zone after a 40-year worst-ever start to the season. Fernandes publicly questioned the former manager's tactics after his side's Champions League thrashing at the hands of Como, and has struggled to find form this season.

Fernandes was brought back into the fold after going through a brief period of being frozen out of Michael Carrick's squad following his incendiary comments following defeat in Italy last month.

Fernandes, who is usually very deliberate in what he says in the media, was scathing in his criticism of coaches after the Como debacle.

'It's a decision from the staff to not press man-to-man and sometimes leave a little space in behind and try to get the ball in the first moment, to wait for them, to give them the ball,' he said.

'But sometimes when you give too much the ball to these teams they get confident, they have so many bodies behind the ball that make you run a lot, make people get frustrated, and then obviously when you recover the ball the legs are, and the brain, much more difficult to make it work.'

His post-Como interview was widely condemned by fans and pundits alike, with Gary Neville lamenting: 'If that's your captain saying that, imagine what they're saying in the dressing room behind closed doors when no one's listening. That's horrific.'

He also told Fernandes to 'read the room' and accused him of being an 'excuse merchant' on his podcast.

Fernandes was left on the bench for Man United's next Premier League appointment, a loss to Bournemouth, before returning to the starting XI against Chelsea the following matchday.

After Man United's comeback win against Roma, Fernandes was defiant in his post-match remarks as he stressed that he had not been sanctioned for undermining Carrick with his initial interview.

'The club needed that win. The players needed that win. It is something we needed as a group of players and staff,' he said. 'We have been working so hard to get out of this situation together. It has been tough. There has been a lot of speculation in the media.

Mauricio Pochettino confirmed Fernandes will remain as captain in his first press conference

'A lot of lies around many things that have happened at this club, between me and the manager, like that we have cleared the air. Nothing like that happened.

'The manager took a decision of making myself on the bench because I wasn't performing. And that's fair.

'Everyone felt like that was a punishment for the words that I had [after Como]. And if it was, it was right.

'The manager makes the decisions. I have to accept it. I have to go forward with that. It doesn't change the belief I have in the manager, the staff and every player at this club.

'And it doesn't change my aim to win every f***ing game that I have ahead of me.'

Fernandes' comments were ultimately unable to keep Carrick in his job however, with the former club captain finally sacked on November 11 after an agonising three-day wait.

Man United's hierarchy, notably chief executive Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox, have come under fire from the fanbase and within the club for their treatment of the departing coach, with Carrick taking two days of training at Carrington as they mulled his sacking.

Wilcox and Berrada jetted to Monaco to meet with Ineos chief Sir Jim Ratcliffe and discuss the departure of Carrick, with the club's Glazer ownership ratifying the decision to replace him with United States national team coach Pochettino.

Pochettino swapped the USA for United on Wednesday and will take charge of his first match against bitter rivals Liverpool today.

#1671. Lewis-Potter commits future to Brentford with new long-term contract

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Brentford have announced that Keane Lewis-Potter has put pen to paper on a new five-and-a-half-year deal with the club.

Lewis-Potter, who scored twice in Brentford's 4-0 win over Everton on Monday, has agreed fresh terms that will keep him at the club until the summer of 2032.

The 25-year-old joined Brentford from Hull City in July 2022 and has gone on to make 144 appearances in all competitions, scoring 15 goals and providing 10 assists.

In 11 matches this season, Lewis-Potter (four) has already beaten his best-ever scoring season in the Premier League (three in 36 apps in 2025-26 and three in 30 in 2023-24).

Lewis-Potter also tops Brentford's ranks for chances created (14) in the Premier League in 2026-27.

"It's the way the club works. We don't just think about tomorrow; we think about next week, next year and the years after," Brentford boss Keith Andrews said.

"We're trying to make the club really secure, really solid and forward-thinking. Keane is another very good player that's just signed up for the long term, so that is really pleasing."

We’re delighted to announce that Keane Lewis-Potter has signed a new long-term contract with us The deal runs until the summer of 2032, with the club option of a further year Many congratulations, Keano https://t.co/3GJu1hEBsN https://t.co/aWrrogJJLJ

— Brentford FC (@BrentfordFC) November 25, 2026

Brentford enjoyed their joint-biggest home win in the Premier League against Everton, equalling their 4-0 thrashing of Manchester United in August 2022.

Lewis-Potter netted his second Premier League brace, with his first coming against Wolves in December 2025, with Vitaly Janelt and Fabio Carvalho also on target.

There were just 178 seconds between Lewis-Potter's two goals, making it the second-quickest Premier League brace for a Brentford player after Yoanne Wissa against Ipswich Town in November 2024 (137 seconds).

Since Andrews took charge of Brentford ahead of the 2025-26 season, of London clubs, only Arsenal (113) have won more Premier League points than the Bees (70).

Brentford and Lewis-Potter will be hoping to build on their win against Everton this Saturday, with a trip to Old Trafford to face Manchester United up next.

#1670. Arsenal injury update: David Raya, Martin Zubimendi, Bukayo Saka latest return dates

Your weekly briefing on Arsenal, featuring team news and expert analysis from Matt Verri

Arsenal are still sweating on the fitness of David Raya as they prepare for a crunch run of fixtures that begins with Sunday’s visit of Manchester City in the Premier League.

The Gunners were rocked by an injury to their influential first-choice goalkeeper during the latter stages of last weekend’s eventful 2-2 draw with Newcastle after he hurt his shoulder during an initially innocuous-looking collision with William Osula.

Raya sat out Tuesday’s lively home draw with Borussia Dortmund in the Champions League, with unconvincing deputy Kepa Arrizabalaga stepping in from the start ahead of No3 Illan Meslier.

Mikel Arteta will be desperate to have the reigning Golden Glove winner back for a crucial stretch of games that sees Arsenal also take on the likes of Tottenham, Real Madrid and Manchester United before Christmas.

With that massive showdown against title rivals City coming up at the Emirates Stadium, here is all the latest Arsenal injury news and return dates, with William Saliba now back and Max Dowman having served his suspension.

Raya was in considerable pain after colliding with Osula at St James’ Park and had to go off after receiving treatment, with his left arm placed in a protective sling before he was promptly sent for scans.

He was seen still wearing that sling while out in London the next day and was then absent from Arsenal’s open training session at London Colney on Monday morning.

Arteta said that he would definitely miss the Dortmund game, but soothed fan fears by stating that the injury was “not too serious” following “encouraging” test results and did not require surgery, raising hopes that he would be in a position to make a quick return against City.

A new update was expected following the draw with Dortmund, when Arteta was coy on if Raya would be involved at the weekend.

“No, we have nothing to add today unfortunately,” Arteta said. “We need to know first how bad it is and whether he has a chance or not [to face Man City].”

Quizzed on if Saka would be available for Manchester United’s visit to north London just before Christmas, the manager said: “I cannot be that specific. In four weeks’ time a lot of things can happen. Maybe it is three and then it is five.

“At the end, there are a few elements. One is the healing of that tissue – and we cannot predict exactly when that tissue is going to be in the best condition to push it.

“Then there is the rehab plan that we have now, what he needs to do in the gym, what he needs to do in terms of treatment and on the field.”

It was later revealed to be a hamstring complaint, which Arteta expects to keep him out for a period of weeks after he played no part against either Newcastle or Dortmund.

"He's out," Arteta said of Zubimendi last week. “Unfortunately he has a slight problem in his hamstring.

"He wasn't too concerned to be fair after the game, but after the MRI scans, it showed that there is an injury there and he's going to be out for a few weeks."

#1669. Jude Bellingham dismisses Ballon d'Or talk after scoring "best goal of my life" against PSV Eindhoven

By Seye Omidiora | 25 Nov 2026 01:48, Last updated: 25 Nov 2026 01:51

Real Madrid midfielder Jude Bellingham has brushed off Ballon d'Or talk after inspiring his side to a commanding 5-1 Champions League comeback victory over PSV Eindhoven.

The 23-year-old England international started Tuesday's league phase encounter at the Santiago Bernabeu on the bench as Jose Mourinho opted to manage his workload following recent fatigue.

With Los Blancos trailing 1-0 at the interval to an Ivan Perisic penalty, Mourinho summoned Bellingham at half-time and the substitute immediately transformed the contest.

After Federico Valverde restored parity five minutes into the second period, Bellingham put the hosts ahead on the hour mark with a sensational strike before later setting up Vinicius Junior's late fifth.

Bellingham's decisive go-ahead strike immediately drew comparisons to club icon Zinedine Zidane, whose famous number five shirt the Englishman wears in the Spanish capital.

Collecting the ball on the edge of the penalty area, the midfielder flicked it up with his first touch before slicing an audacious outside-of-the-boot volley inside the far post.

Speaking after the final whistle, Bellingham admitted the acrobatic effort stood above anything else he has produced in his career so far.

"I think this was the best goal of my life," Bellingham said, as reported by Fabrizio Romano.

@FabrizioRomano That was a prefect goal https://t.co/4j8kLOdUMX

Teammate Bernardo Silva echoed the widespread awe inside the stadium, describing the strike as "one of those moments when you just go, 'Wow!'"

Bellingham's dazzling second-half appearance prompted Mourinho to reiterate his belief that omitting the midfielder from the top 10 at this year's Ballon d'Or ceremony was jarring.

The Portuguese tactician also conceded that leaving his talisman out of the starting lineup had backfired, admitting he had mistakenly believed Madrid could win without him.

When pressed on the prestigious individual accolade afterwards, however, Bellingham made it clear that collective silverware remains his sole obsession.

"Ballon d'Or? I do not care," he declared. "It's for journalists, not for me. I want to win all titles with Real Madrid."

Having helped Los Blancos preserve their 100% start in the Champions League league phase, Bellingham will now look to carry his sparkling form back into La Liga action this weekend.

Mourinho's team are three points off Barcelona in the La Liga table ahead of their next match against Alaves.

#1666. Why Xabi Alonso’s vision and Chelsea’s reality remain worlds apart

Your weekly briefing on Chelsea, featuring team news and expert analysis from Dom Smith

Another chastening week in the unhinged world of Chelsea has shown Xabi Alonso that the thing he most craves is what his team lack more than anything.

Managers are neurotic creatures and Alonso’s great obsession is “control”, which you’d have to say is rather concerning from what we have seen of his tenure so far.

Ask the Spaniard to name his favourite performance from Chelsea’s opening 11 games of the Premier League season and he will cite last month’s 2-0 away win over Everton. A rare victory up north delivered a first top-flight clean sheet since January and, more importantly, was professional and diligent.

There is a time and a place for football as entertainment, but Alonso is in a results-based business and knows, from his unbeaten campaign leading Bayer Leverkusen to Bundesliga glory, that the less memorable wins are key to building a team in control of its destiny, delivering consistent results.

Chelsea are many things; they are not that.

The club were understandably excited in the summer when they secured their first-choice candidate, and appointing Alonso as manager, not head coach, has given the impression that he has more control in the overall running of first-team operations than his recent predecessors.

That is not translating to the pitch, though. Far from it. In every area of the field, control is absent without leave.

Four months in, Xabi Alonso is yet to imprint his identity on Chelsea

Joao Pedro’s thigh injury has left Chelsea hamstrung in attack. Cole Palmer looks lost and ineffectual; Morgan Rogers is left carrying an excessive burden.

The performances with and without another player, Moises Caicedo, are just as strikingly worlds apart from each other. An overreliance on the Ecuadorian has set alarm bells ringing for months.

The constant need for one midfielder to fill in alongside the centre-backs leaves Chelsea brutally outnumbered in the middle of the park, just as in the defeats by Brentford and Tottenham.

Both before and since Maxence Lacroix’s untimely injury, Alonso has been so unable to trust Levi Colwill and Wesley Fofana that 20-year-old Josh Acheampong has proven the only broadly solid defender.

Transfer news LIVE: Arsenal learn £100m twist; new Man Utd target

Fofana risks Chelsea fan fury as he laughs off criticism: ‘Couldn’t care less’

Chelsea handed Joao Pedro warning ahead of £100m transfer decision

Winter escapes and activities to end the year in style

Chopping and changing between a back three and back four is merely a product of Alonso’s desperation to find a defensive unit that works, yet it has been an enemy to that search for control.

Chelsea have seen little of the ball in some games, but the early wins over Fulham and Brighton came through slick play in transition, and Alonso believes control is not just about slow and steady possession.

“We have spells where I would like us to have better control, and I’m not meaning just control with the ball,” he explained.

“You can have control without the ball when you feel comfortable [because] you know the opponent has the ball where you want them to have it.  Then you feel in control. That is the way I like to play.”

Yet there remains a huge disparity between Alonso’s vision of control without the ball and Chelsea’s actual reality.

Teams are consistently occupying the ball in very dangerous areas and creating the better chances. Leeds, for example, could have scored far more than four on Saturday.

Scoring 20 goals and conceding the same number doesn’t spell control, and it is the first time in a decade that Chelsea have lost as many as five of their opening 11 league fixtures.

Friday night against Nottingham Forest must be more like that mature win at Everton with less of the chaos seen from Chelsea since.

Alonso was considered the brightest new tactical mind in management less than two years ago, but is yet to imprint his identity on Chelsea four months in. He is not under immediate pressure of the sack, but grace periods don’t last forever.

#1665. Rodrigo Bentancur transfer: Aston Villa 'pursuit' of £8.4m-valued player could 'trigger' Tottenham Hotspur exit

By Seye Omidiora | 25 Nov 2026 02:12

Argentine giants Boca Juniors are reportedly keen to bring Tottenham Hotspur midfielder Rodrigo Bentancur back to Buenos Aires as they prepare for next year's Copa Libertadores.

While funding a deal for the 29-year-old Uruguay international would normally prove difficult, the potential sale of highly rated youngster Milton Delgado could hand Boca the financial firepower required.

Aston Villa are among a host of English clubs tracking the 21-year-old defensive midfielder, meaning a winter raid from Unai Emery's side could directly threaten Tottenham's midfield depth.

According to Argentine outlets El Crack Deportivo and El Intransigente via Sport Witness, Boca president Juan Roman Riquelme has already started preliminary work on re-signing Bentancur.

Riquelme views the Spurs stalwart as his preferred candidate to replace Delgado should the academy graduate depart La Bombonera in the coming months.

Bentancur progressed through Boca's youth ranks before earning a switch to Juventus in 2017 and is seen as the ideal experienced presence to anchor their upcoming continental campaign.

The South American outfit plan to reinvest the proceeds from Delgado's prospective transfer straight into a formal approach for their former player.

Delgado's stock has risen even further after he played the full 90 minutes in Boca's 2-0 Copa Sudamericana final triumph over Atletico Mineiro on Saturday.

Villa are reportedly preparing a formal January offer for Delgado after scouting the 21-year-old extensively across the past six months.

However, Emery's side are far from alone in the race, with Chelsea, Bournemouth, Brighton and West Ham United all linked with the youngster.

Boca are believed to have previously rejected a £7.5m bid from MLS side Atlanta United back in August, around the same time Chelsea and Bournemouth lodged initial enquiries for the young midfielder, who is valued at €10m (£8.4m) by Transfermarkt.

Portuguese outfit Porto are also believed to be monitoring developments from Europe, leaving Riquelme in a strong position to command a substantial fee if a bidding war erupts.

Even if Boca secure the necessary funds, convincing Bentancur to leave North London could prove complicated given that he signed a new long-term contract with Tottenham in October 2025 and has spent almost a decade competing at the top level in Europe.

#1663. In-form Bournemouth could join elite company in trip to Celta Vigo

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

When Bournemouth fans booked their plane tickets to Spain following the Europa League draw back in August, few would have expected their club to be in the position they are in now.

The clash with Celta Vigo on Thursday gives Bournemouth the opportunity to secure their 10th successive win in all competitions. Their current run of nine wins in a row is already a club record as a Football League team (since 1923-24).

Even the most ardent Bournemouth fans would have laughed at the idea of their club winning 10 successive games in all competitions if you had put it to them a couple of months ago. But maybe we should not be so shocked.

The Cherries ended last season with an 18-game unbeaten run in the Premier League – the strongest finish by any side in the competition – and that was extended to 19 in all competitions, because despite exiting the FA Cup on penalties to Newcastle in January, the third-round match ended in a 3-3 draw at St. James’ Park.

That sequence of results under former manager Andoni Iraola was impressive, but Marco Rose’s achievement since replacing the Spaniard is arguably even better.

"So far, I can just praise the locker room," said Rose about his Bournemouth side.

"We are here to play football and to win the game. Everyone is ready, we have no new injuries ahead of [Thursday's] game. We are glad to have Alex [Scott] and Junior [Kroupi] back and available.

"Celta Vigo are able to run, they are able to press high, they are quite compact and it is hard to score against them.

"They are just lacking goals, but they had the chances [to score]. They are a good team."

Bournemouth's current nine-game winning streak follows an inauspicious start by the new German boss as well. They won just two of their first eight competitive matches of 2026-27 (L3 D3), with both of those victories coming in cup competitions.

Following a 5-1 thrashing at Chelsea on MD6 of the Premier League season, Bournemouth sat in the relegation zone with just three points.

The 3-0 Europa League win over Sturm Graz five days after that loss at Stamford Bridge was the turning point. Since then, Bournemouth have won every game they have played and astonishingly only conceded two goals, despite the injury absence of influential midfielder Alex Scott.

Evanilson has been the star of the winning run, scoring seven goals and assisting two more in his eight appearances.

Postcards from Vigo  https://t.co/LzLiDPrWHK

— AFC Bournemouth  (@afcbournemouth) November 25, 2026

The Brazilian has scored in each of his last five appearances in all competitions for the club, while his run of six consecutive Premier League games scored in is a club record. He might just have one eye on Jamie Vardy’s all-time record of 11 in a row set in 2015.

Thursday’s European clash in Spain offers Bournemouth the chance of making it 10 wins in a row, but how impressive will that run be compared to previous efforts by other Premier League clubs?

Winning so many consecutive games is rare for any Premier League club, let alone one which is not known for being one of English football's powerhouses.

Only seven clubs have managed to go on a winning streak of 10+ competitive games while in the Premier League – all of those have won at least three top-flight English league titles. Bournemouth are only in their 10th season as a top-flight club.

Bournemouth will have to win another 13 competitive games in a row to eclipse the sensational 21-match winning streak by Pep Guardiola’s Manchester City side between December 2020 and March 2021, though.

Starting with a victory at Southampton in the Premier League on 19 December 2020, City enjoyed 21 successive wins in all competitions before a surprise 2-0 home defeat to rivals Manchester United on 7 March 2021.

Arsenal won their final 11 competitive games of the 2001-02 season before adding two more victories at the start of 2002-03 campaign, with that 13-game winning streak the second longest by a Premier League club in all competitions.

Bournemouth should be confident of securing a 10th win in succession against a Celta Vigo side who have won just four of 18 matches in 2026-27, the most recent coming in the Copa del Rey against fourth-tier club Salamanca UDS.

Beat Celta, then Bournemouth's next challenge will be to secure an 11th win in a row in their home game against Fulham, who sit 15th in the Premier League and have won seven points fewer than Rose’s men.

There have only been eight instances of a Premier League team winning 11+ consecutive games. Can Bournemouth become the ninth?

#1662. The next Lamine Yamal? Why not? Roberto De Zerbi sets high bar for Luca Williams-Barnett after 18-year-old thrilled Tottenham fans in win over Ipswich, writes MATT BARLOW

Published: 12:22 EST, 21 November 2026 | Updated: 06:34 EST, 22 November 2026

Luca Williams-Barnett will score better goals. That was the consensus on a day when the Tottenham starlet marked his first Premier League by scoring the first and creating the second.

Roberto De Zerbi compared him to Lamine Yamal after watching the 18-year-old steal the show as Spurs beat Ipswich, their fourth win in five to move within three points of the top four.

'He is a special player, I am not surprised,' said De Zerbi. 'I decided 10 days ago he would play and I asked him two things. First, to play like he is on the park with his friends and then to work hard without the ball, like Raphinha and Yamal.

'In football today players with talent have to work hard and attackers are the first defenders.'

Asked if Williams-Barnett could aspire to the levels of Barcelona’s Yamal, the Spurs boss replied: 'Yes, I think so'. And told how on the teenager had spent the bus ride to the stadium watching clips of Ronaldinho, Neymar and Eden Hazard on YouTube.

His goal was a picture of youthful desire and determination to get across his marker at the back post and be first to a delicious teasing cross delivered by Pedro Porro.

Roberto De Zerbi rates Williams-Barnett as ‘one of the best’ young players he has worked with

Williams-Barnett slid and stretched past Abdoul Ouattara with his right foot as the ball skipped and hit him high on the left thigh before rebounding into the bottom corner.

You make your own luck. The Spurs crowd erupted. They have been waiting to hail another of their own. Maybe this is the one. A goal on his first start, just like Harry Kane, and at 18 years and 51 days, the club’s youngest league scorer since Gareth Bale.

There has been a buzz growing around Williams-Barnett for the last 18 months as he rose through the academy ranks. He made his England Under-19 debut in September, coming on as a sub for Max Dowman, Arsenal’s teenage sensation.

De Zerbi adores his attitude as much as his talent, and a confidence bordering arrogance on display in pre-season when he dinked in a ‘Panenka’ style penalty in a shootout in Australia.

He is right-footed but started against Ipswich wide on the left, in the role no player has made their own since Heung-min Son.

Dominic Solanke, who scored Tottenham's second goal, congratulates his young team-mate

Williams-Barnett might have had a second before half time, a half-chance miscued and a header saved.

Spurs fans responded. When he picked up the ball on halfway early in the second half, they roared him forward into the space ahead. He duly obliged, through the gears into a swagger and into the Ipswich penalty box without meeting a challenge.

Tottenham (4-2-3-1): Kinsky 6; Porro 7, Van Hecke 6, Senesi 6, Udogie 6 (Robertson 80); Fernandes 7, Gallagher 7; Kudus 6, Maddison 7 (Bergvall 64, 5), Williams-Barnett 8 (Savio 64, 6 (Gray 90)); Solanke 7 (Marmoush 64, 5).

Booked: Maddison, Williams-Barnett, Kudus, Fernandes.

Ipswich (3-4-2-1): Walton 7; Furlong 5, Diop 5, O’Shea 6; Outtara 4 (Fatawu 56, 5), Palacios 5 (Florentino 56, 5), Lukic 6, Davis 6 (Greaves 82); Enciso 5, Maeda 5 (Clarke 56, 5); Flemming 6.

Belatedly, Darnell Furlong tried to hold him up. But Williams-Barnett made a yard on the outside and whipped over a cross with his left foot, which fizzed past Walton and was turned in from close range by Dominic Solanke.

The teenager booted the ball jubilantly into the crowd and collected his first yellow card from killjoy referee Rob Jones.

Williams-Barnett left to a standing ovation when he was replaced by Savio in the 64th minute. 'Luca was magnificent,' said Solanke. 'To see him do that on his first Premier League start is crazy.'

Spurs coasted in. It had been comfortable, even without some senior players including Sandro Tonali who had been unwell.

They were solid at the back and creative up front, peppering the Ipswich goal with 18 shots. Mohamed Kudus struck a post from a first-half free kick, won by Williams-Barnett.

Christian Walton made strong saves to deny James Maddison and prevent Dara O’Shea turning into his own goal.

Savio cross hit a post with a deflected cross before he was struck down by a recurrence of the hamstring injury which ruled him out for six weeks. It was the only blemish for De Zerbi, although one to enhance the opportunities ahead for Williams-Barnett.

#1660. Rasmus Hojlund reveals the Manchester United stars left ‘devastated’ by INEOS decision

Rasmus Hojlund has revealed that Bruno Fernandes was among the Manchester United players to be left “devastated” by the recent sacking of Michael Carrick.

Carrick was relieved of his duties as Man Utd boss earlier in November after weeks of intense speculation and less than six months in permanent charge on a two-year contract, with just one win from their opening 10 games having seen his side languish in the Premier League relegation zone.

It is United’s worst start to a top-flight season since 1972, with former Chelsea and Tottenham manager Mauricio Pochettino leaving his role as head coach of the United States national team to quickly succeed Carrick, only to suffer a chastening 4-0 defeat by arch-rivals Liverpool with 10 men in his first match in charge.

Carrick’s final weeks at United saw senior players air their grievances in public interviews following listless defeats, with Lisandro Martinez taking aim at the club’s recruitment after the loss to Atletico Madrid and Fernandes then questioning Carrick’s tactics in the 4-1 thrashing away at Como.

However, captain and coach were said to have held “clear-the-air talks” and been on good terms before the latter’s dismissal, with Hojlund revealing that Fernandes - along with United and Portugal team-mate Diogo Dalot - had been “devastated” by Carrick’s departure but hopeful of bouncing back quickly under his replacement.

The Danish striker was back in Manchester on Tuesday night in the Champions League, scoring for Napoli against City and making headlines with his pro-United celebration in a lively 2-2 draw at the Etihad Stadium.

Hojlund previously spent three years at Old Trafford between 2023-26 following a high-profile £72million transfer from Atalanta aged 20, netting 26 times in 95 total appearances across all competitions before returning to Serie A for £38m in the summer as Napoli exercised their option for a permanent deal following a successful season-long loan spell last term.

“In the international break when I spoke with Bruno and Diogo, they were all obviously devastated that Michael was going but also looking forward to some change,” said Hojlund, who recently scored twice for Denmark in their 4-1 thrashing of a Cristiano Ronaldo-less Portugal in the Nations League.

“I am still speaking with [Denmark team-mate and United player] Patrick [Dorgu] and I just wish the guys all the best and I am sure they will turn it around this season.”

#1659. Mauricio Pochettino faces an 'early January call' as two Champions League clubs 'line up' a raid on Man Utd’s attack

By Seye Omidiora | 25 Nov 2026 02:59

Serie A duo Como and Napoli are reportedly monitoring Manchester United forward Joshua Zirkzee ahead of the January transfer window.

The 25-year-old Netherlands international has struggled to secure regular playing time under multiple managers since arriving at Old Trafford from Bologna in the summer of 2024.

Zirkzee is yet to make a single Premier League start during the 2026-27 campaign, with all seven of his top-flight outings coming from the substitutes' bench.

After nearly leaving England on Deadline Day, when United rejected an approach from Everton, the attacker could now be set for a winter return to Italian football.

The forward has been earmarked as a possible early departure from Old Trafford under Mauricio Pochettino in January.

According to Sky Sports News, both Italian clubs are exploring a mid-season move but are waiting for clarity on Zirkzee's role under new United head coach Mauricio Pochettino.

Pochettino was only appointed last week and handed the Dutchman a 45-minute second-half cameo during Sunday's chastening 4-0 Premier League defeat at Liverpool.

No formal negotiations have been opened with the Red Devils hierarchy yet as suitors wait to discover whether the Argentine tactician considers the forward surplus to requirements.

Zirkzee has managed two goals across his limited substitute appearances this season, netting against Aston Villa in the league and ironically finding the back of the net against Como in the Champions League last month.

The Dutchman's previous pedigree in Italy, where he earned a spot in the Serie A Team of the Year with Bologna, ensures his stock remains high across the peninsula despite his Old Trafford struggles.

Both interested sides have urgent attacking voids to fill when the winter market opens for business.

Como boss Cesc Fabregas recently confirmed that striker Moise Kean faces several months on the sidelines after aggravating a recurring tibia issue in training.

Meanwhile, Napoli boss Massimiliano Allegri is seeking fresh firepower after Lorenzo Lucca struggled to make an impact following his return from a loan spell at Nottingham Forest.

With United already heavily linked with prolific strikers like Vangelis Pavlidis and Ivan Toney to spearhead Pochettino's rebuild, a January exit could ultimately suit all parties involved.

#1658. Borussia Dortmund boss issues ‘strong’ Arsenal verdict after Champions League battle

Your weekly briefing on Arsenal, featuring team news and expert analysis from Matt Verri

Borussia Dortmund boss Niko Kovac has hailed his side’s fight against “strong” Arsenal, but was frustrated by the decision to deny them a penalty.

BVB drew 1-1 with the Gunners at the Emirates Stadium on Tuesday night after Maximilian Beier’s second-half strike cancelled out an early opening effort by Viktor Gyokeres.

Dortmund repelled waves of dominant but ultimately profligate Arsenal pressure throughout an entertaining league phase encounter but also saw a second goal through Jobe Bellingham ruled out for offside.

A draw despite giving up 30 shots and seeing their woodwork hit three times continued a strong run of form for Dortmund, who currently sit inside the Champions League top eight and above Bayern Munich at the summit of the Bundesliga, having now gone nine games unbeaten across all competitions - winning six.

After the game, Kovac said: “It’s a huge point for us, a huge moment for all of us - for the team and for the fans, who turned out in such big numbers today.

“In the end, of course, we’re happy with the point. The game was here in London, so obviously you have to weather a few dangerous situations.

“I think the team put up a really good fight today. No one would say they were being timid or didn't give it their all. We fought as a team, kept coming back, and showed that we can hold our own against a strong opponent.”

However, Kovac believes that Arsenal were fortunate to avoid giving away a penalty when the ball clearly struck the arm of Gyokeres from a Dortmund corner delivery during the second half.

“I thought VAR should have looked at the handball. It would have been worth a check,” he said.

“They are trying to intervene less with the on-field decisions, but it doesn't mean you should not intervene when you should do.

“I am not crying about it. It is what it is. We got a point. It is a big point away to Arsenal, a big one for all of us - our fans, our team and the club.”

#1657. Mauricio Pochettino given £50m transfer budget at Man Utd - here’s who he should sign

Manchester United fans will be dismayed by reports that Mauricio Pochettino will have just £50million to improve his squad during the January transfer window.

A leaky defence has led to calls from ex-players such as Gary Neville for significant investment, but it appears Man Utd will try to do their business on a tight budget in January.

The second window of the season often leads to inflated prices, with clubs capitalising upon other teams’ struggles and desperate need for new players.

The defence is the priority, with Man Utd reportedly keen on finding a new left-back and centre-back, while Pochettino also wants a new striker.

Fikayo Tomori’s spell at AC Milan looks to be coming to a close at the six-year mark, with the England international caught in the transfer merry-go-round back in the summer.

Massimo Allegri froze the centre-back out of the AC Milan squad, only for the Italian giants to fail in recruiting a replacement. Even when drafted back into the first team, Tomori has found gametime hard to come by - waiting six Serie A games for his first appearance of the league season.

Currently sidelined with a hamstring issue, GOAL report that Tomori will not be offered a new contract when his current deal expires next summer. Despite being keen on a return to England, the 28-year-old rejected transfers to Fulham and Coventry City.

Hojlund reveals the Man Utd stars left ‘devastated’ by INEOS decision

Transfer news LIVE: Arsenal learn £100m twist; new Man Utd target

Tomori was said to be holding out on a move to Aston Villa or staying at AC Milan. The defender’s situation at San Siro could mean that Man Utd could reinforce their backline with an experienced player, that is also home-grown, on the cheap.

Milan were fielding bids worth around £15m in the summer, meaning a similar amount or even lower would likely be accepted in January.

To save even more money, Man Utd could make a pre-contract agreement with Tomori in January, paving the way for a free transfer next summer.

They cannot do that with Crystal Palace’s Tyrick Mitchell, despite the left-back also being out of contract at the end of the season. That is because English clubs cannot agree pre-contracts with players at other teams in England.

As such, Man Utd would have to open up their wallet and spend some cash on the 27-year-old, who has over 200 Premier League games under his belt making his debut during the 2019/20 season.

Mitchell has played his entire career for the Eagles, making a total of 260 appearances in blue and red. It has been reported that Palace hold a clause in Mitchell’s current deal to extend it for a further year, which preserves some of the left-back’s value.

Liverpool and Juventus have both previously been credited with an interest in Mitchell, as well as Man Utd. Previous reports have quoted transfer fees of £25m, which appears to be below the going rate for Premier League-proven left-backs.

Ivan Toney is another England international that Man Utd have been linked to. At first glance, the Red Devils’ £50mn budget would appear to nix any potential deal for the former Brentford man, Toney leaving London for £40million two seasons ago to sign for Al-Hilal in Saudi Arabia.

Not only would a transfer fee seemingly be a stretch, but also Toney’s inflated wages playing in the Middle East. However, recent reports from TEAMtalk claim that intermediaries are sounding out a potential loan move to Old Trafford, with the view of a future permanent transfer.

Such an arrangement would allow Man Utd to spend their money elsewhere, before making a decision on investing further cash into Toney after a loan period.

Still only 30 years old, Toney has recently been dropped from England duty. Harbouring ambitions of playing at Euro 2028, a move back to England may improve Toney’s chances of a call-up in two summers’ time.

A potential problem is that two former flames of Toney are interested in a reunion. His former Brentford boss Thomas Frank , now at Crystal Palace, is reportedly keen on bringing Toney back to London, while the striker’s old club Newcastle - backed by Saudi Arabia and managed by ex-Al-Hilal boss Mathias Jaissle - are also sniffing around a potential move.

#1656. Chelsea transfer news: PSG back off from Blues target

By Axel Clody | 25 Nov 2026 06:28

In recent seasons, Manu Kone has often been linked with Paris Saint-Germain, but the capital club have never really tried to sign him. The reason behind that choice has been revealed.

A talented French international from the Paris region, Manu Kone seemed to have the ideal profile to join PSG. The Roma midfielder has often been reported on the capital club's shortlist, but PSG have never really tried to recruit him.

The 25-year-old will return to the Parc des Princes on Wednesday at 8pm UK time, for matchday five of the Champions League with the Italian side.

He will have the chance to show the full extent of his talent to Parisian supporters, although it is unlikely that Kone will join the two-time European champions in the short term, according to L'Equipe.

The sports daily tried to explain the reasons for PSG's choice not to sign the French midfielder. This summer, Paris simply had no desire to recruit another midfielder and wanted to count on their current squad, with its established players such as Vitinha and Joao Neves, and its young gems such as Dro Fernandez and Senny Mayulu.

Paris had an opportunity in the summer of 2024. Before his move to Roma for £15.3m (€18m), the Frenchman was offered to Paris. Some people internally pushed for the capital club to sign this promising and affordable young box-to-box midfielder. Luis Campos has always liked the profile of the former Toulouse player.

However, PSG decided otherwise. 'I do not make all the decisions on my own' - the Paris sporting director said.

L'Equipe concludes that Luis Enrique did not approve the option. The Spanish boss preferred to rely on his Neves-Vitinha-Ruiz trio. Therefore, unless he changes his mind, the Kone option appears to be one to forget in Paris.

While PSG appear to have moved on, Kone has regularly been linked with clubs in England. Chelsea, Liverpool and Manchester United were all credited with interest in the Roma midfielder during the summer transfer window, including on deadline day, according to the Liverpool Echo.

Chelsea were said to still have an interest in late August, with Kone one of several midfielders on their list, according to CaughtOffside. At that stage, the website considered Manchester United effectively out of the race after the signings of Youri Tielemans, Andrey Santos and Carlos Baleba, although that was its own assessment rather than a reported club position.

More recently, Gazzetta dello Sport reported in mid-November that Chelsea could make a move in January. Roma boss Gian Piero Gasperini reportedly vetoed a sale in the final hours of the summer window, and the Italian club are said to value Kone at £47m-£51m (€55m-€60m), compared with the £43m reported in August.

#1655. Glasner ‘no magician’ but expected more Premier League points at Forest

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Oliver Glasner quipped he does not have "magic dust" he can spread to turn Nottingham Forest's Premier League fortunes around after an underwhelming start to the season.

Forest sit 17th in the Premier League ahead of Friday's clash with Chelsea at the City Ground and are only outside the relegation zone on goal difference ahead of Sunderland.

Glasner's side were beaten 2-0 away to Bournemouth last time out, and have now won just two of their last 14 top-flight games (D5 L7), with their problems coming in attack.

The Tricky Trees failed to score against Bournemouth but registered 2.14 expected goals, the highest xG tally by any team not to score in a Premier League match this season.

Forest have failed to score in more Premier League games than any other side this season (six), while only Sunderland (eight) have fewer goals overall than Forest (nine).

Glasner does, however, feel there is room for optimism, though he conceded that he expected to have more points than the nine they currently have after 11 league matches.

"We all thought and wished we would have more points. Performances in games were better than results. We wanted and expected more from us to be honest," Glasner said.

"We have to accept the reality. I'm no magician. I have no magic dust I can spread. We need to improve our individual mistakes.

"We need to improve our efficiency in attack. Still no goals from set pieces. I think I always talked about stability and consistency. This is what we still have to find and do better.

"To really perform consistently on a high level, we get enough points and we get enough wins. Then you climb the table and this is what we're looking for."

Under the lights on Friday night. https://t.co/YFKAJZge9I

— Nottingham Forest (@NFFC) November 24, 2026

Following a 3-1 win at Stamford Bridge in May, Forest are looking to win consecutive league games against Chelsea for the first time since April 1979 (a run of three).

And their hopes of improving in the final third have been boosted ahead of kick-off, with former Chelsea forward Callum Hudson-Odoi back in the Forest fold.

Hudson-Odoi missed Forest's defeat to Bournemouth with an injury picked up during the international break, but he is back involved for the visit of Xabi Alonso's side.

"Yes, Callum Hudson-Odoi trained with us and is fit," Glasner said. "We're just missing Nicolas Domínguez and [Nicolo] Savona. All others are available."

Xaver Schlager was also confirmed to be available for Glasner, having been left on the bench at the Vitaly Stadium after sustaining a slight issue on international duty.

Chelsea are unbeaten in their last five away league games against Forest (W4 D1), with their three consecutive victories their longest run of league wins at the City Ground.

It seems AC Milan have made an offer for Endrick in recent days, with a Spanish journalist shocked at the situation.

Talk of Endrick arriving at San Siro is dominating the news, and it’s clear that Milan are not messing around here. Indeed, they are looking to beat off interest from other European clubs and they may well be close to doing so.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Jose Mourinho is still opposing a deal, but the Brazilian’s entourage was in Italy last week and it seems that a move to San Siro is becoming less of a hypothetical and more of a tangible possibility.

Speaking to SER Radio, Anton Meana looked at the reporting from Italy about the Rossoneri’s interest in Endrick and how the situation was actually unfolding.

“AC Milan’s offer is formal and they want to sign him in January. The Rossoneri have already informed the player, and if he can’t leave in January, they’ll see about negotiations in the summer. But AC Milan’s firm offer is now on the table.

“The owner of AC Milan wants to offer close to 70 million euros to sign Endrick now. The problem is that Mourinho prefers to keep him because he knows there wouldn’t be a signing that could match or surpass the Brazilian.

#1653. Co-owner Brittany Mahomes leads wild celebrations as Kansas City Current wins NWSL title

Published: 09:15 EST, 22 November 2026 | Updated: 09:15 EST, 22 November 2026

Kansas City Current co-owner Brittany Mahomes led the celebrations as the women's soccer club won its first ever NWSL Championship on Saturday.

Brittany, the wife of Kansas City Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes, was at Audi Field in Washington, DC for the final match of the season between the Current and the Washington Spirit.

A thrilling finish to the contest resulted in a 2-1 win for the Current, who have only been in existence for five years.

Brittany, who is pregnant with her fourth child, was seen on the pitch celebrating after her team's inaugural title.

She was seen embracing her team and her co-owners as they jumped up and down in celebration of the achievement.

Brittany was a part of the inaugural ownership group of the club when it was announced as an expansion team in 2020.

KC Current co-owner Brittany Mahomes celebrated her team winning the NWSL title

She was seen jumping up and down and celebrating with the players as the title was clinched

It's the first championship for the expansion club, which began playing in 2021

Brittany's husband, Kansas City Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes, also celebrated the achievement on social media.

The three-time Super Bowl champion reshared the club's announcement on X, adding, 'AHHHHHHHHHH!!!!!!!!!!' He later added, 'LETS GOOOO!!!!!!' and a string of light blue hearts.

Kansas City went ahead in the match in the 54th minute with an 'Olimpico' goal from Vanessa DiBernardo, who watched her corner kick curl to the opposite post to break a first-half deadlock.

With Washington pressing late in added time, the Current were able to score on a counter attack goal from the foot of Brazilian star Debinha to make it 2-0.

Mere seconds later, Washington's Trinity Rodman scored a goal of her own to briefly give Spirit fans hope of a miraculous comeback.

But after 11 elapsed minutes - well beyond the nine given, thanks in part to a scary collision between Rodman and KC keeper Laney Rouse - the final whistle blew as Kansas City clinched the title.

The win for the Current means yet another season of heartbreak for Washington, who have made the last three straight NWSL Championship games and have lost all three.

#1652. Arsenal star sends Man City warning before blockbuster showdown

Your weekly briefing on Arsenal, featuring team news and expert analysis from Matt Verri

Viktor Gyokeres has warned of the obvious threat that Manchester City still pose to Arsenal ahead of their huge showdown this weekend.

The Premier League title rivals lock horns in north London on Sunday afternoon, with six points and two places separating them in the table as things stand.

Defending champions Arsenal have won nine of their first 11 top-flight games this season to already sit six points clear at the summit following a dramatic 2-2 draw at Newcastle, while they remain unbeaten in the Champions League.

That is in stark contrast to City, who sit third behind surprise package Brighton after Saturday’s disappointing home draw with Fulham, which came after back-to-back surprise losses at the hands of Brighton and Nottingham Forest.

Those struggles continued in the Champions League on Tuesday night, when Enzo Maresca’s side twice had to fight back from a deficit to claim a 2-2 home draw with Napoli - after which star striker Erling Haaland expressed concern over their lack of wins.

Despite that disappointing form, Gyokeres believes that City will still present a significant challenge to Arsenal in their blockbuster clash at the Emirates Stadium this weekend.

“They still have a very good squad and very good players,” the Swedish forward said after scoring the opening goal in Arsenal’s 1-1 draw with Borussia Dortmund in the Champions League on Tuesday.

“Sometimes, you may have a period where you don’t get the results all the time – which is normal for any club.

“It is going to be a difficult game on Sunday. But it is always fun with big games. It is going to be good.”

Gyokeres insists that Arsenal will not spend any time thinking about the potentially significant ramifications of City’s Premier League charges on this season’s title race.

The latest reports suggest that City’s appeal could be heard in December, with a potential ruling expected early in 2027.

“It is what it is,” Gyokeres said of the situation, per the Press Association. “We are focused on the game on Sunday.

#1651. "It's like Zidane" - Spanish media in awe of "devastating" Jude Bellingham after Real Madrid win

By Lewis Blain | 25 Nov 2026 07:10

Real Madrid produced a sensational second-half comeback to beat PSV Eindhoven 5-1 in the Champions League on Tuesday evening, with England star Jude Bellingham proving instrumental after being introduced at half-time.

Jose Mourinho's side were trailing 1-0 at the interval following Ivan Perisic's penalty, but Federico Valverde restored parity before the 23-year-old produced a spectacular volley to put Los Blancos ahead. Kylian Mbappe scored twice, and Vinicius Junior added a fifth to complete the turnaround.

Bellingham's influence attracted widespread praise from the Spanish media, with several publications describing him as the decisive figure in Madrid's transformation.

His 45-minute contribution included a goal, an assist and a series of impressive individual statistics.

AS were particularly impressed, publishing the headline "Bellingham: lo cambio todo" - 'Bellingham changed everything'.

Manu de Juan highlighted how the England international reorganised Madrid's midfield, allowing Arda Guler to operate deeper and giving the hosts greater control and attacking momentum. AS also praised his spectacular volley for the 2-1 lead and his subsequent assist for Vinicius.

El Pais delivered perhaps the most glowing assessment, publishing the headline "El esplendor deslumbrante de Bellingham impulsa la goleada del Madrid al PSV" - Bellingham's 'dazzling brilliance' drives Madrid's thrashing of PSV.

David Alvarez argued that Madrid's first-half performance had been lifeless and directionless, with Bellingham's introduction restoring clarity, composure and quality. His spectacular volley was described as a beautiful and devastating goal, with the newspaper suggesting the Englishman's arrival completely transformed the contest.

Mundo Deportivo labelled Bellingham a "superestrella" - 'superstar' - and suggested that he is currently Madrid's best player, while highlighting how his introduction changed the game.

ElDesmarque were equally enthusiastic, awarding the midfielder 9/10 and naming him their MVP. They highlighted his immediate influence, spectacular goal and assist for Vinicius, describing his 45 minutes as an outstanding exhibition.

Real Madrid-focused publications Defensa Central and madridistaReal went even further, awarding him 10/10 and 9.5/10 respectively. Both considered his introduction the turning point in Madrid's victory.

Spanish radio station Cadena SER also marvelled at his volley, with several commentators comparing the technical brilliance of the finish to something Zinedine Zidane might have produced - 'It's like Zizou,' one remarked.

Mourinho was equally impressed, describing the England international's performance as "absolutamente devastador" - 'absolutely devastating'.

The Portuguese coach explained that he had initially considered leaving Bellingham out to protect him from fatigue, believing Madrid could win without him. However, he admitted that having the midfielder available from the bench proved decisive.

Mourinho also described Bellingham as a different type of player who provided something Madrid had been missing during the opening 45 minutes.

The statistics underline why the praise was justified. Despite playing just 45 minutes, Bellingham registered one goal, one assist and created three chances. According to Sofascore, he also completed 100% of his attempted dribbles, won all of his tackles and claimed 75% of his duels.

His influence extended beyond the spectacular finish, with his movement between the lines helping Madrid establish control and create opportunities for their forwards.

There is little doubt that Bellingham was the defining figure in Madrid's comeback - while Mourinho's triple half-time substitution and improved collective pressing also played important roles, the Englishman's ability to bring structure, energy and creativity to the midfield was particularly striking.

Receiving such glowing praise from the Spanish media and his manager after just 45 minutes illustrates the level Bellingham can reach when operating at his best. His goal may have been the highlight, but it was his all-round contribution that made this one of his most impressive performances of the season.

#1648. AC Milan 5-1 Frosinone: Five things we learned – centrality and consistency

AC Milan put on a show at San Siro on Sunday night as they swept Frosinone aside emphatically, beating them 5-1.

The own-goal that Gabriele Calvani scored a few minutes in set the tone for the visitors, while Goncalo Ramos broke his drought after starting and finishing a counter-attack. However, Patrizio Masini’s goal shortly after meant the deficit was halved going into the break.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

In the second half, Milan ran riot. Ardon Jashari and Alphadjo Cisse both had opportunities after being found in behind, and both just minutes after coming off the bench. Then, Christian Pulisic added the finishing touch to make it a five-star night.

It was a win that Milan needed, considering that only Inter out of the current top six, dropped points, and it moves the Rossoneri back into the top four spots. Ivan Stoev has picked out the key talking points from the game.

Technically, Rabiot won the MOTM in our post-game ratings, but we absolutely have to talk about Luka Modric.

I’ve personally had my doubts about the Croatian being able to keep up this season, especially under Ruben Amorim. We all expected the Portuguese coach to bring a lot of intensity to Milan’s game and at times, Modric has seemed to struggle.

Maybe that was because of the team adapting to the new coach, or maybe the midfielder hadn’t completely recovered after the World Cup – who knows.

The reality is that the former Real Madrid man has stepped up after some shaky games at the start of the season and continues to prove his quality on and off the ball and his athleticism and longevity are nothing short of extraordinary.

The vision and passing ability to play the through ball to Rabiot for the opening goal was world-class. He then continued to dictate the tempo and make impressive forward runs, playing the full 90 minutes, giving it his all until the final whistle.

The management really needs to assemble a whole group of people tasked to find a proper replacement for Modric, as he will leave a big gap in that midfield.

To continue with the midfielder theme, we also have to give praise to Rabiot, who has been absolutely brilliant this season. Don’t get me wrong, he was one of the Rossoneri’s best players last year too.

Yet he has found a higher level since the start of the campaign, as he racked up another two assists and forced the own goal. As a result, he now has five goals and seven assists in 10 games in Serie A – extraordinary numbers.

On top of the goal contributions, you can count on the Frenchman to be composed under pressure, tidy with his passing, and efficient in both phases of the game. An absolutely stunning start of the season for Rabiot, who is finding new levels to his game under Amorim.

It was such a dominant win that we can probably cover each player and the positives from their game. Nevertheless, one man needs to be praised for sure and that’s Goncalo Ramos, who got himself back on the scoresheet.

Needless to say, he opened up a lot of spaces for his teammates and had a role in some of the other goals, which he was doing even when he failed to get the ball in the back of the net. This time around, he also got his long-awaited goal.

It was a beauty too, in the sense that he dropped deep into his own half, made the tackle to win the ball and kicked off the counter-attack. Following that, he made the run into the opponent’s box and finished it calmly – it was beautifully orchestrated with Ramos in the centre.

The goal and the encouraging performance are also a relief, as we’ve seen many times how strikers struggle to react when they are not scoring, with the confidence level often dropping which results in overall poor form.

However, the Portuguese striker is clearly not in his head and reacted well to a poor spell that spanned both his club and the national team, as he struggled in the international break too.

We didn’t even see that much of him as Amorim subbed him off rather early and it probably has to do with the fact that Milan need a win on Thursday against Olympiacos, in Greece, and Ramos will most likely start the game as the margin for error is little as things stand.

I mean, what more can you ask from your attackers? Diego Moreira got the hockey assist on the second goal and got an assist for Cisse in the second half and on top of that, was heavily involved and dangerous when the Diavolo went on the counter.

Truthfully, the Belgian should have probably scored a goal or two as he had some very good chances in the opponent’s penalty box, but his shooting let him down this time around. Nevertheless, another electric performance.

Speaking of electric – Pulisic also did very well as he was involved in the first goal – even if it ended up being an own goal, his run forced the Frosinone defender to run back and eventually put the ball in his own net.

The American then got his goal in the second half with a composed finish. He had a very solid game overall with lots of smart movements and combination play- nothing flashy, but the efficiency was there.

Then we also have Cisse, who started the game on the bench but only needed nine or so minutes after coming on to get his goal. Ridiculously, he now has six in 10 in the league or a goal every 74 minutes. The youngster made a good run and managed to keep himself onside in a tricky situation and then finished with composure.

The variety in attack by Milan on the night was a joy to watch, as all the players posed a threat to Frosinone, which in the end was too much for them to handle.

Amorim was well aware of how Frosinone would approach the game, which in itself deserves credit as they came to San Siro to play football instead of sitting back. Unfortunately for them and fortunately for us, the coach and his players knew exactly how to get around the high press.

The Rossoneri were rapid on the counter and created so many chances that the score could’ve easily been even worse for Frosinone. Their high press also didn’t work, as for the majority of the game the Diavolo managed to move the ball around quickly enough, which prevented their opponents from winning it in dangerous areas.

It also must be said that the Portuguese did well to rest some key players after the third goal, as he will need a fresh lineup for the Europa League fixture on Thursday, where Milan need three points against Olympiacos.

Welcome to our Live Comments section, where new comments will appear automatically

Also, it was Pulisics’ pass to Moreira that set-up Cisse’s goal. If were recognizing “hockey assists” then Pulisic’s pass to Moreira was also world-class. Not to be a wet-blanket, but Moreira and Cisse need to develop composure on the ball. Too often Moreira would negate his speed on the ball by dribbling into multiple defenders without looking to pass to an open teammate. Against the top teams Milan will not have as many goal scoring opportunities as they did on Sunday so now is the time to work on finding the open man in the final third.

So young players with potential, need to learn to be better and realise thier potential.

It was a pass in a 3v3 counter-attack situation. Great pass but Modric took out 5 defenders with 1 move. That is why it is world class and Pulisic pass is not mentioned as much.

Did anyone notice how Pulisic slowed down his run, thus letting Ramos reach the penalty box earlier and score his long awaited goal? Such a team player..

He’s always been that guy. Sometimes I wish he can be more ‘selfish’. Another example is the penalty fiasco with Tammy back then.

Yet some people here have called him selfish many times – especially last season when he wasn’t scoring. But then again, those same people praised Leao and probably thought he was Ballon d’Or material. LOL. 🤦‍♂️😂😂😂

Yes. I’d say it was as much about letting Ramos score as it was about “arriving” in the box late, setting up a cut back score, which he learned from Frank Lampard. Both are good things.

#1647. Scott McTominay and girlfriend Cam Reading announce pregnancy: Ex-Man United star celebrates 'precious gift' months after having heart surgery

Published: 11:18 EST, 22 November 2026 | Updated: 12:04 EST, 22 November 2026

Napoli star Scott McTominay and his girlfriend Cam Reading have announced they're expecting their first child together.

The couple shared a joint post on Instagram with one picture of them holding up an ultrasound image, another of Reading reclining in a bikini and a third of the pregnancy test itself.

They revealed the news on the same day McTominay broke Napoli's three-game losing streak, scoring the winner in a 1-0 victory over Torino.

The couple wrote: 'The most precious gift, a lifetime of love.' McTominay, 29, and Reading have settled into life in Italy after he joined from Man United and revived his career, winning the Scudetto and earning Player of the Year honours.

It remains to be seen whether the baby will be born in Italy or back in the UK but the couple were overjoyed at sharing their happy news.

It is not exactly clear when McTominay and Reading first crossed paths but they have at least been together since the summer of 2023, when they were pictured on a boat trip in Greece.

Cam Reading and Scott McTominay shared the news that they're expecting a baby

Reading posted this picture of her bump on her Instagram page and wrote of a 'precious gift'

Reading, a director at asset management firm Fortress Capital partners, has seen her personal celebrity skyrocket in that time, zooming up from 10,000 Instagram followers to over 90,000.

According to La Repubblica, they have moved into a house by Lago Patria, a coastal lake near the suburb of Giugliano.

There, McTominay can be by the seaside quickly after popping out of his door and is only around a 20-minute drive from Napoli's training centre.

The couple regularly share photos from their new life together in Italy and McTominay is adored by fans having repeatedly delivered in big moments, none more so than on the final day of the 2024-25 season when an acrobatic strike put Napoli ahead as they clinched the title over Inter Milan.

This season has been less straightforward for McTominay. The Scotland international underwent heart surgery after being diagnosed with 'a mild benign arrhythmia', which is an abnormal or irregular heart rhythm deemed non-serious and posing no significant risk to overall health.

Before the surgery, the British Heart Foundation explained that the procedure McTominay was having would see heat or cold energy used to create tiny scars in the heart to block faulty signals and restore a typical heartbeat.

The procedure took place at the start of September in Manchester, and he was initially supposed to be on the sidelines for two weeks before returning to training.

But he was ruled out of Scotland action during the international break and is now back on the grass with Napoli, scoring the winner against Torino on Saturday.

McTominay and Reading also posted this snap of the ultrasound and positive test

The midfielder scored the winner on Saturday for Napoli against Torino

He has now scored 33 goals in 92 matches across all competitions with the Partenopei and remains one of Serie A's leading lights.

The Italian press gushed over his contribution on Saturday, with Corriere dello Sport writing: 'He played with fire in his belly.

'Three shots in the opening 16 minutes; seven in total—three on target— and a decisive goal (his fourth against Torino, his favourite Serie A opponent, along with Inter), plus the charisma of a leader.'

#1646. Transfer news: Major Saudi Pro League rule change could shake up the market

By Axel Clody | 25 Nov 2026 07:26

With a little over a month to go until the transfer window reopens, clubs around the world are already moving behind the scenes to strengthen their squads. Saudi Arabia, which has become a leading player in the market in recent years, is considering a change that could boost its domestic league but worry other countries.

According to The Times, the Saudi Pro League (SPL) is considering raising the limit on foreign players ahead of the 2027-28 window, which could trigger a new wave of signings. Saudi clubs are seeking clarification on the matter before the Northern Hemisphere winter window in January.

At present, clubs in Saudi Arabia can register up to eight foreign players in a 25-man squad, with the option of adding two more foreign under-21 players for SPL matches. The idea is to raise that limit to 14 or more, with discussions still ongoing.

Should the new rule come into force, Saudi clubs are likely to make more international signings. That could mark a new phase of departures from Europe to join the Saudi project, which aims to improve the competitive level of local football before the country hosts the World Cup in 2034.

In January 2023, Cristiano Ronaldo joined Al-Nassr after terminating his contract with Manchester United, which began a series of Saudi investments in football. In June of that year, the Public Investment Fund (PIF) took control of the four biggest domestic clubs: Al-Ahli, Al-Hilal, Al-Ittihad and Al-Nassr, the Portuguese star's team.

Then Ballon d'Or winner Karim Benzema was another high-profile name to leave Real Madrid for the Saudi Pro League, followed by stars such as N'Golo Kante and Roberto Firmino. Over the past three seasons, Neymar, Ollie Watkins, Gabriel Martinelli, Tijjani Reijnders, Darwin Nunez, Ivan Toney, Sadio Mane and Joao Felix have also been tempted by the Middle East.

As well as drawing global attention to its league, Saudi Arabia believes the move has helped the development of its homegrown talent. Competing for starting places with foreign stars encourages local players to improve.

On the other hand, critics of the proposal to raise the limit on non-Saudi players argue that the rule change could force local players to move abroad, or even leave bigger clubs for smaller ones, in order to get playing time.

It is worth remembering that the PIF has reduced its international sports investments, to the point of ending its backing of LIV Golf. In April, the fund announced a five-year programme with a greater focus on domestic investment. Privatisations of Saudi clubs have also been recurring, such as the sale of 70 per cent of Al-Hilal in August.

Because of the geopolitical context in the region, including Saudi Arabia's conflict with the Yemen-based Houthi rebels, there is some uncertainty over the league's ability to attract foreign players in the short term. In October, the airport in the capital, Riyadh, was hit by a missile attack that killed 13 people and injured more than 300.

The Asian Cup, which was due to be held in the country between January and February 2027, was postponed earlier this month. Three SPL matches were also postponed after the October Houthi attacks, although organisers did not attribute the decision to the conflict, saying it was motivated by 'logistical considerations'.
