Your weekly briefing on Chelsea, featuring team news and expert analysis from Dom Smith

Chelsea should sign Virgil van Dijk as a free agent if he decides against extending his Liverpool contract, Jamie Redknapp believes.

Xabi Alonso already has a lengthy to-do list as he looks to get Chelsea on song, but patching a leaky back line is a top priority. They have already shipped 20 goals in the league this season and have only kept two league clean sheets in their last 27 matches.

A fine market opportunity could arise in the summer as they look to bolster their ranks, though, as Liverpool captain Van Dijk could become a free agent.

The Dutchman is into the final year of his contract and, at 35 years of age, remains one of the game’s finest centre-backs. It remains to be seen whether he will extend his Liverpool deal, though, as he said earlier this month: “I'm looking after myself and I still have many more years in my opinion. Whatever's going to happen after this season, we'll see.”

For Redknapp, Chelsea would be foolish not to make a move for Van Dijk, who he believes could emulate Thiago Silva’s impact on the club.

“All the great centre-back partnerships, you always have one that’s the dominant one, and normally one that will maybe drop off,” he explained.

“If you talk about probably as good as anything, say Virgil [van Dijk] and Jacquet at the moment, you wouldn’t even know who’s who. They’re both aggressive and they go and win challenges.”

Redknapp, speaking on The Overlap Daily, sponsored by Sky Vegas, continued: “But I’ve seen Chelsea’s defence get bullied time after time. Brian Brobbey was obviously one a few weeks ago at Sunderland. And again, Dominic Calvert-Lewin. They cannot live with anyone that’s got any physicality.

“Do they need to just go and, as I keep hearing people say, ‘You need to buy a centre-back.’”

Redknapp, who spent 11 years at Liverpool as a player, continued, saying Van Dijk could be exactly what Chelsea need to bolster their defence, but he started with the caveat: “I don’t know for sure, he might end up staying. I hope he does. (Chelsea) should try and get Virgil van Dijk in the summer. That’s what I’d do.

#1643. Arsenal injury news: Mikel Arteta drops update on whether David Raya will be fit to face Man City

By Lewis Blain | 25 Nov 2026 07:29

Arsenal boss Mikel Arteta has refused to confirm whether David Raya will be available for their Premier League showdown with Manchester City on Sunday afternoon.

The Spaniard missed Tuesday night's 1-1 draw with Borussia Dortmund in the Champions League after picking up a shoulder injury against Newcastle United at the weekend.

Kepa Arrizabalaga deputised at the Emirates Stadium, with Arteta offering his backing to the goalkeeper should Raya remain unavailable this weekend.

Raya left the pitch in significant pain during Arsenal's 2-2 draw with the Magpies on Saturday night, prompting fears that he could face a lengthy spell on the sidelines.

However, subsequent scans proved positive, with the Spanish goalkeeper avoiding a serious injury and not requiring surgery.

There have been suggestions that Raya could only be sidelined for a matter of days and might therefore be in contention to face City, but Arteta was unwilling to offer any guarantees after the Dortmund draw.

"No, we have nothing to add today unfortunately," the Arsenal manager said (via the Evening Standard). "We need to know first how bad it is and whether he has a chance or not [to face Man City]."

Arsenal will therefore have to wait for further clarity on their first-choice goalkeeper, with Kepa potentially required to retain his place against Enzo Maresca's side, who also drew at home to Napoli this midweek.

Kepa produced a reasonably solid display in Germany, with Arteta describing his performance as "really good" and insisting that Arsenal fully trust their goalkeepers.

The Spaniard made three saves and received a 7.5 Sofascore rating, making him the Gunners' third-best performer on the night. His expected goals prevented figure of 0.38 also reflected a positive contribution.

There were, however, a few moments that offered cause for concern. Kepa was wrong-footed for Dortmund's goal, while he parried a disallowed effort back into a dangerous area and did not look as assured as Raya when dealing with crosses.

Arteta is nevertheless confident in his deputy, saying: "We fully trust our keepers and if he needs to play against City, he will play."

It is encouraging that Kepa has Arteta's backing, but there would understandably be some apprehension about him starting against a side of City's calibre. Raya's command of his penalty area and reliability have made him an important figure for Arsenal, and his absence would be a significant setback.

However, if the first-choice goalkeeper is not ready, Kepa will have to step up when called upon.

#1641. Liverpool tee up deal for Senegal wonderkid as transfer ‘option’ agreed

Liverpool have successfully negotiated the option to sign Senegal wonderkid Sidy Barhama Ndiaye once he turns 18.

Ndiaye, currently 16, trialled with Liverpool’s academy in the summer of 2025 and now has a clear pathway to Merseyside.

Per reports from The Athletic, the Reds have pipped a number of European rivals to get right of first refusal for his signing in January 2028.

English clubs cannot sign players from overseas until they have turned 18, which Ndiaye will do on New Year’s Eve in 2027.

Ndiaye currently plies his trade in his home nation with Diambars FC, whom he helped earn promotion to the Senegalese top flight last season.

Ndiaye is currently away at the Under-17 World Cup in Qatar, picking up a goal and two assists in a 9-0 drubbing of Cuba earlier this week.

Senegal’s only other match at the tournament so far resulted in a 1-1 draw with Croatia. Liverpool fans hoping to get a glimpse of a future star, though, might be tempted to tune into their meeting with Tajikistan on Thursday, November 26.

Liverpool have made a habit of spotting talent at such tournaments. At last year’s U17 World Cup, their scouts brought home Senegal’s Mor Talla Ndiaye, Austria’s Ifeanyi Ndukwe and Belgium’s Lucca Brughmans.

It remains to be seen whether Liverpool will opt to sign Ndiaye in 2028, and what role he might play at the club if they do.

Ndiaye will hope to follow in the footsteps of one of Liverpool’s all-time greats, his countryman Sadio Mane, in making the move to the north-west.

#1640. Martinez likens Ronaldo’s level to Messi, Maradona and Cruyff

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Former Portugal head coach Roberto Martinez said it was a "pleasure" to coach Cristiano Ronaldo, who he believes is on the same level as Diego Maradona, Johan Cruyff and Lionel Messi.

Ronaldo announced his international retirement just days before the most recent break, bringing down the curtain on a glittering career with Portugal.

He is the leading scorer and appearance-maker in the history of men's internationals, plundering 146 goals in 234 games since his Portugal debut in 2003.

His Portugal career ended on a bit of a dour note, as he left the September-October camp early after a falling-out with new boss Jorge Jesus, which resulted in him being handed a 30-day ban by the Portuguese Football Federation (FPF).

During Martinez's tenure, he led Portugal to the quarter-finals of Euro 2024 and won the 2024-25 Nations League but stepped down after their last-16 exit to eventual champions Spain at this year's World Cup.

The Spaniard highlighted just how big a mark Ronaldo made on Portugal's history and had high praise for his former captain.

"For me, it was a pleasure," Martinez said on Amazon Prime when asked about Ronaldo.

"For me and my technical staff, it was a joy to work with him for 37 games. He scored 28 goals [in 37 games under Martinez], and that's probably one of the iconic figures.

"I don't think we will see a player of that stature [again] in Portugal.

"In the last few days, you've had so many subjective opinions about what the player is now, [but] what is not subjective are the stats.

"The way he has impacted the game. We are talking about a player that maybe [is of the level of] Lionel Messi, [Diego] Maradona, Johan Cruyff; those are the stats that a player like Cristiano [has]."

Portugal estará sempre em mim https://t.co/dnFj51rxmh

— Cristiano Ronaldo (@Cristiano) November 5, 2026

Ronaldo retires as the only player to have scored at least 10 goals at both the World Cup (11) and the European Championships (14), with the latter figure being a competition record.

He became the first player to score in six different editions of the World Cup this year, when he helped himself to a brace in a group-stage win over Uzbekistan, and he is also the oldest player to feature in a World Cup knockout-stage match, at the age of 41.

"I don't think you can [surpass his numbers]," Martinez added.

"It's something that you learn with Cristiano; his mindset is not winning something or his motivation wasn't to win the Ballon d'Or.

"His motivation was to be better the next day. His commitment to the game is second to none, and I think the longevity is above any opinion.

"Portugal has a population of 10 million. When Cristiano Ronaldo arrives to the national team [in 2003], [Portugal in] 23-and-a-half seasons have never missed a major tournament.

"That's down to what he brought: the professionalism and his numbers – 234 games [for the national team]."

#1639. Luke McCowan's timely return to form silences Parkhead critics and boosts midfield options

By JOHN MCGARRY, SCOTTISH CHIEF SPORTS FEATURE WRITER

Published: 11:58 EST, 22 November 2026 | Updated: 12:18 EST, 22 November 2026

Almost everyone who has played the game of football at a professional level has experienced a day where they simply can’t do right for doing wrong.

When one heavy touch leads to another and each decision made seems worse than the last one.

Like the buses in his native Greenock, it was Luke McCowan’s misfortune for two such traumatic experiences to arrive in close proximity.

His inept performance as a substitute on a dark night for Celtic in Linz in August will flash through his mind when he’s old and grey.

Handed the opportunity to atone for it with a start in the league game against Rangers at Parkhead the following month, his withdrawal at half-time felt like an act of mercy.

A Celtic supporter all his days, McCowan didn’t have to speak to articulate the depth of his despair in that trying time. Subjected to a barrage of online criticism, the deletion of his social media accounts said enough.

Luke McCowan scored in the 4-1 home victory over St Mirren

Skipper Callum McGregor and McCowan enjoy the victory at full-time

While you could understand why the midfielder would have felt personally responsible for a pair of high-profile losses, there was a lot more to the team’s shortcomings on those occasions than one man performing as if his laces were tied together.

Away to LASK, Celtic were already wilting when he shed his tracksuit. He didn’t stop the slide towards an extraordinary exit from the Champions League but he didn’t instigate it.

At home to Rangers, Celtic were flat and second-best from the outset and remained that way even after McCowan came inside for the second period.

The 28-year-old was not alone in failing to do himself justice on those occasions and in other matches around what was a difficult period for Martin O’Neill’s side. It might just have felt like it.

As shown by his contributions to a side who were capable of winning the title in his first two seasons in Glasgow, McCowan was – and is – a far more accomplished player than those unfortunate episodes suggested.

He wasn’t the first and he won’t be the last player to suffer a crisis of confidence. And despite being no shrinking violet, he would not be human if those experiences didn’t shake him up and lead him to question if he was worthy of wearing the jersey that he always dreamed of.

His display on Saturday should have emphatically answered those inner doubts.

Trusted by his manager to fill the void created by the injury to Mika Baur, McCowan delivered.

Even before he scored to put the game to bed just before half-time, he played smart passes, made intelligent runs and made key interceptions. He looked very much a Celtic player again.

McGregor takes the acclaim from team-mates after scoring Celtic's fourth goal

No one in O’Neill’s side, in fact, did more to ensure that they went up the tunnel at the interval to warm applause.

With Baur’s absence for up to ten weeks already a source of stress to the Celtic manager, Benjamin Nygren’s sore heel would have further disrupted his sleep on Friday night.

Saturday proved to be quite the day for O’Neill’s fringe men, though.

On top of McCowan’s assured display, we witnessed Alex Oxlade-Chamberlain serve up a reminder of why he once wore the jerseys of Arsenal, Liverpool and England.

Playing deeper than McCowan, Oxlade-Chamberlain stretched St Mirren with his pinpoint passing, long and short. He kept the ball in tight areas and made it all look so simple.

He was in the right place at the right time to stroke home Yang Hyun-jun’s cut-back to put his side in front and never put a foot wrong until his legs could give no more.

The cherry on the cake for O’Neill came by way of Joel van den Berg’s debut from the bench.

Having seen the club shell out over £3million to PSV Eindhoven, Celtic supporters were growing a little concerned that the teenager hadn’t yet featured for the first team.

Now fully recovered from an injury, he belatedly caught the eye. Tall, skilful and rangy, he looked the part. Might he have earned himself a call-up to the Europa League squad as a replacement for Baur? You would not be surprised.

Celtic will certainly travel to Portugal to face Torreense on Thursday in optimistic mood after making short work of seeing off the Buddies.

Arriving just before McCowan turned home Kieran Tierney’s cross, Camilo Duran claimed his 14th of the season by bundling in a brilliant assist from the same source. Stationed on the bench throughout, Kasper Hogh wasn’t even afforded a chance to end his 16-game goal drought.

On a good day for a makeshift midfield, Callum McGregor, its mainstay, claimed Celtic’s fourth with a controlled strike after the break.

Sam Johnstone didn’t have a great deal to do, testament to Celtic’s work without the ball. Tierney was excellent for 71 minutes, despite playing the entirety of Scotland’s games with North Macedonia and Switzerland.

The directness and industry of Yang on the right flank was also eye-catching. Omitted from the squad for the second successive match, Haissem Hassan will surely have taken note.

On the other flank, Jota looked like a player who’s threatening to really fire again.

A late run-out for Auston Trusty, the first since the death of his father, was met by warm applause by home fans. O’Neill will certainly need the American in the coming weeks.

While Killian Phillips did spoil Johnstone’s clean sheet by converting a penalty which the keeper gave away, O’Neill would have had few complaints about a display which saw his side create an abundance of opportunities.

It must be said that St Mirren were their own worst enemies. They are proving to be a strange fish under Craig McLeish. Even in defeat, some of their football on Saturday was eye-catching.

Yet again, though, they showed themselves to be a soft touch defensively. They were fortunate not to ship more than four and it’s hardly a new thing, either.

The Buddies haven’t kept a clean sheet since winning by a goal at Rugby Park on September 2. In the ten subsequent matches, they’ve picked the ball out of their net 23 times. It’s becoming a real concern.

While they are more creative and entertaining than when Stephen Robinson was in charge, they could badly do with becoming as hard to beat as they were under their former boss.

They are now just five points above Kilmarnock ahead of their meeting in Paisley this weekend. That would be an opportune moment for it all to come together.

#1638. Man United XI vs Sporting: Starting lineup, confirmed team news, injury latest for Champions League today

The Standard's journalism is supported by our readers. If you click links to other sites on this page, we will earn commission.

Luke Shaw is only fit enough for the bench as Manchester United face Sporting this evening.

The left-back has missed the last eight games across all competitions with a muscular injury, but could make his return in Lisbon.

New head coach Mauricio Pochettino endured a horror start to his Man Utd tenure with a heavy 4-0 defeat by rivals Liverpool in the Premier League on Sunday.

The Red Devils were down to 10 men after just eight minutes at Anfield when Leny Yoro fouled Alexander Isak and received a red card, which has since been overturned following a successful appeal.

United suffered no new injury blows on Merseyside, but the result was “painful” according to Pochettino, and he will be looking to put things right immediately in Europe’s top competition on Wednesday night.

The former Tottenham and Chelsea boss sprung a surprise with the inclusion of Matthijs de Ligt in his starting XI against Liverpool, with the Dutchman having previously been sidelined for a year with a persistent back injury.

The centre-back looked awkward for much of the match, and his selection was scrutinised intensely afterwards.

And he unsurprisingly does not keep his place in Lisbon, with Harry Maguire restored.

That could see Lisandro Martinez plugged in at left-back once more if Shaw is not ready to start, although the Argentine had to shift inside after Yoro’s red card against Liverpool, with Patrick Dorgu then moving back.

Diogo Dalot failed to impress on Sunday and sees himself rotated out for Noussair Mazraoui, while in the engine room, Youri Tielemans was hooked for Mason Mount in the second half. The Belgian keeps his place.

Bryan Mbeumo was the man sacrificed following the early sending off at Liverpool as Pochettino resorted to damage limitation, but the Cameroon international should make a quick return here.

Matheus Cunha led the attack but was replaced by Joshua Zirkzee at half-time. The Brazilian is suspended tonight, however.

On the injury list remain Benjamin Sesko, Marcus Rashford, Carlos Baleba and Manuel Ugarte, while back-up goalkeeper Karl Darlow has also yet to return.

Confirmed Man Utd XI vs Sporting (4-2-3-1): Lammens; Yoro, Maguire, Martinez, Mazraoui; Tielemans, Mainoo; Amad, Fernandes, Mbeumo; Zirkzee

#1637. PSG vs Roma: Luis Enrique issues warning before Roma clash

By Axel Clody | 25 Nov 2026 07:34

Paris Saint-Germain are still coming to terms with the loss of Desire Doue for at least six months because of a serious knee injury, and are making their final preparations to face Roma in the Champions League. One of Luis Enrique's biggest concerns ahead of the game is the red-hot form of Donyell Malen, Roma's top scorer.

At a press conference on Tuesday (24 November), the Spanish manager went out of his way to praise the Dutch forward, who already has 16 goals and four assists in 15 games for Roma this season. Luis Enrique highlighted Malen's improvement since January, when he moved to Italy and developed enormously under Gian Piero Gasperini, forcing Paris Saint-Germain to draw up a special containment plan.

'I am impressed with Donyell Malen and the number of goals he has scored, he has been great this season. Since he started playing as a centre-forward, he has been doing very well. We have to be very careful' - the manager said.

Paris Saint-Germain face Roma on Wednesday (25 November) at 8pm UK time at the Parc des Princes, on matchday five of the league phase. The Spanish boss will try to extend his side's perfect record to stay top of the table, while the Italian manager knows the importance of a surprise result to move towards the knockout phase, as Roma sit 20th with four points.

More than his goalscoring record, the number 14 concerns Luis Enrique because his profile enhances Gasperini's style of play: attacking runs in behind, control of the penalty area and a great ability to finish. Before Malen, Roma suffered from the lack of a player with those characteristics, as neither Artem Dovbyk nor Evan Ferguson had success in the first half of 2025-26.

The solution found by the manager was to use the winter transfer window to take the 27-year-old from Aston Villa, where he had few opportunities as a starter. In England, the Dutchman was used mostly as a winger by Unai Emery, but the Roma boss saw his potential to play in a more central role.

The six-month loan was the turning point for Roma, who climbed from sixth to third in Serie A, securing a return to the Champions League after an eight-year absence. With 14 goals and two assists in 18 league games, Malen was signed permanently from Aston Villa for £23m (€27m).

In 2026-27, thanks to the number 14's fluid partnership with Matias Soule, Paulo Dybala, Wesley, Rodrigo Mora and company, Roma are established in the top four and are Serie A title contenders, sitting second with 30 points, two behind leaders Lazio after 12 matches. Roma have not been Italian champions since 2000-01.

61 shots (30 on target) 26.5 per cent goal conversion rate An average of one goal every 70 minutes An average of 11 successful dribbles per game (52.5 per cent) 39 duels won (41.5 per cent) 10 fouls won Data from Sofascore

Mobility is one of the Dutch forward's trademarks, as he often drops close to team-mates to offer a passing option during build-up and to create space in the opposition defence for others to advance. Out of possession, Malen is also a key part of Roma's pressing to win the ball back in favourable conditions for a shot.

In the best year of his career, the Roma number 14 is the biggest threat to Paris Saint-Germain's defensive system, which knows it cannot afford to slip. Otherwise, Malen is likely to punish the French side with his technical ability and finishing efficiency, even when chances are rare.

Liverpool are without Cody Gakpo and Ryan Gravenberch for their Champions League clash with Club Brugge tonight.

The Dutch duo were both absent for Sunday’s 4-0 thrashing of fierce rivals Manchester United in the Premier League and won’t return as Andoni Iraola’s side head to Belgium on Wednesday.

"I think with Cody it's a soleus injury, it's a muscle injury,” Iraola said at his pre-match press conference. "It's not a big thing but I think we expected that he was out. He's going to be out even for the weekend [against Everton]. It's more predictable.

In Gravenberch’s absence, Trey Nyoni gets the nod in midfield alongside Florian Wirtz.

#1635. GdS: ‘Numbers like Kaka’ – why Rabiot is so important to Milan with renewal imminent

Adrien Rabiot has had an outstanding start to the 2026-27 season, and he is showing absolutely no signs of slowing down.

La Gazzetta dello Sport (seen below) begin a report this morning by pointing out what Rabiot said after Milan’s 5-1 demolition of Frosinone on Sunday: “An assist is better than a goal.” He was the man of the match against Frosinone: five goals were scored, yet none bore his name.

Still, the Frenchman made himself the stand-out performer, thanks to his tireless running, leadership, and a series of decisive passes, not to mention his role in the opening goal, which came via an own-goal.

It was a summer of doubts for Rabiot, given that his extended vacation was interpreted by some as a sign of discontent and a longing to reunite with his former mentor – Massimiliano Allegri – at Napoli. Yet, he has transformed into a cornerstone of this new era.

The former PSG man is now a decisive force on the pitch, integral to Ruben Amorim’s tactical framework, and a true leader. The numbers demonstrate this perfectly: Rabiot is the first midfielder to contribute to at least one goal (scoring or assisting) in seven consecutive Serie A appearances since Kaká in 2004.

With five goals and six assists, he recently became the first midfielder in the last 20 years of Serie A to record more than 10 goal contributions within the first 10 matches of a single season. In total, Rabiot has surpassed the milestone of 50 direct goal involvements in Serie A (29 goals and 22 assists).

Milan trust him, and the feeling is mutual. As previously mentioned, the very fact that he remained with the Rossoneri over the summer – publicly reaffirming his commitment to the club – is reflected in his attitude, both on and off the field.

Adrien Rabiot – Goal Contributions so far

12 G/A in 14 Games https://t.co/s8oTle9GBn

He is always smiling and highly active on social media; his numbers on Instagram are as impressive as his stats on the field. He posts photos of his goals, his celebrations and embraces with Diego Moreira, with whom he is clearly building a close bond.

Amorim said after the game: “Adrien can play as a ’10,’ an attacking midfielder, an ‘8,’ or even as a playmaker – though he doesn’t particularly like that role. He is certainly one of the best players I have ever coached, and one of the best midfielders in Europe.”

Speaking to Telefoot, Rabiot addressed the topic of his excellent start statistically: “It’s a positive thing to have players capable of being decisive, even if they aren’t forwards. It also serves as an encouragement to those around us.

“At Milan, we have quite a few young players, and it’s important for them to have role models in their day-to-day lives. I had only been back from vacation for a week when he was already talking to me about a contract renewal.

“I told him, ‘Coach, take it easy!’ (laughs). But, naturally, it’s significant for a player to feel that kind of trust—the coach relies on us, holds us in high regard, and makes us feel important.”

Further significant remarks regarding Rabiot were made by Gerry Cardinale on the eve of the most recent league match, specifically concerning his imminent contract renewal.

“I love Adrien, he’s one of my favourite players. He’s fantastic. I have enormous respect for him and his family. We are in talks, and I hope we reach a happy conclusion soon. I believe he should be a signature player for Milan. Could it be a Christmas gift for the fans? Absolutely, and for me, too.”

The renewal will happen, and it will happen soon. Any delay until the new year should not be interpreted as a negative sign. Rather, it reflects the fact that everything is already settled, and there is no rush to finalise the signature.

Adrien’s current deal – which runs until 2028 – will be extended to 2030, with an additional one-year option. From his current age of 31, he will remain a fixture in the Rossoneri midfield until he is 33 or 34, the prime of his footballing maturity.

Now into his thirties, he will also earn a more lucrative contract than his current one, which pays him €3.5m net per season. It is worth noting that in the summer of 2025, Adrien was acquired from Marseille for €7m after a training-ground altercation with Jonathan Rowe.

It was, by any definition, a fantastic deal. As for the future, Rabiot has a role model he can observe from very close quarters: “Modrić trains as if he were 21, he’s an example to follow. The closer you get to the end of your career, the more you start to savor every moment. I try to do the same.”

With the imminent contract extension, Adrien Rabiot is also set to conclude his career in the red and black colours, and that would make everyone happy.

#1634. Is Matheus Cunha injured? Why Manchester United star isn’t in squad to face Sporting

Mauricio Pochettino will not be able to call on Matheus Cunha as he chases his first win with Manchester United.

The Red Devils’ new boss is facing just his second match in charge of the club as he looks to bounce back from the weekend’s chastening 4-0 defeat by Liverpool.

He will return to the Champions League for the first time since leaving Paris Saint-Germain this evening, with a tricky tie away at Sporting on the docket.

However, in a selection blow, he will not be able to make use of one of his more threatening forwards, with Cunha left out of the Lisbon-bound travelling squad.

There was some positive news in the squad, though, as Luke Shaw and Karl Darlow came back into contention after injury layoffs, but the absence of Cunha is a serious setback for Pochettino as he looks to breathe life into his nascent United tenure.

Matheus Cunha was left out of the travelling squad for Manchester United’s meeting with Sporting as he is serving a red card suspension.

The Brazilian forward was dismissed in second-half injury time as United came from behind to beat Roma 3-2 last time out in the Champions League.

Having trailed by two goals to nil with just 17 minutes played, a second-half penalty from Bruno Fernandes and a quickfire brace from Cunha flipped the script.

Cunha, though, was shown two yellow cards in a chaotic finish.

The first came when he removed his shirt celebrating what proved to be the winning goal, and he picked up a second in the 91st minute for a needless, reckless late tackle on Leonardo Balerdi.

He will serve his suspension against Sporting tonight and be available again when United host RB Leipzig in two weeks’ time, on December 8.

#1633. 'The main problem' - Enzo Maresca defends surprise Man City tactical decision after 2-2 Napoli draw

By Lewis Blain | 25 Nov 2026 07:48

Manchester City boss Enzo Maresca has explained some of his unexpected selection and tactical decisions after his side were held to a 2-2 draw by Napoli at the Etihad Stadium on Tuesday evening.

The result saw City twice come from behind, but their defensive problems continued as they dropped further points in the Champions League.

Maresca also acknowledged that his side are still searching for the right balance between attacking and defending following his arrival as Pep Guardiola's successor.

Maresca left Jeremy Doku and Iliman Ndiaye on the bench for the opening hour, while Phil Foden was also rested, prompting questions about his selection.

The City boss explained that his decisions were based on how he expected Napoli to set up, with the visitors having recently used a 3-5-2 or 3-5-1-1 formation.

"We expected Napoli to play 3-5-2 or 3-5-1-1 as they did in recent matches, so that would basically leave eight players in the middle, and hope to create more spaces down the wings," Maresca told Sky Sport Italia.

He wanted Rayan Cherki to operate out wide and exploit those spaces, although City struggled to turn their possession into enough chances during the first half.

Maresca also defended his decision to use Ayyoub Bouaddi in a deeper midfield role alongside Elliott Anderson, explaining that he wanted to maintain balance while allowing six players to attack.

However, the manager admitted that City's defensive shortcomings remain a significant concern.

"The main problem is that we are conceding too many goals, and we need to do something about that," he added.

Maresca also acknowledged that finding the right approach would take time, comparing City's transition to the challenges Arsenal and Manchester United experienced following the departures of Arsene Wenger and Sir Alex Ferguson.

It is not unusual for Maresca to rotate his City side during midweek fixtures, but leaving Doku, Ndiaye and Foden out of the starting lineup for a potentially important Champions League match was still a notable decision.

City ultimately rescued a point, but the draw could prove costly in their hopes of progressing in the competition, particularly given their recent struggles for consistency.

Perhaps Maresca also had this weekend's showdown with Premier League title rivals Arsenal in mind, with City travelling to the Emirates for Sunday's late kick-off.

That is not to suggest the manager deliberately sacrificed the Napoli fixture, but resting Foden and keeping two dangerous wide players in reserve could indicate that he was considering the demands of a huge domestic encounter.

City need to find greater defensive stability regardless of the opposition, as Maresca himself acknowledged, but Sunday's meeting with the Gunners may have been a factor in how he approached his midweek selection.

Published: 12:40 EST, 22 November 2026 | Updated: 12:40 EST, 22 November 2026

Tuur Rommens has urged his Rangers team-mates to use a breakneck run of three home games in eight days to build a platform from which to launch a real assault on the Premiership title.

Derek McInnes’ side play host to Aberdeen on Tuesday and then have Falkirk and Dundee United visiting – with Belgian left-back Rommens clear on the need to use the Ibrox atmosphere as a weapon.

‘At the away games, there’s a lot of fans, but at home there’s even more, so it gives an extra boost,’ he said.

Tuur Rommens (right) celebrates with match-winner Ryan Naderi at Fir Park

‘I guess Aberdeen, it’s a difficult one, but we’ll try to keep on winning.’

#1631. Mauricio Pochettino explains surprise Manchester United squad decision for Sporting clash: ‘Great opportunity’

Mauricio Pochettino has explained his decision to hand Joshua Zirkzee a first start of the season against Sporting in the Champions League.

The Argentine named just his second United team in Lisbon on Wednesday evening as he looked to bounce back from a damning 4-0 defeat by Liverpool on his managerial bow.

In Portugal, he made four changes from the side he named at Anfield, with Harry Maguire, Noussair Mazraoui and Amad Diallo all coming into the side.

Perhaps his most notable call, though, saw striker Zirkzee chosen to lead the line, making his first start of the campaign.

The Dutchman has been bumped up the pecking order somewhat for this match, with fellow striker Benjamin Sesko out injured and deputy Matheus Cunha suspended.

Pochettino, though, said he hopes Zirkzee can kick on as a more dependable option, given United’s thin ranks.

Asked to explain the selection, he told TNT Sports: “Cunha is suspended, of course, Sesko is injured. I think it is a great opportunity for Josh (Zirkzee) to show his quality.

“I think it is an important game to start to think that he can be a very important player for the team, and today is an opportunity for him.”

Zirkzee was entirely peripheral under Michael Carrick and had looked to leave United in the summer transfer window. He was the subject of a loan bid from Everton on Deadline Day, but no move materialised.

Pochettino, though, seems optimistic he can bring Zirkzee in from the cold as United look to salvage their campaign, both domestically and abroad.

#1629. Alexander Isak closes in on Mohamed Salah record with latest Liverpool goal

Alexander Isak is closing in on a record held by Mohamed Salah with his latest Liverpool goal.

The Swedish striker did not take long to open the scoring as Liverpool faced Club Brugge in the Champions League on Wednesday night.

Bradley Barcola won the ball high up the pitch to set the Reds on the attack and Dominik Szoboszlai teed Isak up to finish from close range.

It was a significant goal for Isak, who has now scored in six consecutive away matches for Liverpool.

It is a feat that very few men have bettered. According to the stat gurus at Opta, no Liverpool player has ever scored in more than seven consecutive away appearances.

Salah is the current record holder, and should Isak find the back of the net in this weekend’s Merseyside derby at the Hill Dickinson Stadium, he would equal the Egyptian king’s record. Add another against Chelsea at Stamford Bridge on December 5, and he could surpass it.

Prior to the launch of the Premier League, Sam English, John Evans and John Aldridge all scored in seven consecutive away matches.

Salah called time on his Liverpool career at the end of last season, leaving with 257 goals and 123 assists across 442 appearances.

He now plies his trade in Turkey with Trabzonspor, where he has made a bright start to life, tallying 16 goal contributions in his first 17 appearances.

#1627. Man Utd defender can 'pack his bags' in January as key Mauricio Pochettino transfer decision looms

By Lewis Blain | 25 Nov 2026 08:07

Noussair Mazraoui could be heading towards the Manchester United exit door when the January transfer window opens.

AC Milan are considering a move for the Morocco international as they look to strengthen their defensive options under former Red Devils boss Ruben Amorim.

However, any potential departure will depend on Mauricio Pochettino's assessment of the 29-year-old over the coming weeks.

Mazraoui has experienced mixed fortunes since joining United from Bayern Munich, with injury problems restricting him to fewer than 1,000 Premier League minutes last season.

His fitness has improved this term, and he has featured six times in the league, partly because of injuries to United's other full-back options.

However, his long-term future at Old Trafford is now uncertain, with AC Milan reportedly keeping tabs on his situation.

According to reports in Italy (via Sport Witness), Milan have discussed Mazraoui's profile with their transfer team as they consider defensive reinforcements under Amorim.

The Portuguese coach has regularly used a back four this season and could view the United defender as an attractive option because of his ability to operate on either side.

There is reportedly a belief that Mazraoui could 'pack his bags in January', with the Serie A giants potentially open to pursuing a deal.

However, everything hinges on Pochettino's plans for the player. The Argentine is yet to make a final decision, with the next few weeks expected to help determine whether Mazraoui is allowed to leave.

United have several areas of the squad requiring attention, and selling Mazraoui could provide Pochettino with additional funds to work with in January.

The Argentine is believed to have a budget of just £50m, with the club expected to make only two additions unless significant circumstances change.

With central defence, left-back and striker all potential priorities, every extra contribution to the transfer kitty could prove valuable.

Mazraoui has not consistently established himself in one position at Old Trafford, and a departure could benefit all parties if Milan are prepared to offer a reasonable fee.

United should not allow sentiment to get in the way of a sensible decision. If Pochettino does not see Mazraoui as an important part of his plans, cashing in during January could help fund reinforcements elsewhere.

There is still a decision to be made, but with multiple positions needing attention, every little helps.

#1626. CM: Milan considered Maresa before Man City move – the background

Ruben Amorim became the AC Milan head coach in the summer, but he was far from the only name the management considered.

Calciomercato.com have published a report revealing some of the background on Enzo Maresca, who became Manchester City’s new manager on July 1st after an incredible successful decade under the iconic Pep Guardiola.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Maresca signed a contract until June 2029, but he confirmed in a press conference on the eve of the Champions League match against Napoli that he could have been the manager of an Italian team today instead.

“In March, April, and May, there were contacts with an Italian team, but not with Napoli. I never spoke to the president of Napoli, I never spoke to anyone,” said the coach, a native of the province of Salerno.

Continuing in that press conference, the former Leicester City and Chelsea boss spoke rather intriguingly about the possibility of returning to work in Italy one day.

“You never know. I’m delighted to be here, because this is a great club, an organization that has had three coaches in the last 17 years. This shows how differently we work, compared to my country. For Italian football, however, I say there’s no single solution,” he said.

“If we’re where we are, something needs to change. We need to be a little more courageous. Every time we miss a World Cup or a European Championship, people say everything needs to change, and then nothing ever changes.”

Excluding Napoli – who last spring were already aware of Antonio Conte’s desire to leave – which club or clubs might have contacted Maresca shortly before the end of last season?

Maresca was one of the candidates Gerry Cardinale’s Milan considered, the report claims. The Rossoneri owner made it clear early in his search that he was looking for a coach capable of playing a dominant and attacking style of football.

Names like Andoni Iraola (who ended up at Liverpool) were also floated, but in the end Cardinale opted to go with Ruben Amorim, another coach with ties to Manchester given he had been sacked by United a few months prior.

The other avenue leads to Fiorentina, where Fabio Paratici was looking for a coach with different characteristics than Paolo Vanoli. La Viola’s sporting director had his eye on Maresca, but ultimately the courtship of City and being Guardiola’s successor was too appealing.

#1624. Rangers must find their shooting boots quicker to prevent the need to dig themselves out of needless holes

Published: 12:52 EST, 22 November 2026 | Updated: 13:26 EST, 22 November 2026

Derek McInnes chose to dress up the poor level of chance conversion from his Rangers side as something for those insistent on dwelling on the negatives at the end of a last-gasp win over Motherwell.

That’s fair enough. He wants to keep the energy up. He wants to place the focus, instead, on a 13-game unbeaten run. He wants to make more of the fact his team are capable of digging in and getting wins over the line by hook or by crook even when it isn’t going exactly to plan.

It’s a form of motivation, and motivating people doesn’t always come through hammering on about their deficiencies. The truth is this, though: you really shouldn’t be needing a scrappy 88th-minute winner courtesy of a couple of jammy deflections in a game which has seen you deliver 29 shots on goal with 11 of those on target.

Yes, Motherwell keeper Alex Paulsen had a good night. One double save from substitute Findlay Curtis and Dujon Sterling in the 85th minute was quite exceptional. This, however, wasn’t quite the superhuman display from the Kiwi that many were making it out to be.

A lot of the saves he made were straightforward. Too often, Rangers blazed efforts high and wide. They dominated the first quarter of this game until Jake Girdwood-Reich cancelled out Manny Fernandez’s early opener, lost their rhythm a bit, as they are wont to do, and then ran the show completely in the second half.

They should have won by a country mile and it is necessary to look into why they didn’t.

Ryan Naderi rejoices in scoring Rangers' late winner against Motherwell

Emmanuel Fernandez broke the deadlock on eight minutes at Fir Park

McInnes was justified in being happy with many aspects of his side’s performance at Fir Park. Ryan Naderi did put in a strong display as he spearheaded the frontline, although he did miss two gilt-edged chances before settling it late on with an untidy effort that deflected off Martin Moormann — who had already blocked a Badredine Bouanani shot — and landed in the net.

The Czech international is developing a reputation for important goals that are getting Rangers out of the mire — and keeping them in contention for the title — but McInnes needs infinitely more in terms of numbers from those around him.

Not xG or pass completion or any of those niche interests. Goals and assists is what we’re talking about here. The stuff that really changes games and puts points on the board.

First in the dock on this front, talented individuals that really need to be held to account, are attackers Minsu Kim and Bouanani. Listen, McInnes has already spoken plenty on the need for both of them to deliver more in those key metrics. He obviously doesn’t want to come across as a stuck record.

Both players are technically proficient. They are exciting. The view from this vantage point is that they very definitely do have it in them to be gamechangers, but they’re starting to get a little bit annoying now.

Thanks to the corner that set up Fernandez for the opening goal, Minsu, who started in a more central role with Kevin Kelsy being benched, does have one assist on the board finally. That’s a pretty grim return, though, from 15 appearances.

Particularly worrying from the South Korean was his reaction when presented with a golden opportunity to break his scoring duck just before the hour. Naderi teed him up perfectly with a pass to the left. Minsu had time to control the ball and pick his spot.

His sclaffed effort, easily saved by Paulsen at the near post, was atrocious. It reeked of a guy short of confidence in the final third and growing progressively more anxious about getting his name on the scoresheet. Maybe he’s just trying too hard, but he needs to get the finger out, keep the mind calm and start taking the heat off the likes of Naderi and Kelsy with some major contributions.

Same goes for Bouanani. His late effort did, at least, lead to Naderi’s winner, albeit more through accident than design, but his record reads one goal and one assist in 10 appearances. He’s a dangerous, tricky winger. He beats people for fun. He should be doing more than this.

Djeidi Gassama, a more limited player than Minsu or Bouanani, started against Motherwell and does have five assists to his name, but he’s only managed one goal, in a 5-1 League Cup rout of St Mirren.

Meanwhile, Findlay Curtis has no goals and no assists from 15 outings, although only five of those have been first-team starts.

That’s four blokes who play along the frontline and they’ve managed two goals between them. You do the maths on that.

Derek McInnes was delighted at full-time but Rangers should have won with more comfort

There are others throughout the team, though, who can be doing more to make life easier from a goalscoring perspective.

Fernandez announced himself as a real threat from set-pieces last season. He’s a real weapon in the air. Saturday’s goal was his first this term. Rangers need to do better at harnessing what he brings in an attacking context from dead-ball situations.

A few more in the way of goal interventions from midfield would be welcome, too. Dan Neil can finish. He showed that with those two spectacular goals against Celtic in the 3-0 Premier Sports Cup win at Ibrox in September.

In his 17 other outings outwith that match, however, he has only scored once and delivered one assist. He had a brilliant chance at Fir Park just after the interval and slid it wide of the far post.

Nico Raskin, meanwhile, has one goal and no assists to his name.

He put one great chance from a header wide in the second half. Then he blazed over from a promising position after releasing Bouanani out wide with a super diagonal ball and running a ridiculous distance to latch onto the return.

McInnes insists he’s never seen a squad practise crossing and shooting like this one. However much they are doing in training at Auchenhowie, they need to bring it to matchdays.

Everything is there for Rangers this season. There are definitely promising signs in their overall play while Celtic, of course, are poorly run from a footballing perspective with an OAP manager, and a fanbase in open revolt against the board.

Rangers now have a run of six games from eight at home that could — and should — be a real platform for a serious title bid.

They just have to wake up to the fact that depending on Naderi to drag them out of a hole and drag them over the line again and again and again is simply not a sustainable way of working.

Motherwell (4-2-3-1): PAULSEN 8.5; Sparrow 7, Girdwood-Reich 7, Moormann 7, Longelo 6; Fadinger 6, Priestman 6; Maswanhise 6, Said 5 (Charles-Cook 15 (Kanga 63)), Hodge 5 (Bjorgolfsson 86); Palmer-Houlden 5 (Hendry 63). Booked: Hendry. Manager: Alfred Johansson 6.

Rangers (4-2-3-1): Pandur 7; Sterling 7, Fernandez 7, Makhanya 6, Rommens 6; Raskin 7, Neil 6.5 (Chukwuani 86); Bouanani 7, Minsu 6.5 (Curtis 78), Gassama 6 (Kelsy 69); Naderi 7.5. Booked: Naderi. Manager: Derek McInnes 7.

#1623. Report: Liverpool transfer target is '100% out' in January, he'll cost €50m

Liverpool aren't in the best run of form at the moment.

The Reds are miles away from first-placed Arsenal and, right now, it doesn't feel like they have the quality among their ranks to get back to the top of the Premier League table.

Fans expected Liverpool to be challenging for the title this season, especially after their £150 million + spend in the summer.

That obviously hasn't worked out with fans now questioning whether the club even has enough strength among their ranks to get them where they need to be.

Right now, the January transfer window is just over a month away and, fans are expecting a lot of change to take place.

So, the fact that one of their reported targets are '100%' on their way out of Anfield is a very good sign.

Barcelona are '100%' going to sell Alejandro Balde in January

Since the arrival of Ronald Araujo, Liverpool's defence has been fairly solid.

The Uruguayan has brought an extra layer of stability to Andoni Iraola's ranks and has helped take a lot of pressure off the shoulders of Jeremy Jacquet.

Thanks to how strong Araujo has been, Jacquet has been allowed to take his time to settle into Premier League life and, he's probably been one of Liverpool's best signings thanks to that.

Right now, it's unclear what the Reds' priorities are going to be in January but, thanks to an update from journalist Juan Jesus, a bit of a better insight has now been given to fans.

"Despite Deco’s words, Alejandro Balde is 100% out. Several clubs know this and are closely monitoring his situation, including Manchester United, PSG, AC Milan and Liverpool," he shared via X.

"Barça expects the bidding to drive up the price and is confident of securing his departure for at least 45–50 million euros."

Alejandro Balde's new price tag is expensive

When talk of Liverpool being linked with Balde first emerged, the deal was pitched as an unmissable offer for the Reds.

Talk of a deal worth around £30 million was being mooted with other clubs such as Manchester United also linked with an interest.

However, the fact that the deal could end up costing around €50 million (£41.9 million) makes things a little harder to understand.

Obviously, Balde is an incredible player and would help solve two of the Reds' main issues going into 2027.

But, £41.9 million is a lot of money for the club to spend on another left-back.

Everyone thought that Milos Kerkez was going to be the second coming of Andy Robertson after he was signed for £40 million but, in reality, he still needs to do a lot of work to improve his game.

Right now, it's unclear what plans Liverpool have for the upcoming transfer window but, if they don't make a couple of meaningful signings, by the end of the 2026-27 season, they'll be fighting for a Champions League place, rather than the title.

#1622. Liverpool vs Arsenal Preview: Team News, Tactics, Lineups and Prediction

Home » Home 2 » Liverpool vs Arsenal Preview: Team News, Tactics, Lineups and Prediction

Table-toppers Arsenal travel to Anfield tonight with their first Premier League trophy since the ‘invincibles’ season of 2004 in sight. The Gunners top the table and with stuttering performances from Manchester City and a Leicester City whose fairytale run seems at an end, and are in pole position to finish the current campaign as champions.

While Jurgen Klopp’s men are still finding their way inconsistently since his appointment, Arsenal are in top form with five victories out of their last six matches. In comparison, Liverpool have been as easy to predict as a magic 8 ball, with impressive wins over Leicester City and Manchester City, but accompanied with horrific losses against Watford and West Ham. With fourth place still within grasp and with an impressive record against the table topping teams this season, Liverpool would look to give their long suffering fans some cheer with which to greet this New Year.

The Reds desperately need a victory to steady the ship as their erratic and wayward form sees them enter 2016 still outside the top 4 and distant from any title challenge.

With a host of injuries to his main XI, Jurgen Klopp could be forgiven for dipping into the transfer market so early. The Reds have captured QPR right-back Steven Caulker along with Marko Grujic in the January transfer window.

With Grujic returning to his former club Red Star Belgrade on loan, Steven Caulker is likely to be given a run out as a substitute with the current spate of Liverpool injuries.

Ings, Sturridge, Lovren, Coutinho, Origi and Flanagan are amongst the Liverpool afflicted and will take no part in the match ahead. With Lovren out, Kolo Toure and Mamadou Sakho look likely to be Klopp’s first choice central defending partnership.

Alberto Moreno and Nathaniel Clyne should start as full-backs for the Liverpool side and will be crucial in any attempt to penetrate the Gunner’s defences. Emre Can and Lucas should marshal the midfield, while James Milner, Firmino and Adam Lallana look to give Petr Cech some concerns about his goal. Leading the line should be Christian Benteke, who’s lack of form doesn’t threaten this match as manager Klopp has few options in his position.

Probable Starting XI (4-5-1): Mignolet; Clyne, Sakho, Toure, Moreno; Lucas, Can, Firmino, Lallana, Milner, Benteke.

Arsenal must show that they have the one quality required of all champions : Consistency. The task is hereby straightforward for Wenger’s men. Win, keep winning, regardless of your manner and the title is yours.

With half the season concluded, Arsene Wenger must be wishing that he received a Christmas gift from the Arsenal medical team. Injuries have decimated his midfield with Wilshire, Cazorla, Rosiscky, Coquelin and Sanchez out of the game.

There is some good news with Mesul Ozil having managed to partake in some leisure instead of participating in the FA cup victory over Sunderland. Keeping the nimble playmaker fit would be key to Arsenal aspirations, both in this match and for the remainder of the season.

With both Petr Mertersacker and Gabriel available, it would be interesting to see whom Arsene Wenger picks out for his starting XI. Koscielny, Bellerin and Monreal have nailed down their place in the defence and the inclusion of the slower Mertersacker or the inconsistent Gabriel may have a defining moment in the game.

With Arsenal’s midfield woes, it should fall to Flamini to screen the defence with Ramsey alongside him. Walcott, Ozil and Joel Campbell should be the main thrusts of Arsenal’s attacking play with Giroud as the elegant, decisive focus.

Probable Starting XI (4-5-1): Cech; Bellerin, Gabriel, Koscielny, Monreal; Flamini, Ramsey, Ozil, Walcott, Campbell; Girourd.

With previous encounters between these teams resulting in high scoring draws, we favour a repeat of last year’s epic 2-2 result for the same fixture. Martin Skrtel’s 97th minute header in front of the Kop capped a memorable game which also had Fabio Borini sent off and we expect similar fireworks at Anfield tomorrow.

#1618. Journalist: Andoni Iraola refused to strike deal for World Cup star

Liverpool head coach Andoni Iraola reportedly refused to strike a deal for a World Cup star over the summer. He got his wish - and was absolutely right.

Andoni Iraola didn't have the easiest job when he took over as Liverpool head coach in the summer. He inherited a squad that was incredibly expensive - by far the most in the Reds' history - but wasn't playing well.

Wasn't playing well at all, actually. Liverpool's points last season were generated through individual efforts rather than team play, surviving on the fact they had more talent than their opponents.

The potential was always massive, then, but the pressure was high and it was completely unclear if the group could actually play together. Moreover, Liverpool intended to spend even more over the summer and would lost some incredibly important players.

It's now November and we're still completely unclear whether this group can play together. But things are promising. And you've got to say that some of that promise is thanks to Iraola putting his foot down.

Alisson Becker's contract technically expired last summer, but Liverpool triggered an option in the deal that extended it for an extra year. Their plan at one stage appeared to be that they'd extent it so they could sell Alisson for a bit of money before they lost him for free.

Juventus were heavily interested in signing Alisson. It certainly appeared that a deal would go through, too, only for things to fizzle out and for the goalkeeper to remain with Liverpool this season.

It appears that Iraola played a large role in that happening. Journalist Nicolo Schira reports that Iraola considered Alisson to be non-transferrable and wouldn't let him depart the club.

What a decision that was. Alisson has had a tremendous start to the season, firmly re-establishing himself as no.1 and one of the best goalkeepers on the planet right now.

On top of that, Iraola kept one of the most experienced players at the club - something incredibly important with all this turnover each summer. It was unquestionably the correct decision.

And one that looks like it might result in committing to more years of Alisson. Schira says that Liverpool are in talks to get a new contract signed, potentially extending things to 2029. And to say we're behind that decision would be an understatement.

#1617. FIFA Slaps Real Madrid, Atletico Madrid With 1-Year Transfer Bans

Home » Home 2 » FIFA Slaps Real Madrid, Atletico Madrid With 1-Year Transfer Bans

The ban will start from the July transfer window this year and finish with the January transfer market in 2017.

Atletico were also fined 900,000 Swiss francs (820,000 euros) and Real 360,000 (330,000 euros).

“The two clubs were found to have violated several provisions concerning the international transfer and first registration of minor players as well as other relevant provisions with regard to the registration and participation of certain players in competitions,” said a FIFA statement.

Barcelona has just ended a one year ban for similar reasons.

Real and Atletico were “issued with a reprimand and given 90 days in which to regularise the situation of all minor players concerned,” FIFA said. They can still sell players during the transfer ban.

FIFA said the alarm was raised over the two clubs by FIFA’s Transfer Matching System and its disciplinary committee completed the inquiry.

Under international football rules, players under 18 cannot be transferred to another country, except in limited circumstances. All transfers need the approval of a special FIFA committee.

“The investigations concerned minor players who were involved and participated in competitions with the clubs over various periods between 2007 and 2014 (Atletico Madrid) and between 2005 and 2014 (Real Madrid),” FIFA said.

The ban follows a similar sanction handed to European champions Barcelona, who were unable to register new players during 2015.

Barca were initially banned in April 2014, but managed to delay the sanction taking affect until the transfer windows in January and the summer 2015 by launching an ultimately unsuccessful appeal to the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS).

By delaying the ban, Barca managed to sign the likes of Luis Suarez and Ivan Rakitic in the summer of 2014 to propel them to a treble of La Liga, Champions League and Copa del Rey.

The news is just the latest institutional embarassment for Real Madrid just over a week after they appointed French legend Zinedine Zidane.

Madrid have sacked two Champions League winning coaches in Carlo Ancelotti and Rafael Benitez in the past seven months, as well as being thrown out of the Copa del Rey for fielding an ineligible player.

The sanction could also be bad news for the likes of Paris Saint-Germain and Manchester United, who had targeted Madrid stars Cristiano Ronaldo and Gareth Bale with Real highly unlikely to dispose of their best players without the chance to sign suitable replacements.

La Liga leaders Atletico Madrid’s usually hectic transfer policy will also be put on hold. However, Diego Simeone’s men look better placed to cope with the ban having invested heavily in young talent over the past year.

Neither Real no Atletico made an immediate comment on whether they would appeal.

#1615. Yang believes Celtic can defy the odds with history-making move into the Europa League knock-out phase

By JOHN MCGARRY, SCOTTISH CHIEF SPORTS FEATURE WRITER

Published: 13:39 EST, 22 November 2026 | Updated: 13:49 EST, 22 November 2026

Yang Hyun-jun is predicting that Celtic can make Europa League history by bouncing back from a dismal start in the group stage to qualify.

Since the competition was revamped by UEFA in 2024, no side have made it through to the knock-out round having lost their first three games.

With defeats to Ferencvaros, Benfica and Celta Vigo arriving in quick succession, Martin O’Neill’s men looked to be heading for an early exit.

After beating Besiktas last time out, however, they are still in with a shout when matchday five takes them to Portugal to face Torreense on Thursday.

Winger Yang, who made his first start since early September in the win over St Mirren on Saturday, feels there’s a growing belief among the players they can yet emulate last season’s feat of reaching the play-off round.

‘Can we make history? Of course,’ he said. ‘We believe we can qualify. We are getting better all the time. You could see that against Besiktas.

Yang made his first start since early September in Celtic's victory over St Mirren on Saturday

Martin O'Neill aims to keep Celtic's Europa League hopes alive by beating Torreense this week

‘They are a very good team, and that has given us the belief that we can go to the next round. It’s important to take it game-by-game, though. This is the most important one. If we can get the points we can go on from there, step-by-step.’

Torreense made history last season by becoming the first second-tier team to win the Portuguese Cup and qualify for Europe. Despite currently sitting 13th in that division, they have confounded expectations by taking six points from four Europa League games.

‘We are playing against a Portuguese second division team but we have to be focused and aggressive,’ warned Yang. ‘They are higher than us in the Europa League table. They’ve already won two matches so they will be a good team.

‘We have to approach it the same way as we would playing a team like Benfica or Sporting Lisbon. We have to go there and try to win. If we play like we did against St Mirren, we can do it.’

Meanwhile, Yang is adamant that being made exempt from military service wasn’t even on his mind as South Korea won the Asian Games this year.

Played in Japan in September and October, Yang’s side defeated the hosts 1-0 in the final.

That meant all the South Korean players were no longer obliged to spend time serving in the military before they turn 28.

Yang, 24, who suffered a hamstring injury in the opening victory against Qatar, reflected: ‘It was great. Obviously, it was nice to win it but I also got injured, which was unfortunate.

‘I was trying to be around the team, to help in any way I could.

‘It wasn’t really about the national service. Everyone was playing for the team, the country and the fans.

‘We managed to get the victory. Being exempt from national service was just a bonus, I guess.

‘The celebrations were enjoyable. It’s the first time my national team have won the Asian Games.

‘It was really hard — especially the game against Japan. It was a great achievement.’

Andoni Iraola and Julian Ward have cast their net far and wide to find new players for Liverpool to target.

This inconsistency among Liverpool's ranks has massively impacted the way that things have gone for them this season.

Right now, they're fourth in the Premier League table but, if they want to get back to the top and start challenging for silverware, they're going to have to spend even more money.

Liverpool and Manchester City want to sign Yunus Akgun

One area that Liverpool heavily focused on improving in the summer was their attack.

Bradley Barcola and Victor Munoz were signed in the summer transfer window just gone and, the season before that, Alexander Isak, Hugo Ekitike and Florian Wirtz were all brought in.

#1610. Sampdoria swept aside by rampant Napoli – are the Partenopei on course for their first Scudetto in 26 years?

Home » Home 2 » Sampdoria swept aside by rampant Napoli – are the Partenopei on course for their first Scudetto in 26 years?

Dries Mertens celebrating with his team-mates on the touchline after his decisive goal in the 4-2 victory at Sampdoria is typical of the spirit and togetherness that has seen Napoli storm to the top of the Serie A title. It was in dedication to Chelsea loanee Nathaniel Chabolah who recently lost his mother a a nice touch to show that there is much more to life than football, even though they have put themselves in a wonderful position to end Juventusa dominance and end a 26-year wait for the Scudetto.

Five straight wins have put Maurizio Sarria s team two points clear at the top, with the former Empoli manager breathing a new lease of life throughout a team that have always looked capable of competing for the title, yet ultimately fallen short when the pressure to deliver grew. He has transformed the entire dynamics of how Napoli play, with clinical attacking movement combined with a rock-solid defence within a 4-3-3 system that is getting the very best from the players at his disposal. This seasona s statistics proved that point; Napoli are far and away the highest scorers in Serie A this season, while only Inter Milan and Juventus have a better defensive record. Just one defeat in the twenty league games since the opening day loss at Sassuolo is another illustration of just how good Napoli have been this season, with the crushing 4-0 win at AC Milan in early October a sign of what the Partenopei are truly capable of.

Juventus were always likely to be favourites for the Scudetto on Coral and any other football odds site as their dominance of Italian football threatens to extend into its fifth season, so it is perhaps refreshing from a purista s perspective that Napoli have emerged as real contenders to challenge the Bianconeri. Massimo Allegria s side have stormed up the table in ominous fashion following a surprisingly slow start to the season, with eleven straight victories serving a serious warning to Napoli that they will make them fight all the way for the 2015/2016 Serie A title. It remains to be seen how Sarri and his team handle the pressure of having Juventus breathing down their necks, but the fact they have scored twelve goals in their last three games would indicate that

Some may have been surprised by Gonzalo Higuaina s decision to swap Real Madrid for Naples in the summer of 2013, but the 28-year-old has become one of the most feared strikers in Italy. The Argentine international has formed a wonderful strikeforce at the front of a three-man attack, with Jose Callejon and Lorenzo Insigne adding searing pace and skill on either side of a frontman who has made a career from being a true predator inside the box.

Twenty-one games in as many Serie A games this season puts him amongst the most in-form strikers in world football, with his clinical finish which opened the scoring against Sampdoria proving just how good he has been in front of goal. It is the sort of purple patch that any striker worth their salt would dream to be in; Coral have unsurprisingly backed Higuain as favourite to score in their next game against Sarria s former employers Empoli who have kept just one clean sheet from their last five league fixtures. Napoli will need Higuain to carry his rich vein of form throughout the rest of the season if they are to have any chance of maintaining their wonderful pace and sprint clear of the chasing pack.

Napoli have won many admirers across Europe for the quality of football they have played this season, but it remains to be seen if they have the mentality to pass the acid test and keep the momentum going between now and the end of the season. Recent history would suggest that their chances are not great; the Partenopei, then managed by Walter Mazzarri, put themselves in a wonderful position in 2012/2013, only to finish runners-up behind Juventus as the odd slip at the wrong times proved costly in their pursuit of Juventus. A number of third-placed finishes would also suggest that Napoli have lacked the mentality and guile to end their long wait for a Scudetto, but there is real excitement in Naples that the current crop of players have what it takes to stop the Old Lady from making it five titles in a row.

#1609. Real Madrid: “Something is happening, watch out!” – Thierry Henry impressed by Mourinho's emerging side

By Axel Clody | 25 Nov 2026 09:50

Real Madrid thrashed PSV Eindhoven 5-1 in the Champions League on Tuesday night and are growing in strength this season, thanks to the work of Jose Mourinho and the form of several players.

Thierry Henry's words on CBS on Tuesday night sum up the feeling that is starting to emerge around Real Madrid:

'Real Madrid played an exceptional game. Playing like that, they are serious contenders for the Champions League. They are improving enormously from week to week. Something is going on at Real Madrid, watch out!'

After a start to the season marked by some turbulence, Real Madrid appear to have found their cruising speed. The spectacular win over PSV Eindhoven (5-1) in the Champions League confirmed that impression. Mourinho's side have just strung together a tenth consecutive victory in all competitions and have a perfect record in the Champions League, with five wins from five games. Above all, Real Madrid seem to have taken a step forward in their ability to turn games around.

The script against the Dutch side was far from straightforward. Trailing at half-time after a particularly worrying first half, Real Madrid looked a completely different team after the break. It was a reaction that bore the signature of their manager, who made three changes at half-time.

The other big positive of the evening was Jude Bellingham. Left on the bench at kick-off, the Englishman made a sensational entrance at half-time, to the point of transforming his side. His work rate, ability to get forward and influence between the lines immediately gave Real Madrid more options. His superb goal, scored after a remarkable piece of skill, rewarded a top-class performance.

Thierry Henry, again, was full of admiration:

'(Jude) Bellingham is incredible, the way he plays. Wearing the number 5 at Real Madrid is not easy, but he does it with astonishing ease. His personality is extraordinary. I cannot believe that some people doubted him in his own country. But he has silenced the sceptics with his current performances and proved to them that they were wrong at the World Cup. He always delivers with his attitude and his play.'

Beyond his statistics, with seven goals and five assists in 18 appearances, Bellingham brings an extra dimension to Real Madrid's midfield. Mourinho therefore has a player capable of turning a game, but also of giving a real identity to the side's attacking play.

The Englishman's performance should not, however, overshadow Mourinho's decisions. At half-time, the Portuguese made a bold call with three changes: Bellingham, Ibrahima Konate and Dean Huijsen replaced Aurelien Tchouameni, Antonio Rudiger and Eder Militao. It was a spectacular reshuffle, particularly at centre-back, where the two starters were punished after a difficult first half.

But there was also a desire to rebalance the side behind this choice. By installing Arda Guler and Bernardo Silva in midfield, Mourinho prioritised technical control and ball circulation. Real Madrid were able to push their block up, press higher and regain control of the game. The manager also explained that he used several video clips during the break to correct his players' defensive and attacking mistakes.

'Mourinho is building a fantastic team. Week after week, we see them improving. They lost to Atletico Madrid and we thought the season was over, but they managed to pull themselves together by beating Barcelona' - Carragher said.

The former Liverpool player's comments reflect an enthusiasm that now goes beyond the result of a single match. With a manager capable of changing the course of a game, a rediscovered Bellingham and a side gaining in coherence, Real Madrid are starting to look like credible contenders for the European title. At the same time, Paris Saint-Germain have lost two attacking options in Desire Doue and Khvicha Kvaratskhelia.

#1608. EPL Prepares for Most Exciting Title Race in Years

Home » Home 2 » EPL Prepares for Most Exciting Title Race in Years

Now that all of the top four English Premier League teams have had a chance to play each other, we find ourselves looking at one of the most wide open title races in recent memory. As of this writing, the league leaders are only separated by a mere six points. With the exception of Manchester City, we could very well see a new face hoisting the Premier League trophy at the end of the season.

For much of the year, it looked like Arsenal would be in the running for its first league title in more than a decade. With the Gunners’ recent victory against Leicester City, they are very much back in the conversation. Danny Welbeck returned to the pitch for the first time this season and made an immediate impact for Arsene Wenger’s squad, scoring the last-minute, game-winning goal to propel the team to within two points of the top spot. Given that even more key players are set to return to action for Arsenal in the coming months, this is easily the best shot they have had of winning a championship since their undefeated 2003-04 season.

Another surprise team that certainly deserves its own mention is Tottenham Hotspur. Following the club’s controversial defeat of Manchester City, the Spurs sit in second place, a mere two points behind Leicester City and ahead of Arsenal on goal differential. Tottenham have yet to win a title in the Premier League era and they have not won an English championship since 1961. The team has done a superb job of backing up star striker Harry Kane with a glut of promising young players, and their goal tally only helps to reinforce the wisdom behind the strategy of manager Mauricio Pochettino.

Meanwhile, Manchester City is still hoping to snag its third title as something of a swan song for exiting manager Manuel Pellegrini. It was recently announced that the club had hired Pep Guardiola . from Bayern Munich to take charge of the team beginning with next season. Thus, Pellegrini has been forced to endure the rest of the campaign as a dead man walking. Despite the impending exit of Pellegrini, City are still in the race for the Premier League title in addition to both the F.A. Cup and Champions League. Theoretically, the club could pull off a treble, if it can manage a solid string of performances during the final half of the season.

At the beginning of the season, it was expected that the usual suspects would once again dominate the league. Many predicted the reigning champs at Chelsea to repeat their success. However, a shocking season has seen the team part ways with controversial manager Jose Mourinho and struggle to remain in the top half of the tables with hopes of a Champions League spot dashed long ago.

For the first time in years, there’s a chance to see a completely new team win the league. No matter which club you support, there’s no denying that this has made for one of the most thrilling contests in recent memory. In a league where money talks, small fish like Leicester City are surprising everyone, and we can only hope that this means a new era of parity for the Premier League.

While the visitors sit at the top of the Championship table, the Saints are just seven points adrift of opponents who are now viewed as one of their fierce rivals.

More than six months on from Tonda Eckert being found guilty of launching a spying mission on a Middlesbrough training session ahead of their playoff semi-final, Southampton have moved on from the controversy that rocked English football.

While Eckert will accept the attention that Friday's game attracts, he will remain focused on trying to secure promotion to the Premier League.

Despite being docked four points as part of their punishment from the Football Association, Southampton can move to within four points of Boro with victory on the South coast.

That said, the Saints have struggled for consistency of late, only collecting five points from four games and conceding a late equaliser to draw 1-1 at Sheffield United on Tuesday night.

Nevertheless, Southampton have been sensational at their home ground. Not only have 22 points being accumulated from a possible 24, they have scored 22 goals and conceded just five.

As for Middlesbrough, they make the long trip south having collected 12 points from eight fixtures, albeit only prevailing on three occasions.

As for Boro, Sebastian Berhalter is expected to return in central midfield, with Myles Peart-Harris potentially being used further forward.

Providing that Lankshear shows no ill-effects from Tuesday's game, he should start, with David Strelec likely dropping down to the bench to accommodate an extra midfielder.
